claims.statement: Rübezahl (Polish Liczyrzepa, Duch Gór; Czech Krakonoš) is a folkloric mountain spirit of the Giant Mountains (Krkonoše, Karkonosze) on the Czech–Polish border, subject of many German, Polish and Czech legends.
claims.statement_id: Rübezahl (Polandia: Liczyrzepa, Duch Gór; Ceko: Krakonoš) adalah roh gunung dalam cerita rakyat dari Pegunungan Raksasa (Krkonoše, Karkonosze) di perbatasan Republik Ceko dan Polandia, tokoh banyak legenda Jerman, Polandia, dan Ceko.
claims.quote: is a folkloric mountain spirit (woodwose) of the Giant Mountains (Czech: Krkonoše , Polish: Karkonosze , hence his name in Czech and Polish), a mountain range along the border between the Czech Republic and Poland. He is the subject of many legends and fairy tales in German, Polish, and Czech folklore.

claims.statement: One reading of the name comes from Johann Karl August Musäus's story: Rübezahl abducted a turnip-loving princess (Rüben), who asked him to count (zählen) the turnips in the field and escaped while he counted.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu tafsiran nama berasal dari kisah Johann Karl August Musäus: Rübezahl menculik putri penyuka lobak (Rüben), sang putri memintanya menghitung (zählen) lobak di ladang, dan kabur selagi ia menghitung.
claims.quote: One interpretation is from the story How Rübezahl Got his Name by Johann Karl August Musäus, which recounts how Rübezahl abducted a princess who liked turnips (German: Rüben , singular Rübe). ... The princess asks him to count (zählen) the turnips in the field. While he counted, she escaped.

claims.statement: The Polish name Liczyrzepa is a direct translation of the German name, introduced by Stanisław Bełza in 1898.
claims.statement_id: Nama Polandia Liczyrzepa adalah terjemahan langsung nama Jerman, diperkenalkan Stanisław Bełza pada 1898.
claims.quote: The Polish name Liczyrzepa is a direct translation of the German name, introduced by Stanisław Bełza in 1898.

claims.statement: In Czech tales Krakonoš gave people sourdough and invented kyselo soup; when fog rises from the bottom of the Kotel, people say Krakonoš is cooking kyselo.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Ceko, Krakonoš memberi orang ragi asam dan menciptakan sup kyselo; bila kabut naik dari dasar lembah Kotel, orang berkata Krakonoš sedang memasak kyselo.
claims.quote: In Czech fairytales, Rübezahl (Czech: Krakonoš ) gave sourdough to people and invented the traditional regional soup kyselo. In the Giant Mountains is a mountain named Kotel, which means cauldron. When fog rises from the valley at the bottom of the Kotel, people say that Krakonoš is cooking kyselo.

claims.statement: Rübezahl is a mocking name that provokes his anger; respectful names include 'Lord of the Mountains' (Herr vom Berge, Herr der Berge).
claims.statement_id: Rübezahl adalah nama ejekan yang membangkitkan amarahnya; sebutan hormatnya antara lain "Penguasa Gunung" (Herr vom Berge, Herr der Berge).
claims.quote: Rübezahl is a name of ridicule, the use of which provokes his anger. In fact calling him by this nickname was the one crime he would not tolerate. Respectful names are "Lord of the Mountain(s)" (Herr vom Berge, Herr der Berge)

claims.statement: In legend Rübezahl appears as a capricious giant, gnome or mountain spirit; friendly to good people, teaching medicine and giving presents, but taking severe revenge on those who deride him, and sometimes a trickster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Rübezahl tampil sebagai raksasa, gnom, atau roh gunung yang berubah-ubah; ramah kepada orang baik, mengajari pengobatan dan memberi hadiah, tetapi membalas keras orang yang mengejeknya, dan kadang berperan sebagai penipu.
claims.quote: In legends, Rübezahl appears as a capricious giant, gnome, or mountain spirit. With good people he is friendly, teaching them medicine and giving them presents. If someone derides him, however, he exacts a severe revenge. He sometimes plays the role of a trickster in folk tales.

claims.statement: Rübezahl is the lord of weather of the mountains, similar to the Wild Hunt, sending lightning, thunder, fog, rain and snow even while the sun shines.
claims.statement_id: Rübezahl adalah penguasa cuaca pegunungan, mirip Perburuan Liar, yang tiba-tiba mengirim petir, guntur, kabut, hujan, dan salju walau matahari bersinar.
claims.quote: Rübezahl is the fantastic lord of weather of the mountains and is similar to the Wild Hunt. Unexpectedly or playfully, he sends lightning and thunder, fog, rain and snow from the mountain above, even while the sun is shining.

claims.statement: Rübezahl was first depicted in 1561 on a map by the geographer Martin Helwig, is no older than the 15th century, and his legend probably arose among immigrant miners.
claims.statement_id: Rübezahl pertama kali digambarkan pada 1561 di peta ahli geografi Martin Helwig, tidak lebih tua dari abad ke-15, dan legendanya mungkin lahir di kalangan penambang pendatang.
claims.quote: Représenté pour la première fois en 1561 sur une carte du géographe Martin Helwig, il n'est pas antérieur au XVe siècle. Sa légende naquit probablement parmi les mineurs immigrants dans la région.

claims.statement: He appears especially as a monk in an ash-grey habit, but also as a miner, squire or craftsman, in animal form, or as an object (tree stump, stone, cloud).
claims.statement_id: Ia menampakkan diri terutama sebagai biarawan berjubah kelabu abu, tetapi juga sebagai penambang, bangsawan muda, tukang, dalam wujud hewan, atau sebagai benda (tunggul pohon, batu, awan).
claims.quote: Insbesondere zeigt er sich als Mönch in aschgrauer Kutte (vergleichbar Wodan im Wolkenmantel), aber auch als Bergmann, Junker, Handwerker und in ähnlicher Gestalt und Verkleidung, aber auch in Tiergestalt oder als Gegenstand (Baumstumpf, Stein, Wolke).

claims.statement: He sometimes leads walkers astray and is said to own a garden of wondrous herbs that he defends against intruders.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia menyesatkan pengembara, dan konon ia memiliki kebun tanaman ajaib yang dibelanya dari penyusup.
claims.quote: Bisweilen werden Wanderer von ihm in die Irre geleitet. Er soll einen Garten mit Wunderkräutern besitzen, den er gegen Eindringlinge verteidigt.

claims.statement: By legend this capricious giant lives in the heart of the Giant Mountains in Silesia and can take various forms, including a monk, a miner, a wild hunter or a tree stump.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, raksasa yang berubah-ubah ini tinggal di jantung Pegunungan Raksasa di Silesia dan bisa mengambil berbagai rupa, seperti biarawan, penambang, pemburu liar, atau tunggul pohon.
claims.quote: La légende veut que ce géant capricieux vive au cœur des monts des Géants, en Silésie, et puisse prendre des apparences différentes, dont celle d'un moine, d'un mineur, d'un chasseur sauvage ou d'une souche d'arbre.

claims.statement: Rübezahl is seen as guardian of the Giant Mountains; from a bad demon causing storms and heavy snow he evolved into a guardian of the poor in his mountains.
claims.statement_id: Rübezahl dipandang sebagai penjaga Pegunungan Raksasa; dari setan jahat pembawa badai dan salju lebat, ia berkembang menjadi pelindung orang miskin di pegunungannya.
claims.quote: Rübezahl is seen to be the guardian of the Giant Mountains. ... Historically, his character has kept on expanding; from a bad demon causing storms and heavy snow, he evolved into a guardian of the poor people living in his mountains.

claims.statement: The Rübezahl story was first collected by Johannes Praetorius in Daemonologia Rubinzalii Silesii (1662) and later appeared in Musäus's Legenden von Rübezahl (1783).
claims.statement_id: Kisah Rübezahl pertama dikumpulkan dan dituliskan Johannes Praetorius dalam Daemonologia Rubinzalii Silesii (1662), lalu muncul dalam Legenden von Rübezahl karya Musäus (1783).
claims.quote: The Rübezahl story was first collected and written down by Johannes Praetorius in the Daemonologia Rubinzalii Silesii (1662). The character later appeared in Johann Karl August Musäus's "Legenden von Rübezahl " (1783)

claims.statement: Another proposed etymology is Riebezagel, combining the personal name Riebe with Middle High German zagel, 'tail', from his depiction as a tailed demon.
claims.statement_id: Etimologi lain yang diajukan adalah Riebezagel, gabungan nama diri Riebe dan kata Jerman Hulu Pertengahan zagel, "ekor", dari penggambarannya sebagai setan berekor.
claims.quote: Another proposed etymology is Riebezagel, from a combination of the personal name Riebe and the Middle High German zagel, meaning "tail", from his pictorial representation as a tailed demon.

claims.statement: Vellamo (also Wellamo) is the goddess of water, lakes and seas in Finnish mythology, called Veen emäntä, 'Mistress of Water'.
claims.statement_id: Vellamo (juga Wellamo) adalah dewi air, danau, dan laut dalam mitologi Finlandia, dijuluki Veen emäntä, "Nyonya Air".
claims.quote: is the goddess of water, lakes and seas in Finnish mythology. She is called Veen emäntä 'Mistress of Water'.

claims.statement: Vellamo's husband is the Finnish sea god Ahti; in Finnish fishing spells Vellamo and Ahti are asked to bring their cattle (fish) into the nets.
claims.statement_id: Suami Vellamo adalah dewa laut Finlandia Ahti; dalam mantra memancing Finlandia, Vellamo dan Ahti diminta membawa ternak mereka (ikan) ke jaring.
claims.quote: Vellamo's husband is the Finnish sea god Ahti. In Finnish fishing spells, Vellamo and Ahti are asked to bring their cattle (fish) into fishing nets.

claims.statement: The Mistress of Water had cows and often helped poor people by sending them cattle; while her cows ate on the beach she sat a little way off on a rock combing her hair.
claims.statement_id: Nyonya Air memiliki sapi dan sering menolong orang miskin dengan mengirimi mereka ternak; saat sapinya makan di pantai, ia duduk agak jauh di atas batu sambil menyisir rambut.
claims.quote: The Mistress of Water also had cows. She often helped poor people by sending them cattle. ... When the Mistress's cows were on the beach eating, she herself is sitting a bit further away on a rock, combing her hair.

claims.statement: She was especially respected by fishermen; seeing her even far away while seining guaranteed plenty of fish.
claims.statement_id: Ia sangat dihormati nelayan; siapa yang melihatnya, walau dari jauh, saat menjaring dijamin mendapat banyak ikan.
claims.quote: She was especially respected by fishermen; if you saw her, even far away, while seining, you were guaranteed to get plenty of fish.

claims.statement: The name Vellamo is thought to come from Finnish velloa, 'to churn', describing the movement of water and waves; Kaarle Krohn and Uno Harva considered it a later-formed name.
claims.statement_id: Nama Vellamo diduga berasal dari kata Finlandia velloa, "mengaduk", yang menggambarkan gerak air dan ombak; Kaarle Krohn dan Uno Harva menganggapnya nama bentukan belakangan.
claims.quote: The name "Vellamo" has been theorized to come from the Finnish word velloa , which means 'to churn', describing the movement of water and waves. Kaarle Krohn and Uno Harva considered the name Vellamo to be a later-formed name

claims.statement: Vellamo is much respected by fishermen, who pray to her for miraculous catches; she can also control the winds to help sailors and controls storms and waves.
claims.statement_id: Vellamo sangat dihormati nelayan yang berdoa kepadanya demi tangkapan besar; ia juga dapat mengendalikan angin untuk membantu pelaut serta mengendalikan badai dan ombak.
claims.quote: Vellamo est très respectée des pêcheurs, qui prient pour elle dans l'espoir de pêches miraculeuses. Vellamo peut également contrôler les vents pour aider les marins, elle contrôle les tempêtes et les vagues.

claims.statement: Vellamo is described as tall and beautiful, wearing a blue dress of sea moss, and is sometimes shown with a fish tail like a mermaid.
claims.statement_id: Vellamo digambarkan tinggi dan cantik, mengenakan gaun biru dari lumut laut, dan kadang ditampilkan berekor ikan seperti putri duyung.
claims.quote: Vellamo est décrite grande et belle, et porte une robe bleue faite de mousse de mer. Elle est parfois représentée avec une queue de poisson, comme une sirène

claims.statement: Vellamo lives with her husband Ahti in the undersea palace of Ahtola; she owns magic cows living on undersea fields and sometimes, in morning mist, leads them to the surface to eat sea foam.
claims.statement_id: Vellamo tinggal bersama suaminya Ahti di istana bawah laut Ahtola; ia pemilik sapi ajaib yang hidup di padang bawah laut dan kadang, saat kabut pagi, menggiring sapinya ke permukaan untuk makan buih laut.
claims.quote: Vellamo vit avec son époux Ahti dans le palais sous-marin de Ahtola. Elle est la maîtresse de vaches magiques qui vivent sur des champs sous-marins. Parfois, lors des périodes de brumes matinales, elle mène ses vaches au-dessus de la surface pour manger l'écume des mers

claims.statement: Vellamo is pictured as a mermaid on the coat of arms of Päijät-Häme.
claims.statement_id: Vellamo digambarkan sebagai putri duyung pada lambang Päijät-Häme.
claims.quote: Vellamo pictured as a mermaid in the coat of arms of Päijät-Häme.

claims.statement: A South Karelian runic song calls the Nixie (Näkki) the offspring of Vellamo and Ahti.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah lagu runik Karelia Selatan menyebut Nixie (Näkki) keturunan Vellamo dan Ahti.
claims.quote: A South Karelian runic song calls the Nixie (Näkki ) the offspring of Vellamo and Ahti.

claims.statement: Seeing the water goddess as a 'Water Mother' matches many other Finno-Ugric peoples' views, such as the Mordvin Ved-ava.
claims.statement_id: Pandangan dewi air sebagai "Ibu Air" sejalan dengan pandangan banyak bangsa Finno-Ugria lain, seperti Ved-ava bangsa Mordvin.
claims.quote: Seeing the water goddess as a "Water Mother" lines with many other Finno-Ugric people's views, such as the Mordvin Ved-ava.

claims.statement: A Karelian runic song tells of a hero such as Väinämöinen catching a fish he tries to cut and eat; it leaps away, revealing herself as the 'watery maiden of Vellamo' and 'Ahti's only child'.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah lagu runik Karelia mengisahkan pahlawan seperti Väinämöinen menangkap ikan yang hendak dipotong dan dimakannya; ikan itu melompat pergi dan mengaku "gadis air Vellamo" serta "anak tunggal Ahti".
claims.quote: A Karelian runic song describes a hero, such as Väinämöinen, catching a fish he tries to cut and eat. The fish jumps away, revealing herself to be a "watery maiden of Vellamo" and "Ahti's only child"

claims.statement: The Alp of German folklore is sometimes likened to a vampire but behaves more like an incubus; Alp is the German form of the word that became English elf, and it is also called trud, mar, mart, mahr, schrat and walrider.
claims.statement_id: Alp, makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, kadang disamakan dengan vampir tetapi perilakunya lebih mirip inkubus; kata Alp adalah bentuk Jerman dari kata yang menjadi elf dalam bahasa Inggris, dan ia juga disebut trud, mar, mart, mahr, schrat, dan walrider.
claims.quote: Alp is sometimes likened to a vampire, but its behavior is more akin to that of the incubus. ... The word Alp is the German form of the word that comes into English as elf, both descended from Common Germanic. It is also known by the following names: trud, mar, mart, mahr, schrat, and walrider.

claims.statement: The Alp is typically male, the mara and mart appearing more feminine versions; its victims are often women whom it attacks at night by controlling their dreams, hence the German Alptraum ('elf-dream'), a nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Alp biasanya jantan, sedangkan mara dan mart tampaknya versi lebih feminin; korbannya sering perempuan yang diserangnya pada malam hari dengan mengendalikan mimpi mereka, dari situ kata Jerman Alptraum ("mimpi elf"), yaitu mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: An Alp is typically male, while the mara and mart appear to be more feminine versions of the same creature. Its victims are often females, whom it attacks during the night, controlling their dreams and creating horrible nightmares (hence the German word Alptraum ["elf-dream"], meaning a nightmare).

claims.statement: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and grows heavier until the terrified, breathless dreamer wakes, unable to move under its weight.
claims.statement_id: Alpdruck terjadi saat Alp duduk mengangkangi dada orang tidur dan makin berat hingga korban terbangun ketakutan dan sesak napas, tak bisa bergerak di bawah bebannya.
claims.quote: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and becomes heavier until the crushing weight awakens the terrified and breathless dreamer. The victim awakes unable to move under the Alp's weight.

claims.statement: Alpe also show elf-like mischief, such as souring milk, tangling hair into 'elfknots' and riding horses to exhaustion at night.
claims.statement_id: Alpe juga suka berbuat iseng seperti elf, misalnya mengasamkan susu, mengusutkan rambut menjadi "simpul elf", dan menunggangi kuda sampai kelelahan pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Alpe also exhibit a tendency for mischief similar to elves, like souring milk and re-diapering a baby ... They also enjoy tangling hair into "elfknots" or chewing and twisting horse's tails. They will ride a horse to exhaustion during the night

claims.statement: The Alp is best known for shapeshifting, like werewolf-lore creatures; it can become a cat, pig, dog, snake or small white butterfly, and is said to fly like a bird.
claims.statement_id: Alp paling dikenal karena kemampuan berganti rupa, mirip makhluk dalam kisah manusia serigala; ia dapat berubah menjadi kucing, babi, anjing, ular, atau kupu-kupu putih kecil, dan konon bisa terbang seperti burung.
claims.quote: The Alp is best known for its shapeshifting abilities, similar to the creatures from werewolf lore. It may change into a cat, pig, dog, snake or a small white butterfly. It has also been said that it can fly like a bird and ride a horse.

claims.statement: Its hat is called the Tarnkappe ('cap of concealment'), giving the Alp magic powers and invisibility while worn; an Alp that loses it will offer a great reward for its return.
claims.statement_id: Topi Alp disebut Tarnkappe ("topi penyamaran"), yang memberinya kekuatan gaib dan kemampuan tak terlihat selama dipakai; Alp yang kehilangan topi ini akan menawarkan imbalan besar untuk pengembaliannya.
claims.quote: The hat is known as a Tarnkappe (the literal translation being "camouflage cap" or "cap of concealment") which is simply a hat (or less commonly a veil) that gives the Alp magic powers and the ability to turn invisible while worn ... An Alp who has lost this hat will offer a great reward for its safe return.

claims.statement: Protections include a broomstick under the pillow, iron horseshoes on the bedpost, shoes pointing to the door, a mirror on the chest, steel and crosses; plugging holes, especially keyholes, before a visit keeps the Alp out.
claims.statement_id: Penangkal Alp antara lain sapu di bawah bantal, ladam besi di tiang ranjang, sepatu menghadap pintu, cermin di dada, baja, dan salib; menyumbat lubang, terutama lubang kunci, sebelum ia datang akan mencegahnya masuk.
claims.quote: Protections against an Alp include laying a broomstick under a pillow, iron horseshoes hung from the bedpost, placing shoes against the bed with the toes pointing toward the door, or placing a mirror on the chest. Steel and crosses are also used. ... Plugging up any holes, specifically keyholes, before a visitation will keep the Alp out.

claims.statement: Nachtalb is a late name for a fantasy and legendary being originally called Mahr that weighs on people at night and fills them with dread.
claims.statement_id: Nachtalb adalah sebutan belakangan untuk makhluk khayalan dan legenda yang semula bernama Mahr, yang menindih manusia pada malam hari dan membuat mereka ngeri.
claims.quote: Nachtalb ist eine späte Bezeichnung für ein Fantasie- und Sagenwesen, das ursprünglich „Mahr“ hieß und in der Nacht auf Menschen lastet (vgl. Albtraum) und ihnen Grauen einflößt.

claims.statement: A child may become an Alp if the mother bites a horse collar during an extremely long childbirth, or if born with a caul or hair on the palms; stillborn infants are suspected of returning from the grave as Alpe.
claims.statement_id: Anak bisa menjadi Alp bila ibunya menggigit kekang kuda untuk meredakan sakit persalinan yang sangat lama, atau bila lahir berselaput atau berambut di telapak tangan; bayi lahir mati juga diduga kembali dari kubur sebagai Alp.
claims.quote: Children may become an Alp if a woman bites a horse collar to ease the pain during an extremely long and tortuous childbirth. Also, a child born with a caul} or hair on the palms may become an Alp. ... Stillborn infants are also suspected to return from the grave as Alpe and torment their family.

claims.statement: It is usually a small black being that attacks sleeping people and domestic animals, rarely objects, and enters through keyholes or knot-holes.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini biasanya kecil dan hitam, menyerang manusia dan hewan peliharaan yang tidur, jarang juga benda, dan masuk lewat lubang kunci atau lubang dahan.
claims.quote: Es handelt sich gewöhnlich um ein kleines, schwarzes Wesen, das schlafende Menschen und Haustiere anfällt, selten auch Gegenstände. Es dringt durch Schlüssel- oder Astlöcher ein.

claims.statement: In Germanic folk belief an Alb is a low-ranking subterranean nature spirit; Alben are elf-like beings close to kobolds and dwarves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Jermanik, Alb adalah roh alam bawah tanah berderajat rendah; Alben adalah makhluk sejenis elf yang dekat dengan kobold dan kurcaci.
claims.quote: Dem germanischen Volksglauben nach steht ein „Alb“ für einen unterirdischen Naturgeist mit niederem Rang. Alben sind elbische Wesen, die den Kobolden und Zwergen nahe stehen

claims.statement: The Alp is in many cases considered a demon, but in some instances it arises from the spirits of recently dead relatives, closer to a spirit or ghost.
claims.statement_id: Alp dalam banyak kasus dianggap setan, tetapi ada pula yang tercipta dari roh kerabat yang baru meninggal, lebih mirip roh atau hantu.
claims.quote: The Alp, in many cases, is considered a demon, but there have been some instances in which the Alp is created from the spirits of recently dead relatives, more akin to a spirit or ghost.

claims.statement: Gandalf (Old Norse Gandálfr) is a dvergr (Norse dwarf) in Norse mythology appearing in the 'Tally of the Dwarves' in the Völuspá of the Poetic Edda and in the Prose Edda.
claims.statement_id: Gandalf (Nordik Kuno: Gandálfr) adalah dvergr (kurcaci Nordik) dalam mitologi Nordik yang muncul dalam "Daftar Para Kurcaci" di puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi serta dalam Edda Prosa.
claims.quote: is a Dvergr (Norse dwarf) in Norse mythology, appearing in the so-called 'Tally of the Dwarves' within the poem Völuspá from the Poetic Edda, as well as in the Prose Edda.

claims.statement: The name derives from Old Norse gandr (magical entity, e.g. wands or monsters) and álfr (elf), thus a protective spirit wielding a magic wand.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini berasal dari kata Nordik Kuno gandr (entitas gaib, misalnya tongkat sihir atau monster) dan álfr (elf), sehingga berarti roh pelindung yang memegang tongkat sihir.
claims.quote: The name derives from the Old Norse words gandr (magical entity e.g. wands, monsters etc.) and álfr (elf), thus a protective spirit who wields a magical wand.

claims.statement: The name was also used for a Norse king in the Heimskringla.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini juga dipakai untuk seorang raja Nordik dalam Heimskringla.
claims.quote: The name was also used for a Norse king in the Heimskringla.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Gandalf is a dwarf (enano) appearing in the poem Völuspá of the Poetic Edda.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Gandalf adalah kurcaci (enano) yang muncul dalam puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi.
claims.quote: En la mitología nórdica, Gandalf es un enano que aparece en el poema Völuspá de la Edda poética.

claims.statement: The name derives from Old Norse gandr (staff) and álfr (elf), a protective spirit wielding a staff, perhaps a magic wand.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini berasal dari kata Nordik Kuno gandr (tongkat) dan álfr (elf), yakni roh pelindung yang memegang tongkat, mungkin tongkat sihir.
claims.quote: El nombre deriva de las palabras en nórdico antiguo gandr (vara) y álfr (elfo), es decir, un espíritu protector que esgrime una vara, tal vez una varita mágica.

claims.statement: In his fiction J. R. R. Tolkien eventually named his wizard Gandalf after the dwarf, but first used the name for the leader of the dwarf party (finally called Thorin Oakenshield).
claims.statement_id: Dalam karya fiksinya, J. R. R. Tolkien akhirnya menamai penyihirnya Gandalf menurut kurcaci ini, tetapi semula memakai nama itu untuk pemimpin rombongan kurcaci (yang akhirnya bernama Thorin Oakenshield).
claims.quote: In his fictional writings, J. R. R. Tolkien eventually named his wizard Gandalf after the Dvergr, but initially used the name for the head of the dwarf party (ultimately to be called Thorin Oakenshield).

claims.statement: A half-elf is a mythological or fictional being born of an immortal elf and a mortal human, often depicted as very beautiful and magically gifted, sometimes torn between the two worlds they inhabit.
claims.statement_id: Setengah-elf adalah makhluk mitologis atau fiktif yang lahir dari elf abadi dan manusia fana, sering digambarkan sangat rupawan dan berkekuatan gaib, kadang terbelah di antara dua dunia yang dihuninya.
claims.quote: A half-elf is a mythological or fictional being, born of an immortal elf and a mortal human. They are often depicted as very beautiful and endowed with magical powers; they may be presented as torn between the two worlds that they inhabit.

claims.statement: Half-elves became known in modern times mainly through J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth writings but originate in Norse mythology; one appeared in Lord Dunsany's 1924 book The King of Elfland's Daughter.
claims.statement_id: Setengah-elf dikenal di masa modern terutama lewat tulisan Dunia Tengah J. R. R. Tolkien tetapi berasal dari mitologi Nordik; seorang setengah-elf muncul dalam buku Lord Dunsany tahun 1924, The King of Elfland's Daughter.
claims.quote: Half-elves became known in modern times mainly through J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth writings but have origins in Norse mythology. A half-elf appeared in Lord Dunsany's 1924 book The King of Elfland's Daughter.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology a half-elf is the offspring of an elf and a human; major examples are Skuld and Högni. Högni was a Thidreks saga hero born to a human queen visited by an elf while the king was away, and Skuld a Danish princess in Hrólf Kraki's saga.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, setengah-elf adalah keturunan elf dan manusia; contoh utamanya Skuld dan Högni. Högni adalah pahlawan Thidreks saga yang lahir dari ratu manusia setelah elf mendatanginya saat raja pergi, dan Skuld adalah putri Denmark dalam saga Hrólf Kraki.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, a half-elf is the offspring of an elf and a human. Major examples include Skuld and Högni. Högni was a hero in Thidreks saga, born to a human queen when an elf visited her while the king was away. Skuld was a Danish princess, as told in Hrólf Kraki's saga.

claims.statement: King Helgi, sleeping alone, let in a ragged person on a midwinter night; she said he had freed her from a curse, and three years later the elf-woman returned and left a daughter at his door named Skuld, meaning 'what you should do'.
claims.statement_id: Raja Helgi, yang tidur sendirian, membukakan pintu bagi sosok berpakaian compang-camping pada malam pertengahan musim dingin; perempuan itu berkata ia telah dibebaskan dari kutukan, dan tiga tahun kemudian perempuan elf itu kembali dan meninggalkan seorang putri di pintu raja bernama Skuld, yang berarti "apa yang harus kaulakukan".
claims.quote: King Helgi, sleeping alone as he had not been invited to King Adils's wedding, let in a ragged person on a midwinter night. ... She told him he had freed her from a curse and asked to leave. ... three years later the woman, an elf, returned and left a daughter at his door. She told him that the child's name was Skuld, which means "what you should do".

claims.statement: She said the King would be rewarded for breaking the curse, but his people would suffer because he had not done as she asked; she never returned, and Skuld was always angry.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkata raja akan mendapat imbalan karena mematahkan kutukan, tetapi rakyatnya akan menderita karena raja tidak menuruti permintaannya; ia tak pernah kembali, dan Skuld selalu marah.
claims.quote: She said that the King would gain the reward for breaking the curse, but that the King's people would suffer as the King had not done as she had asked. She never came back, but Skuld was always angry.

claims.statement: The scholar Hilda Ellis describes Skuld as evil: in the saga she used magic to raise an army against her half-brother Hrólf, and her men sprang up again as fast as they were killed, fighting harder.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Hilda Ellis menggambarkan Skuld sebagai jahat: dalam saga ia memakai sihir untuk membangkitkan pasukan melawan Hrólf, saudara tirinya, dan prajuritnya yang dibunuh segera bangkit dan bertarung lebih kuat.
claims.quote: The scholar Hilda Ellis describes Skuld as evil, recalling that in the saga, Skuld used magic to raise an army against Hrólf, her half-brother. As quickly as Hrólf's warriors kill Skuld's men, they spring up, fighting more strongly than ever.

claims.statement: Högni too is 'essentially a demonic character', his name linked to German Hexe ('witch') and English hag; the scholar Alexander Krappe sees his being an elf's son as fitting that role.
claims.statement_id: Högni juga "pada dasarnya tokoh iblis", namanya dikaitkan dengan kata Jerman Hexe ("penyihir") dan kata Inggris hag; sarjana Alexander Krappe menilai statusnya sebagai putra elf sesuai dengan peran itu.
claims.quote: Högni too is "essentially a demonic character", his name connected to the German Hexe, 'witch', and to the English "hag"; the scholar Alexander Krappe sees his being the son of an elf as fitting in to that role

claims.statement: In Middle-earth half-elves are children of Elves and Men who can choose Elvish immortality or mortal life; since Tolkien popularised them they have spread through role-playing games, video games and films, and Dungeons & Dragons has its own half-elf race.
claims.statement_id: Di Dunia Tengah, setengah-elf adalah anak Elf dan Manusia yang dapat memilih keabadian Elf atau hidup fana Manusia; sejak dipopulerkan Tolkien mereka dikenal luas dalam permainan peran, gim video, dan film, dan Dungeons & Dragons punya ras setengah-elf sendiri.
claims.quote: In Middle-earth, half-elves are the children of Elves and Men, and can choose either Elvish immortality or the mortal life of Men. ... Since their popularisation by Tolkien, half-elves have become widely known in role-playing games, and in turn in video games and spin-off films. The role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons features its own race of half-elves

claims.statement: In fiction, especially heroic and high fantasy, a semi-elfe or demi-elfe is the product of an elf's union with another humanoid creature, most often a human.
claims.statement_id: Dalam karya fiksi, terutama fantasi heroik dan fantasi tinggi, semi-elfe atau demi-elfe adalah hasil persatuan elf dengan makhluk humanoid lain, paling sering manusia.
claims.quote: un semi-elfe ou demi-elfe est le fruit de l'union d'un elfe et d'une autre créature humanoïde, le plus souvent humaine.

claims.statement: Landvættir ('land spirits') are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry; tied to specific places, their wellbeing is needed for the land to be fruitful, and Old Norse sources show them as potentially harmful and able to drive away unwanted people.
claims.statement_id: Landvættir ("roh tanah") adalah roh tanah dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat sesudahnya, dan Heathenry modern; mereka terikat pada tempat tertentu, kesejahteraannya syarat kesuburan tanah, dan dalam sumber Nordik Kuno mereka bisa berbahaya serta mampu mengusir orang yang tak diinginkan.
claims.quote: Landvættir ("land spirits" or "land wights") are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry. They are closely associated with specific locations and their wellbeing is presented as being required for the land they inhabit to be fruitful. In Old Norse sources, they are depicted as being potentially harmful and capable of driving away unwanted individuals

claims.statement: The preamble of the heathen laws said men should not sail with carved figureheads, and if they did, should remove them before land came in sight.
claims.statement_id: Pembukaan hukum kafir menyatakan orang tidak boleh berlayar dengan kepala berukir di kapalnya, dan bila ada, harus melepasnya sebelum daratan terlihat.
claims.quote: Translation: It was the beginning of the preamble of the heathen laws that men should not take ships to sea with carved figure heads upon their sterns, but if they did, they should take them off before they came in sight of land

claims.statement: The book later states no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.
claims.statement_id: Landnámabók kemudian menyatakan tak seorang pun berani tinggal di tempat Hjörleif menetap karena landvættir.
claims.quote: Later, the book states that no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.

claims.statement: In this account, women take food to stone piles or flat stones hoping the landvættir will make them prosperous.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan itu, para perempuan membawa makanan ke tumpukan batu atau batu datar dengan harapan landvættir membuat mereka makmur.
claims.quote: In this account, the women take food to stone piles or flat stones, hoping that in return the landvættir would make them prosperous.

claims.statement: Norway's Gulating laws of the later 13th century outlawed the belief that howes, woods and waterfalls were inhabited by landvættir, deeming it heresy and heathen.
claims.statement_id: Hukum Gulating Norwegia dari paruh kedua abad ke-13 melarang kepercayaan bahwa gundukan kubur, hutan, dan air terjun dihuni landvættir, karena dianggap bidah dan bagian agama kafir.
claims.quote: The Norwegian Gulating laws, written in the latter half of the 13th century, made illegal the belief that howes, wooded areas and waterfalls, were inhabited by landvættir, considering it a heresy and belonging to the heathen religion.

claims.statement: King Harald sent a warlock to Iceland in altered shape; he went as a whale and saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian spirits, great and small.
claims.statement_id: Raja Harald menyuruh seorang penyihir pergi ke Islandia dalam wujud lain; ia berangkat sebagai paus dan melihat semua gunung dan bukit penuh roh penjaga, besar dan kecil.
claims.quote: King Harald told a warlock to hie to Iceland in some altered shape, and to try what he could learn there to tell him: and he set out in the shape of a whale. ... where he saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian-spirits, some great, some small.

claims.statement: He was driven off in the east by a great dragon with poison-blowing snakes, toads and lizards, in the north by a great bird, in the west by a great bull with other landvættir, and in the south by a huge bergrisi with an iron staff.
claims.statement_id: Ia diusir di sisi timur oleh naga besar yang diikuti ular, kodok, dan kadal penyembur racun, di utara oleh burung besar, di barat oleh banteng besar beserta landvættir lain, dan di selatan oleh bergrisi raksasa bertongkat besi.
claims.quote: First on the East side by a large dragon followed by snakes, toads and lizards who blew atter, or poison, at him, then on the North side by a great bird with many smaller birds, next in the West a large bull followed by beasts and other landvættir, and finally a huge bergrisi with an iron staff in the South

claims.statement: The four landvættir are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters: the dragon (Dreki), eagle or griffin (Gammur), bull (Griðungur) and giant (Bergrisi); they appear on the Icelandic arms and the reverse of króna coins.
claims.statement_id: Empat landvættir kini dianggap pelindung empat wilayah Islandia: naga (Dreki), elang atau griffin (Gammur), banteng (Griðungur), dan raksasa (Bergrisi); keempatnya tampil pada lambang Islandia dan sisi belakang koin króna.
claims.quote: Les quatre Landvættir sont aujourd'hui considérés comme les protecteurs des quatre quartiers d'Islande : le dragon (Dreki) dans le Nord-Est, l'aigle ou griffon (Gammur) dans de Nord-Ouest, le taureau (Griðungur) dans le Sud-Ouest, et le géant (Bergrisi) dans le Sud-Est. Les quatre Landvættir de l'Islande sont représentés sur les Armoiries de l'Islande et sur l'envers des pièces

claims.statement: Some scholars suggest landvættir are chthonic spirits of the dead, while others interpret them as nature spirits because they sometimes live in never-populated land.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sarjana menduga landvættir adalah roh chthonic dan arwah orang mati, sedangkan yang lain menafsirkannya sebagai roh alam karena kadang menghuni tanah yang tak pernah didiami.
claims.quote: Some scholars have suggested that landvættir are chthonic and spirits of the dead, but others have interpreted them as nature spirits, since they sometimes live in land that has never been populated.

claims.statement: Scholars have linked landvættir to other land-dwelling beings such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they may have been identified at different times.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana mengaitkan landvættir dengan makhluk lain penghuni tanah seperti elf, kurcaci, dan landdísir, yang mungkin pernah disamakan dengannya pada masa berbeda.
claims.quote: Landvættir have been variously connected by scholars to other beings believed to inhabit the land such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they were potentially identified at different points in history.

claims.statement: As a compound, land-vættir has been rendered 'guardian spirits of a country', 'land-spirits', 'landwights' or 'nature spirits'.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai kata majemuk, land-vættir diterjemahkan antara lain sebagai "roh penjaga negeri", "roh tanah", atau "roh alam".
claims.quote: As a compound, land-vættir has been variously translated as "guardian spirits of a country", "land-spirits", "landwights" or "nature spirits".

claims.statement: In Danish folklore the helhest ('Hel horse') is a three-legged horse associated with Hel, death and illness, said to have been seen in various places in Denmark.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Denmark, helhest ("kuda Hel") adalah kuda berkaki tiga yang dikaitkan dengan Hel, kematian, dan penyakit, dan disebut pernah terlihat di berbagai tempat di Denmark.
claims.quote: In Danish folklore, a helhest (Danish "Hel horse") is a three-legged horse associated with Hel. Various Danish phrases are recorded that refer to the horse. The Helhest is associated with death and illness, and it is mentioned in folklore as having been spotted in various locations in Denmark.

claims.statement: According to Jacob Grimm the helhest was sometimes described as going 'around the graveyard on three legs, causing death', and from Schleswig comes the phrase that in plague time 'Hel rides about on a three-legged horse, destroying men'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Jacob Grimm, helhest kadang digambarkan berjalan "mengitari pemakaman dengan tiga kaki, membawa kematian", dan dari Schleswig tercatat ungkapan bahwa saat wabah "Hel berkeliling di atas kuda berkaki tiga, membinasakan manusia".
claims.quote: According to Jacob Grimm, the helhest was sometimes described as going "around the graveyard on three legs, causing death", and from Schleswig, a phrase is recorded that, in time of plague, "die (corrected by Grimm from der) Hel rides about on a three-legged horse, destroying men".

claims.statement: Legend says that formerly in every churchyard a living horse was buried before any human body, and this horse reappears as the 'Hel-horse'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, dahulu di setiap halaman gereja seekor kuda hidup dikubur sebelum jenazah manusia mana pun, dan kuda ini muncul kembali dengan nama "kuda Hel".
claims.quote: Legend dictates that "in every churchyard in former days, before any human body was buried in it, a living horse was interred. This horse re-appears and is known by the name of 'Hel-horse.'"

claims.statement: The 19th-century scholar Jacob Grimm theorised that before Christianisation the helhest was originally the steed of the goddess Hel.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana abad ke-19 Jacob Grimm berteori bahwa sebelum kristenisasi, helhest semula tunggangan dewi Hel.
claims.quote: 19th century scholar Jacob Grimm theorizes that, prior to Christianization, the helhest was originally the steed of the goddess Hel.

claims.statement: By folklore the Hel-horse at times appears in the Aarhus Cathedral yard; a man who looked at it from his window turned deathly pale, then fell sick and died. At Roskilde Cathedral people once spat on a narrow stone under which a helhest was said to be buried.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, kuda Hel kadang muncul di halaman Katedral Aarhus; seorang lelaki yang melihatnya dari jendela menjadi pucat pasi, lalu sakit dan meninggal. Di Katedral Roskilde, orang dahulu meludahi batu sempit tempat helhest konon dikuburkan.
claims.quote: According to folklore, the Aarhus Cathedral yard at times features the Hel-horse. ... upon looking out the window he grew deathly pale, but would not detail afterward what he had seen. Soon thereafter he grew sick and died. At the Roskilde Cathedral, people in former times would spit on a narrow stone where a Helhest was said to be buried.

claims.statement: The helhest of folklore was believed to appear at night in cemeteries and announce the death of anyone who saw it; it was a three-legged horse, sometimes also a headless one.
claims.statement_id: Helhest dalam cerita rakyat diyakini muncul pada malam hari di pemakaman dan menandakan kematian siapa pun yang melihatnya; wujudnya kuda berkaki tiga, kadang juga kuda tanpa kepala.
claims.quote: Le Helhest du folklore était censé apparaître la nuit dans les cimetières, et annoncer la mort de toute personne qui le voyait. C'est une créature surnaturelle en forme de cheval à trois jambes, mais parfois aussi de cheval sans tête.

claims.statement: Several Danish phrases about the horse were recorded in the 19th century, such as 'to walk like a Hel-horse' for someone stepping heavily and noisily; the 19th-century scholar Benjamin Thorpe linked the phrase 'he gave death a pack of oats', said of a survivor of near-fatal illness, to the helhest.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah ungkapan Denmark terkait kuda ini tercatat pada abad ke-19, seperti "berjalan seperti helhest" untuk orang yang melangkah berat dan berisik; sarjana abad ke-19 Benjamin Thorpe mengaitkan ungkapan "ia memberi kematian sekarung gandum" bagi orang yang selamat dari penyakit mematikan dengan helhest.
claims.quote: A number of Danish phrases connected to the horse were recorded in the 19th century, such as "at gå eller træde som en Helhest" ("to walk or step like a Hel-horse") for someone who takes strong or heavy steps and thus causes noise. ... Benjamin Thorpe connects the Danish phrase "he gave death a pack of oats" when an individual survives a near-fatal disease to notions of the Helhest

claims.statement: In Norse mythology according to the Gylfaginning, Annar (Old Norse Annarr, 'second, another') is the father of Jörð (Mother Earth) by Nótt (Night); the form Ónar (Ónarr, 'gaping') occurs as a variant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik menurut Gylfaginning, Annar (Nordik Kuno Annarr, "yang kedua, yang lain") adalah ayah Jörð (Ibu Bumi) dari Nótt (Malam); bentuk Ónar (Ónarr, "yang menganga") muncul sebagai varian.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, according to the Gylfaginning, Annar (Old Norse Annarr 'second, another') is the father of Jörð (Mother Earth) by Nótt (the Night). The form Ónar (Old Norse Ónarr 'gaping') is found as a variant.

claims.statement: Annar/Ónar is also the name of a dwarf in the Völuspá's catalogue of dwarfs, repeated in the Gylfaginning.
claims.statement_id: Annar/Ónar juga nama seorang kurcaci dalam daftar kurcaci Völuspá yang diulang dalam Gylfaginning.
claims.quote: Annar/Ónar is also the name of a dwarf in the catalogue of dwarfs in the Völuspá that is repeated in the Gylfaginning.

claims.statement: Nótt was given to a man named Naglfari, their son being Aud; afterwards she wed Annar, and their daughter was Jörð ('Earth').
claims.statement_id: Nótt diberikan kepada lelaki bernama Naglfari dan putra mereka Aud; kemudian ia menikah dengan Annar, dan putri mereka Jörð ("Bumi").
claims.quote: She was given to the man named Naglfari; their son was Aud. Afterward she was wedded to him that was called Annar; Jörð ['Earth'] was their daughter.

claims.statement: Snorri may have used a source in which annar ('second, another') meant Odin, for he had just written of Odin: 'The earth was his daughter and his wife'.
claims.statement_id: Snorri mungkin memakai sumber yang memaksudkan annar ("yang kedua, yang lain") sebagai Odin, karena ia sendiri baru menulis tentang Odin: "Bumi adalah putrinya dan istrinya".
claims.quote: Snorri might have been using a source in which annar 'second, another' was intended to mean Odin, for he himself had just previously written of Odin: "The earth was his daughter and his wife...".

claims.statement: In the Skáldskaparmál Snorri instead uses the form Ónar, giving 'daughter of Ónar' as a kenning for Jörð.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Skáldskaparmál Snorri justru memakai bentuk Ónar dan memberi "putri Ónar" sebagai salah satu kenning untuk Jörð.
claims.quote: But in the Skáldskaparmál Snorri uses the form Ónar instead, giving "daughter of Ónar" as one of the kennings for Jörð.

claims.statement: Since Annarr is also an epithet of Odin and Snorri Sturluson says Jǫrð was both his daughter and wife, Annarr may be Odin himself, though this is also judged unlikely.
claims.statement_id: Karena Annarr juga salah satu julukan Odin dan Snorri Sturluson menyebut Jǫrð putri sekaligus istri Odin, Annarr mungkin identik dengan Odin, tetapi hal itu juga dinilai tidak mungkin.
claims.quote: Poiché Annarr è anche uno degli epiteti di Odino, e Snorri Sturluson afferma che Jǫrð fosse insieme figlia e sposa di quest'ultimo, è possibile che Annarr vada identificato con lo stesso Odino, ma è allo stesso tempo improbabile

claims.statement: In the pseudo-historical genealogy of Odin's ancestors in the introduction to Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, one Athra is said to be 'whom we call Annar'; what this means is unknown.
claims.statement_id: Dalam silsilah semu-sejarah leluhur Odin di pengantar Edda Prosa karya Snorri Sturluson, seorang Athra disebut "yang kita sebut Annar"; maksudnya tidak diketahui.
claims.quote: In the pseudo-historical genealogy of Odin's ancestors in the introduction to Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, a certain Athra is said to be he "whom we call Annar". What this refers to is unknown.

claims.statement: In Nordic mythology Blóðughófi (sometimes Blodughofi, Old Norse 'Bloody Hoof') is Freyr's horse, notable for passing safely through fire and darkness; he is attested in several þulur of horses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Blóðughófi (kadang ditulis Blodughofi, berarti "Kuku Berdarah" dalam Nordik Kuno) adalah kuda Freyr yang dikenal mampu melintasi api dan kegelapan dengan selamat; ia tercatat dalam beberapa þulur kuda.
claims.quote: In Nordic mythology, Blóðughófi (sometimes anglicised Blodughofi and meaning "Bloody Hoof" in Old Norse) is the horse of Freyr and is notable for his ability to pass safely through fire and darkness. He is attested in several þulur of horses.

claims.statement: In Kálfsvísa Blóðughófi is named in a list of horses whose rider is the 'Slayer of Beli', a name for Freyr.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kálfsvísa, Blóðughófi disebut dalam daftar kuda dengan penunggang "Pembunuh Beli", sebutan untuk Freyr.
claims.quote: In Kálfsvísa, Blóðughófi is named in a list of horses, where their rider is specified as the "Slayer of Beli", a name for Freyr

claims.statement: In Þorgrímsþula Blóðughófi is listed among horses ridden by 'öflgan Atriða', sometimes read as a name of Freyr, though the closely related spelling Atriða is used for Odin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Þorgrímsþula, Blóðughófi disebut dalam daftar kuda yang ditunggangi "öflgan Atriða", yang kadang ditafsirkan sebagai nama Freyr, walau ejaan yang mirip, Atriða, dipakai sebagai nama Odin.
claims.quote: In Þorgrímsþula, Blóðughófi is named among a list of horses ... Here, they are described as being ridden by "öflgan Atriða ", sometimes interpreted as a name of Freyr; however, the closely related spelling Atriða is used as a named of Odin.

claims.statement: In one anonymous þula Blóðughófi appears in a list of horses under the variant Blóðhófr ('Blood-hoof').
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu þulur anonim, Blóðughófi disebut dalam daftar kuda dengan varian nama Blóðhófr ("Kuku-darah").
claims.quote: In one of the anonymous þulur, Blóðughófi is named in a list of horses, as the variant, Blóðhófr (Blood-hoof)

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Blóðughófi is the god Freyr's mount, described as able to cross fire and darkness; in Old Norse the name means 'bloody hoof'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Blóðughófi adalah kuda tunggangan dewa Freyr yang digambarkan mampu melintasi api dan kegelapan; dalam Nordik Kuno namanya berarti "kuku berdarah".
claims.quote: Blóðughófi est, dans la mythologie nordique, le cheval servant de monture au dieu Freyr. Il est décrit comme capable de traverser le feu et les ténèbres. ... En vieux norrois, le nom Blóðughófi signifie « sabot sanglant ».

claims.statement: In Skírnismál Freyr gives Skírnir his horse, which can run through fire to Jötunheimar for the wooing of Gerðr, though the horse is not named.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Skírnismál, Freyr memberikan kudanya kepada Skírnir, kuda yang mampu berlari menembus api menuju Jötunheimar untuk meminang Gerðr, tetapi kuda itu tidak dinamai.
claims.quote: In Skírnismál, Freyr gives Skírnir his horse, which is able to run through fire to reach Jötunheimar for the wooing of Gerðr; however, the horse here is not named.

claims.statement: The title of Gerður Kristný's Blóðhófnir (2010), a poetic retelling of the myth of Gerðr, Freyr and Skírnir, varies the name Blóðughófi.
claims.statement_id: Judul Blóðhófnir (2010) karya Gerður Kristný, penceritaan ulang puitis mitos Gerðr, Freyr, dan Skírnir, adalah variasi nama Blóðughófi.
claims.quote: The title of Gerður Kristný's Blóðhófnir (2010), a poetic retelling of the myth of Gerðr, Freyr, and Skírnir, is a variation on the name Blóðughófi.

claims.statement: Durinn (or Durin) is a dwarf according to stanza 10 of the Völuspá in the Poetic Edda, repeated in the Gylfaginning of the Prose Edda; he was the second created after the first and foremost dwarf, Mótsognir.
claims.statement_id: Durinn (atau Durin) adalah kurcaci menurut bait ke-10 puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi, diulang dalam Gylfaginning dari Edda Prosa; ia yang kedua diciptakan setelah kurcaci pertama dan terkemuka, Mótsognir.
claims.quote: is a dwarf according to stanza 10 of the poem Völuspá from the Poetic Edda, and repeated in Gylfaginning from the Prose Edda. He was the second created after the first and foremost dwarf Mótsognir.

claims.statement: He is also attested in Hervarar saga, forging the magic sword Tyrfing with the dwarf Dvalin; in variant texts of the saga he is called Dulinn.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga tercatat dalam Hervarar saga, menempa pedang ajaib Tyrfing dibantu kurcaci Dvalin; dalam varian teks saga itu ia disebut Dulinn.
claims.quote: He is also attested in Hervarar saga, where he forged the magic sword Tyrfing with the help of the dwarf Dvalin. In variant texts of the saga Durinn is known as Dulinn.

claims.statement: Durin, also Durinn (Old Norse), was the second dwarf created by the gods in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Durin, juga Durinn (Nordik Kuno), adalah kurcaci kedua yang diciptakan para dewa dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Durin, auch Durinn (altnordisch), war der zweite Zwerg, der von den Göttern in der nordischen Mythologie erschaffen wurde.

claims.statement: In Karl Simrock's translation of the Völuspá the gods take counsel over who should make the race of dwarfs from Brimir's blood and limbs; Modsognir became the mightiest and Durin after him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Völuspá oleh Karl Simrock, para dewa bermusyawarah siapa yang akan menciptakan bangsa kurcaci dari darah dan anggota tubuh Brimir; Modsognir menjadi yang terkuat dan Durin sesudahnya.
claims.quote: Hochheilge Götter hielten Rath, Wer schaffen sollte der Zwerge Geschlecht Aus Brimirs Blut und blauen Gliedern. Da ward Modsognir der mächtigste Dieser Zwerge und Durin nach ihm.

claims.statement: Durin and Mótsognir formed spontaneously when Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve made the world from the body of the cosmic giant Ymir; the gods then gave them intelligence and human appearance.
claims.statement_id: Durin dan Mótsognir terbentuk dengan sendirinya ketika Odin serta saudaranya Vili dan Ve menciptakan dunia dari tubuh raksasa kosmis Ymir; para dewa lalu memberi mereka akal dan rupa manusia.
claims.quote: Durin (el durmiente) y Mótsognir (de feroz rugido) se formaron de forma espontánea cuando Odín y sus hermanos Vili y Ve crearon el mundo a partir del cuerpo del gigante cósmico Ymir. ... Los dioses les concedieron la inteligencia y una apariencia humana.

claims.statement: In J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium Durin is the name of several Dwarf kings, including Durin the Deathless, eldest of the Seven Fathers of their race.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legendarium J. R. R. Tolkien, Durin adalah nama beberapa raja kurcaci, termasuk Durin yang Abadi, yang tertua dari Tujuh Leluhur bangsa mereka.
claims.quote: In the legendarium of J. R. R. Tolkien, Durin is the name given to several kings of the Dwarves including Durin the Deathless, the eldest of the Seven Fathers of their race.

claims.statement: Hafgufa (Old Norse haf 'sea' + gufa 'steam') is a sea creature said to inhabit Iceland's waters (the Greenland Sea) and south toward Helluland; though thought a sea monster, research suggests the stories came from a whale feeding technique called trap-feeding.
claims.statement_id: Hafgufa (Nordik Kuno haf, "laut", + gufa, "uap") adalah makhluk laut yang konon menghuni perairan Islandia (Laut Greenland) hingga ke selatan menuju Helluland; meski dianggap monster laut, penelitian menduga kisahnya berasal dari teknik makan paus yang disebut trap-feeding.
claims.quote: Hafgufa (Old Norse: haf "sea" + Old Norse: gufa "steam"; "sea-reek"; "sea-steamer") is a sea creature, purported to inhabit Iceland's waters (Greenland Sea) and southward toward Helluland. Although it was thought to be a sea monster, research suggests that the stories originated from a specialized feeding technique among whales known as trap-feeding.

claims.statement: In the Snorra Edda the hafgufa appears in the list (þulur) of whales; some copies spell it hafgúa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Snorra Edda, hafgufa muncul dalam daftar (þulur) paus; di beberapa salinan ejaannya hafgúa.
claims.quote: In the Snorra Edda, the hafgufa ("sea-steamer") appears in the list (þulur) of whales. The spelling is also hafgúa in some copies.

claims.statement: The hafgufa is mentioned in the mid-13th-century Norwegian tract Konungs skuggsjá ('King's Mirror'); later recensions of Örvar-Odds saga present hafgufa and lyngbakr as similar but distinct creatures.
claims.statement_id: Hafgufa disebut dalam risalah Norwegia pertengahan abad ke-13 Konungs skuggsjá ("Cermin Raja"); resensi lebih akhir Örvar-Odds saga menampilkan hafgufa dan lyngbakr sebagai makhluk serupa tetapi berbeda.
claims.quote: The hafgufa is mentioned in the mid-13th century Norwegian tract called the Konungs skuggsjá ("King's Mirror"). Later recensions of Örvar-Odds saga feature hafgufa and lyngbakr as similar but distinct creatures.

claims.statement: The King described the hafgufa as a massive fish more like an island than a living thing, concluded there were only two and both infertile or the seas would be full of them, and said it belched out so much food that it drew all nearby fish.
claims.statement_id: Sang raja menggambarkan hafgufa sebagai ikan raksasa yang lebih mirip pulau daripada makhluk hidup, menyimpulkan hanya ada dua ekor yang mandul agar laut tidak penuh dengan mereka, dan menuturkan bahwa ia bersendawa mengeluarkan banyak makanan yang menarik semua ikan di sekitarnya.
claims.quote: He described the hafgufa as a massive fish that looked more like an island than like a living thing. ... He concluded there must be only two of them and that they must be infertile, otherwise the seas would be full of them. The King described the feeding manner of hafgufa: The fish would belch, which would expel so much food that it would attract all the nearby fish.

claims.statement: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga from the late 14th century hafgufa is the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl), feeding on whales, ships, men and anything else; the crew sailed between its nostril and lower jaw, mistaking them for two great rocks.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi akhir Örvar-Odds saga dari akhir abad ke-14, hafgufa adalah monster laut (sjóskrímsl) terbesar yang memangsa paus, kapal, manusia, dan apa saja; awak kapal berlayar di antara lubang hidung dan rahang bawahnya, yang mereka kira dua batu besar.
claims.quote: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga dating to the late 14th century, hafgufa is described as the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl ) of all, which fed on whales, ships, men, and anything it could catch ... it was the nostril and lower jaw which they had sailed in-between, although they mistook these for two massive rocks rising from the sea.

claims.statement: Once many fish had crowded into its mouth and belly, it shut its mouth and devoured them all at once.
claims.statement_id: Setelah banyak ikan berdesakan di mulut dan perutnya, ia menutup mulut dan melahap semuanya sekaligus.
claims.quote: Once a large number had crowded into its mouth and belly, it would close its mouth and devour them all at once.

claims.statement: Hafgufa ('ocean vapour'), or havguva, havgumsen or havstramben, is an enormous sea monster described in Norse literature.
claims.statement_id: Hafgufa ("uap samudra"), atau havguva, havgumsen, atau havstramben, adalah monster laut raksasa yang digambarkan dalam sastra Nordik.
claims.quote: Hafgufa (vapeur de l'océan), ou havguva, ou havgumsen, ou havstramben désigne un énorme monstre marin décrit dans la littérature nordique

claims.statement: According to Bishop Gunnerus of Trondheim, it was the kraken itself.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Uskup Gunnerus dari Trondheim, hafgufa adalah kraken itu sendiri.
claims.quote: Selon l'évêque Gunnerus de Trondheim, il s'agirait du kraken lui-même.

claims.statement: Norse mythology has a bird named Víðópnir.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik ada burung bernama Víðópnir.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Víðópnir ( Old Norse pronunciation:

claims.statement: According to the eddic poem Fjölsvinnsmál, Víðópnir or Víðófnir is a rooster in the crown of the world tree, variously shown as a falcon, sitting between the eyes of the cosmic eagle Hræsvelgr atop Mímameiðr, a tree taken to be Yggdrasil.
claims.statement_id: Menurut puisi Edda Fjölsvinnsmál, Víðópnir atau Víðófnir adalah ayam jantan di mahkota pohon dunia, kadang digambarkan sebagai elang alap, yang duduk di antara mata elang kosmis Hræsvelgr di puncak Mímameiðr, pohon yang dianggap sama dengan Yggdrasil.
claims.quote: According to the eddic poem, Fjölsvinnsmál, Víðópnir or Víðófnir [ˈwiːðˌoːvnez̠] is a rooster that inhabits the crown of the world tree, variously represented as a falcon, sitting between the eyes of the cosmic eagle Hræsvelgr at the top of the tree of life, Mímameiðr (Mimi's Tree), a vast tree taken to be identical with the World Tree, Yggdrasil.

claims.statement: He is golden and shines like a thunderstorm; as an almost immortal guardian he watches over the world tree's integrity and is a terror to the giant Surt of Muspellsheim and the giantess Sinmara of Niflheim.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwarna emas dan bersinar seperti badai petir; sebagai penjaga yang nyaris abadi ia menjaga keutuhan pohon dunia, dan dianggap momok bagi raksasa Surt dari Muspellsheim dan raksasa perempuan Sinmara dari Niflheim.
claims.quote: Er ist von goldener Farbe und leuchtet wie ein Gewitter. Als nahezu unsterblicher Wächter wacht er über die Unversehrtheit dieses Weltenbaums. So gilt er auch als Schrecken des Riesen Surt aus der Feuerwelt Muspellsheim und der Riesin Sinmara aus der Eiswelt Niflheim

claims.statement: Widofnir can only be killed with the weapon Lævateinn, a twig made by Loki; Sinmara guards it and lends it only to one who first brings her a tail feather of Widofnir.
claims.statement_id: Widofnir hanya dapat dibunuh dengan senjata Lævateinn, ranting buatan Loki; senjata itu dijaga Sinmara, yang hanya meminjamkannya kepada orang yang lebih dulu membawakan bulu ekor Widofnir.
claims.quote: Widofnir kann man aber nur töten mit der Waffe Läwateinn (an. Lævateinn „Schadenszweig“), einem Zweig, der von Lopt („der Luftige“ = Loki) geschaffen wurde. Über die Waffe wacht Sinmara, die unterhalb der Totengitter wohnt. Sie leiht Läwateinn für den Kampf mit Widofnir aber nur dem, der ihr zuvor eine Schwanzfeder Widofnirs bringt.

claims.statement: Karl Joseph Simrock interpreted the name Widofnir (Viðófnir/Viðópnir) as Windofnir, 'wind-weaver'.
claims.statement_id: Karl Joseph Simrock menafsirkan nama Widofnir (Viðófnir/Viðópnir) sebagai Windofnir, "penenun angin".
claims.quote: Karl Joseph Simrock deutete den Namen Widofnir (an. Viðófnir/Viðópnir) im Sinne von Windofnir „Windweber“.

claims.statement: Jacob Grimm compared it with the cock on maypoles and the weathercock on church towers, and thought Christian missionaries may have appropriated the heathen symbol with new meaning.
claims.statement_id: Jacob Grimm membandingkannya dengan ayam di tiang Mei dan ayam angin di menara gereja, dan menganggap mungkin para misionaris Kristen mengambil alih simbol kafir itu dengan makna baru.
claims.quote: Jacob Grimm stellte ihr Aussagen zum Hahn auf den Maibäumen, zum Wetterhahn auf den Kreuzbäumen der Wenden und zum Wetterhahn auf den Kirchtürmen vergleichend gegenüber. Er hielt es für möglich, dass die christlichen Missionare sich das heidnische Symbol umdeutend aneigneten

claims.statement: One source treats Víðópnir as Veðrfölnir, the falcon standing between the eyes of Hraesvelg, the giant eagle atop Yggdrasil.
claims.statement_id: Satu sumber menyamakan Víðópnir dengan Veðrfölnir, elang alap yang berdiri di antara mata Hraesvelg, elang raksasa di puncak Yggdrasil.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie nordique, Veðrfölnir (le dessèche-vent en vieux norrois) (orthographié également , Víðópnir ou Víðófnir) est le faucon qui se tient entre les yeux de Hraesvelg, l'aigle géant qui se tient tout en haut d'Yggdrasil.

claims.statement: Belsnickel (also Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel and others) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer in the folklore of the Palatinate of south-western Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland and the Odenwald of Baden-Württemberg, also preserved among the Pennsylvania Dutch and German-Brazilians.
claims.statement_id: Belsnickel (juga Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel, dan lain-lain) adalah sosok pembawa hadiah Natal yang pemarah dan berbaju bulu dalam cerita rakyat Pfalz di barat daya Jerman di sepanjang Rhein, Saarland, dan Odenwald di Baden-Württemberg, dan juga dipertahankan dalam komunitas Pennsylvania Dutch serta Jerman-Brasil.
claims.quote: Belsnickel (also known as Belschnickel, Belznickle, Belznickel, Pelznikel, Pelznickel, Bell Sniggle) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer figure in the folklore of the Palatinate region of southwestern Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland, and the Odenwald area of Baden-Württemberg. The figure is also preserved in Pennsylvania Dutch communities and Brazilian-German communities.

claims.statement: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in German-speaking folklore and may be based on the Knecht Ruprecht myth; but he visits alone rather than with Nicholas, combining threatening and benign aspects.
claims.statement_id: Belsnickel berkerabat dengan pendamping Santo Nikolaus lain dalam cerita rakyat Eropa berbahasa Jerman dan mungkin bersumber dari mitos Knecht Ruprecht; namun ia tidak mendampingi Nikolaus, melainkan datang sendiri dan memadukan sisi mengancam dan sisi baik.
claims.quote: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in the folklore of German-speaking Europe. He may have been based on an older German myth, Knecht Ruprecht ... Unlike those figures, Belsnickel does not accompany Saint Nicholas but instead visits alone and combines both the threatening and the benign aspects

claims.statement: Belsnickel is a fur-wearing man, ragged and dishevelled, carrying a switch to beat naughty children and pockets full of cakes, sweets and nuts for good ones.
claims.statement_id: Belsnickel adalah lelaki berbaju bulu yang compang-camping dan kumal, membawa ranting untuk memukul anak nakal sekaligus saku penuh kue, permen, dan kacang untuk anak baik.
claims.quote: Belsnickel is a man wearing fur. He is typically very ragged and disheveled. He wears torn, tattered, and dirty clothes, and he carries a switch in his hand with which to beat naughty children, but also pockets full of cakes, candies, and nuts for good children.

claims.statement: The Belsnickel figure originated in the Palatinate; immigrants to Pennsylvania brought their German traditions, and Belsnickel was known there in the early 1800s.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh Belsnickel berasal dari Pfalz; para imigran ke Pennsylvania membawa tradisi Jerman mereka, dan Belsnickel sudah dikenal di Pennsylvania awal abad ke-19.
claims.quote: The Belsnickel character originated in the Palatinate. When people immigrated to Pennsylvania, they brought their German traditions with them. Belsnickel was known in Pennsylvania in the early 1800s.

claims.statement: The traditional Belsnickel came to houses one or two weeks before Christmas, rapped on door or window with his stick, had children answer a question or sing, then tossed sweets on the floor; those who jumped too fast might be struck with his switch.
claims.statement_id: Belsnickel tradisional datang ke rumah-rumah satu atau dua minggu sebelum Natal, mengetuk pintu atau jendela dengan tongkat, meminta anak menjawab pertanyaan atau bernyanyi, lalu melempar permen ke lantai; anak yang terlalu cepat menyambar bisa terkena rantingnya.
claims.quote: The traditional Belsnickel showed up at houses 1–2 weeks before Christmas ... He would rap on the door or window with his stick and often the children would have to answer a question for him or sing some type of song. In exchange he would toss candies onto the floor. If the children jumped too quick for the treats, they may end up getting struck with Belsnickel's switch.

claims.statement: Pelzmärtel (also Pelzmartin and others) is a name for the pre-Christmas gift-bringer common in parts of Franconia (southern Germany), regionally also Pelznickel.
claims.statement_id: Pelzmärtel (juga Pelzmartin dan sebagainya) adalah nama pembawa hadiah sebelum Natal yang umum di sebagian Franken (Jerman selatan), dan di beberapa daerah disebut Pelznickel.
claims.quote: Der Pelzmärtel (auch Pelzemärtel, Pelzermärtel, Pelzamärdl, Belzermärdl, Bulzermärtl, Belzemärdl oder Pelzmartin) ist ein in Teilen Frankens (Süddeutschland) verbreiteter Name für den vorweihnachtlichen Gabenbringer. Regional tritt er auch als Pelznickel auf.

claims.statement: Pelzmärtel comes from Pelz (West Central German pelzen, 'to beat') and Märtel, a diminutive of Martin; Nickel is the diminutive of Nikolaus.
claims.statement_id: Pelzmärtel berasal dari Pelz (dari kata Jerman Tengah Barat pelzen, "memukul") dan Märtel, bentuk kecil nama Martin; Nickel adalah bentuk kecil Nikolaus.
claims.quote: Pelzmärtel leitet sich von Pelz (vom westmitteldeutschen „pelzen“, was so viel wie „prügeln“ bedeutet) und der fränkischen Verkleinerungsform für Martin, „Märtel“ bzw. „Martel“; „Nickel“ ist entsprechend die Verkleinerungsform für Nikolaus.

claims.statement: In Brazilian towns such as Guabiruba, Santa Catarina, he is known as Pelznickel, appearing two days a year, on St Nicholas's day and Christmas Eve; said to live in the forest the rest of the year, he is called Papai Noel do Mato, 'Santa of the forest'.
claims.statement_id: Di kota-kota Brasil seperti Guabiruba, Santa Catarina, ia dikenal sebagai Pelznickel yang muncul dua hari setahun, pada hari Nikolaus dan malam Natal; sepanjang sisa tahun ia konon tinggal di hutan sehingga dijuluki Papai Noel do Mato, "Sinterklas hutan".
claims.quote: wie Guabiruba, im Staat Santa Catarina, ist er unter dem Namen Pelznickel bekannt. ... Der Pelznickel erscheint an zwei Tagen im Jahr, an Nikolaus und an Heiligabend. Den Rest des Jahres lebe er im Wald. Darum wird er dort auch als Papai Noel do Mato, „Weihnachtsmann des Walds“, bezeichnet.

claims.statement: The Elwetritsch is an imaginary bird-like creature reported in south-western Germany (especially the Palatinate and nearby); with emigrants the belief spread to Eastern Europe and North America (Pennsylvania) in the 18th century and to South America (Brazil) in the 19th.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch (juga Elwetrittche, Ilwedritsch) adalah makhluk khayalan mirip burung yang dikabarkan di barat daya Jerman (terutama Pfalz dan sekitarnya); bersama emigran, kepercayaan ini menyebar ke Eropa Timur dan Amerika Utara (Pennsylvania) pada abad ke-18 dan ke Amerika Selatan (Brasil) pada abad ke-19.
claims.quote: also Elwetrittche, Ilwedritsch; in the plural Elwedritsche(n) - is an imaginary bird-like creature that is reported in southwest Germany (especially in the Palatinate and neighboring regions). ... With emigrants, the belief in the existence of Elbedritsche also spread to Eastern Europe and North America (Pennsylvania) in the 18th century and to South America (Brazil) in the 19th century.

claims.statement: The Elwetritsch (mock-scientific Latin Bestia palatinensis) is a bird-like fabulous creature of south-western Germany, especially the Palatinate, seen as the local counterpart of the Bavarian Wolpertinger or Thuringian Rasselbock.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch (dalam Latin semu ilmiah Bestia palatinensis) adalah makhluk khayalan mirip burung dari barat daya Jerman, terutama Pfalz, dan dianggap padanan lokal Wolpertinger dari Bayern atau Rasselbock dari Thüringen.
claims.quote: in pseudowissenschaftlichem Latein Bestia palatinensis) ist ein vogelähnliches Fabelwesen, von dem in Südwestdeutschland und vor allem in der Pfalz berichtet wird. Die Elwetritsch ist als lokale Entsprechung zu Fabelwesen anderer Regionen anzusehen, wie dem bayerischen Wolpertinger oder dem thüringischen Rasselbock.

claims.statement: Elwetritschen are described as broadly chicken-like but said to be barely able to use their wings, so they keep to underbrush or under vines; they are sometimes shown with deer antlers and a very long beak.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch digambarkan mirip ayam, tetapi konon hampir tak bisa memakai sayapnya sehingga harus tinggal di semak belukar atau di bawah tanaman anggur; kadang digambarkan bertanduk rusa dan berparuh sangat panjang.
claims.quote: Elwetritschen werden als im weitesten Sinne hühnerähnlich beschrieben. Allerdings heißt es, sie könnten ihre Flügel kaum gebrauchen, weshalb sie sich überwiegend im Unterholz oder unter den Rebstöcken aufhalten müssten. Manchmal werden Elwetritschen auch mit einem Hirschgeweih abgebildet, ihr Schnabel wird oft als sehr lang dargestellt.

claims.statement: Elwetritschen are said to come from crossing chickens, ducks and geese with forest kobolds and elves; as poultry offspring they lay eggs, which because of their forest-spirit descent grow during brooding.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch konon berasal dari persilangan ayam, bebek, dan angsa dengan kobold dan peri penghuni hutan; sebagai keturunan unggas ia bertelur, tetapi karena darah roh hutannya, telurnya tumbuh selama masa pengeraman.
claims.quote: Elwetritschen sollen aus Kreuzungen von Hühnern, Enten und Gänsen mit im Wald lebenden Kobolden und Elfen stammen. Als Geflügelabkömmlinge legen sie selbstverständlich Eier, die allerdings wegen der Waldgeisterherkunft während der Brutzeit wachsen.

claims.statement: In many Palatinate villages tourists are offered an Elwetritsch hunting licence for fun; the best time is dark new-moon nights, and in one variant the catcher needs a sack, an oil lamp and a club.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak desa Pfalz, wisatawan ditawari izin berburu Elwetritsch sebagai hiburan; waktu berburu terbaik malam gelap saat bulan baru, dan dalam satu cara penangkap memerlukan karung, lampu minyak, dan pentung.
claims.quote: In etlichen pfälzischen Gemeinden wird Touristen als launiger Zeitvertreib der Erwerb eines Elwetritschen-Jagdscheins angeboten. ... Die günstigste Jagdzeit sind dunkle Neumond­nächte. Bei einer Variante der Jagd benötigt der Fänger einen Sack, eine Öllampe und einen Knüppel.

claims.statement: Beaters shout 'tritsch, tritsch' and strike trees or vineyard posts to flush the creatures into the sack; the often unsuspecting catcher is sometimes secretly left outdoors until he gets home frozen and empty-handed.
claims.statement_id: Para penghalau berteriak "tritsch, tritsch" dan memukul pohon atau tiang kebun anggur agar Elwetritsch lari ke karung; penangkap yang sering tak curiga kadang ditinggalkan diam-diam di luar sampai pulang kedinginan tanpa hasil.
claims.quote: Treiber versuchen, durch lautes „Tritsch, tritsch“-Rufen und durch Stockschläge gegen Bäume oder Weinbergspfähle die Elwetritschen aufzuscheuchen, damit sie in den Sack des Fängers flüchten. ... Der häufig ahnungslose Fänger und Jagdscheinaspirant wird gelegentlich heimlich im Freien zurückgelassen, bis er endlich durchgefroren – und ohne Jagdbeute – heimfindet.

claims.statement: One reading holds the second part of the name unclear, while the first refers to elves or Elben, female forest spirits of Germanic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Satu tafsiran menganggap asal bagian kedua nama itu tidak jelas, sedangkan bagian pertama merujuk pada elf atau Elben, roh hutan perempuan dalam mitologi Jermanik.
claims.quote: Eine Deutung geht davon aus, die Herkunft des zweiten Wortteils sei unklar und strittig, während der erste Bezug nehme auf die Elfen beziehungsweise Elben als weibliche Waldgeister aus der germanischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: The oldest written mention comes from Luckenbach, Texas: in 1847 sources reported German hunters had seen an 'Elfendritschenwolpertinger' in the woods around South Grape Creek.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis tertua berasal dari Luckenbach, Texas: pada 1847 sumber melaporkan para pemburu Jerman melihat seekor "Elfendritschenwolpertinger" di hutan sekitar South Grape Creek.
claims.quote: The oldest written mention to date comes from Luckenbach, Texas. In 1847, sources reported that an “Elfendritschenwolpertinger” had been seen by German hunters in the woods around South Grape Creek.

claims.statement: To protect themselves from Elwetritsch attacks, hunters drink plenty of alcohol before and during the hunt, its smell supposedly keeping the creatures away.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi diri dari serangan Elwetritsch, para pemburu minum banyak alkohol sebelum dan selama perburuan, yang baunya konon menjauhkan makhluk itu.
claims.quote: Um sich vor Angriffen der Elwetritschen zu schützen, trinken die Jäger vor und während der Jagd reichlich Alkohol, dessen Geruch angeblich die Elwetritschen auf Distanz hält.

claims.statement: The fur-bearing trout is a legendary creature of American and Icelandic folklore that grew thick fur to keep warm; tales of furry fish date to the 17th century, and the earliest American publication is a 1929 Montana Wildlife article by J.H. Hicken.
claims.statement_id: Trout berbulu adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Amerika dan Islandia yang menumbuhkan bulu tebal untuk menjaga panas tubuh; kisah ikan berbulu berasal dari abad ke-17, dan terbitan Amerika tertua adalah artikel majalah Montana Wildlife tahun 1929 oleh J.H. Hicken.
claims.quote: The fur-bearing trout (or furry trout) is a legendary creature found in American folklore and Icelandic folklore. According to folklore, the trout has created a thick coat of fur to maintain its body heat. Tales of furry fish date to the 17th century. The earliest known American publication dates from a 1929 Montana Wildlife magazine article by J.H. Hicken.

claims.statement: Fur-bearing trout are purportedly found in the Arkansas River, northern North America and Iceland; the tale says the waters are so cold the fish evolved fur, while another theory blames four jugs or two bottles of hair tonic spilled into the Arkansas River.
claims.statement_id: Trout berbulu konon ditemukan di Sungai Arkansas, Amerika Utara bagian utara, dan Islandia; menurut kisahnya air di sana begitu dingin sehingga ikan itu menumbuhkan bulu, sementara teori lain menyebut empat kendi atau dua botol tonik rambut tumpah ke Sungai Arkansas.
claims.quote: Fur-bearing trout are fictional creatures that are purportedly found in the Arkansas River, northern North America, and Iceland. ... the waters of lakes and rivers in the area are so cold that they evolved a thick coat of fur to maintain their body heat. Another theory says that it is due to four jugs – or two bottles – of hair tonic being spilled into the Arkansas River.

claims.statement: One early claim comes from a 17th-century Scottish immigrant's letter to relatives about 'furried animals and fish' being plentiful in the New World.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu klaim awal berasal dari surat seorang imigran Skotlandia abad ke-17 kepada kerabatnya tentang berlimpahnya "hewan dan ikan berbulu" di Dunia Baru.
claims.quote: one of the earlier claims date to a 17th-century Scottish immigrant's letter to his relatives referring to "furried animals and fish" being plentiful in the New World.

claims.statement: In Icelandic legend the Loðsilungur is a furry trout created by demons and giants, an inedible fish that overruns rivers as punishment for human wickedness.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Islandia, Loðsilungur adalah trout berbulu ciptaan setan dan raksasa, ikan tak bisa dimakan yang memenuhi sungai sebagai hukuman atas kejahatan manusia.
