claims.quote: According to Icelandic legend, the Lodsilungur (Loðsilungur [is]) is a furry trout that is the creation of demons and giants. The Lodsilungur are described as inedible fish that overwhelm rivers and are a form of punishment for human wickedness.

claims.statement: No fur-bearing trout species is known, but the mould Saprolegnia can infect fish and make them look covered in white 'fur'.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada spesies trout berbulu yang diketahui, tetapi jamur Saprolegnia dapat menginfeksi ikan sehingga tampak tertutup "bulu" putih.
claims.quote: There are no known examples of any fur-bearing trout species, but other examples of hair-like growths on fish are known. The "cotton mold", Saprolegnia, can infect fish, which can result in the appearance of fish covered in white "fur".

claims.statement: The trucha peluda is a legendary creature of US and Icelandic folklore; a taxidermy specimen by Ross C. Jobe in the Royal Museum of Scotland is a trout with white rabbit fur 'ingeniously' attached.
claims.statement_id: Trucha peluda adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Serikat dan Islandia; spesimen awetan buatan Ross C. Jobe di Royal Museum of Scotland adalah trout yang "dengan cerdik" ditempeli bulu kelinci putih.
claims.quote: La trucha cubierta de pelos (o trucha peluda) es una criatura legendaria que aparece en el folclore estadounidense y en el islandés. ... Una trucha peluda taxidermizada por Ross C. Jobe es un ejemplar del Museo Real de Escocia; se trata de una trucha con pelo de conejo blanco «ingeniosamente» adherido.

claims.statement: The hamingja was a type of female guardian spirit in Norse mythology believed to accompany a person and decide their luck and happiness; hence the word also means happiness, as in modern Icelandic, and when the person died it passed to a beloved family member.
claims.statement_id: Hamingja adalah jenis roh pelindung perempuan dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini menyertai seseorang dan menentukan untung serta kebahagiaannya; karena itu namanya juga berarti kebahagiaan, seperti dalam bahasa Islandia modern, dan saat orang itu meninggal, hamingja beralih kepada anggota keluarga tercinta.
claims.quote: The hamingja was a type of female guardian spirit in Norse mythology. It was believed that she accompanied a person and decided their luck and happiness. Consequently, the name was also used to indicate happiness, and that is what it means in modern Icelandic. When a person died, the hamingja passed to a beloved family member

claims.statement: One's hamingja could be lent to a friend, as when Hjalti Skeggiason, before a perilous voyage, asked Olaf II of Norway to lend him his; it usually appears in sleep as an animal, or can be a sleeping person's spirit in animal form, like Bödvar Bjarki in the saga of Hrólfr Kraki.
claims.statement_id: Hamingja bisa dipinjamkan kepada teman, seperti saat Hjalti Skeggiason hendak berlayar berbahaya dan meminta Olaf II dari Norwegia meminjamkan hamingja-nya; ia biasanya muncul saat tidur berwujud hewan, atau bisa berupa roh orang tidur dalam rupa hewan, seperti Bödvar Bjarki dalam saga Hrólfr Kraki.
claims.quote: It was even possible to lend one's own hamingja to a friend, as happened when Hjalti Skeggiason was about to leave on a perilous voyage and asked Olaf II of Norway to lend him his hamingja. It usually appears during sleep in the form of an animal. It can also be the spirit of a sleeping person who appears in the form of an animal, as Bödvar Bjarki in the saga of Hrólfr Kraki.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology hamingja (Old Norse 'luck') refers to two concepts: the personified good fortune of an individual or family, and the altered appearance of shape-shifters; Andy Orchard and Rudolf Simek note parallels with the fylgja.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, hamingja (Nordik Kuno, "keberuntungan") merujuk pada dua konsep: perwujudan untung baik seseorang atau keluarga, dan rupa yang berubah dari pengubah wujud; Andy Orchard dan Rudolf Simek mencatat kemiripannya dengan fylgja.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, hamingja (Old Norse "luck") refers to two concepts: the personification of the good fortune or luck of an individual or family, the altered appearance of shape-shifters. Both Andy Orchard and Rudolf Simek note parallels between the concept of the hamingja and the fylgja.

claims.statement: In Norse belief the Hamingja is a family's tutelary force, which could be pictured as a gigantic woman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Nordik, Hamingja adalah kekuatan pelindung sebuah keluarga yang dapat digambarkan sebagai perempuan raksasa.
claims.quote: La Hamingja est, dans les croyances nordiques, la force tutélaire d'une famille, que l'on pouvait représenter par une femme gigantesque.

claims.statement: This tutelary force watched over the good conduct of its descendants.
claims.statement_id: Kekuatan pelindung ini mengawasi perilaku baik keturunannya.
claims.quote: cette force tutélaire, qui veillait au bon comportement de ses descendants.

claims.statement: The luck may be passed to the owner's descendant or to a tribe member for a perilous journey; it grants wealth, success and power, accrues over a lifetime, and hamingja is sometimes used to mean honour.
claims.statement_id: Keberuntungan itu dapat dialihkan kepada keturunan pemiliknya atau kepada anggota suku untuk perjalanan berbahaya; ia memberi kekayaan, keberhasilan, dan kekuasaan, bertambah sepanjang hidup, dan kadang hamingja dipakai untuk menyebut kehormatan.
claims.quote: Luck may be transferred to a descendant of the owner, or to a member of a tribe for a perilous journey. It accords wealth, success and power, and it accrues over a life time. Sometimes hamingja is used to denote honor.

claims.statement: Icovellauna was a Celtic goddess worshipped in Gaul; her shrines included an octagonal temple at Le Sablon in Metz, built over a spring and yielding five inscriptions to her, and Trier, where she was honoured in an inscription in the Altbachtal temple complex.
claims.statement_id: Icovellauna adalah dewi Kelt yang dipuja di Gaul; tempat pemujaannya meliputi kuil segi delapan di Le Sablon, Metz, yang dibangun di atas mata air dan menghasilkan lima prasasti untuknya, serta Trier, tempat ia dihormati dalam prasasti di kompleks kuil Altbachtal.
claims.quote: Icovellauna was a Celtic goddess worshiped in Gaul. Her places of worship included an octagonal temple at Le Sablon in Metz, originally built over a spring, from which five inscriptions dedicated to her have been recovered, and Trier, where Icovellauna was honored in an inscription in the Altbachtal temple complex.

claims.statement: Both places lie in the Moselle valley of eastern Gaul, now Lorraine in France and Rhineland-Palatinate in Germany; one inscription was, unusually, cut on a copper tablet in Roman cursive.
claims.statement_id: Kedua tempat itu berada di lembah Sungai Moselle di Gaul timur, kini Lorraine di Prancis dan Rheinland-Pfalz di Jerman; salah satu prasasti, agak tidak biasa, diukir pada lempeng tembaga dengan huruf kursif Romawi.
claims.quote: Both of these places lie in the valley of the river Moselle of eastern Gaul in what are now Lorraine in France and Rhineland-Palatinate in Germany. One such inscription was, somewhat unusually, inscribed on a copper tablet in Roman cursive letters.

claims.statement: At the Metz temple a spiral staircase led down to the water so worshippers could leave offerings in the spring or take the waters; ex-votos there included a statuette of a local Gaulish Mercury, coins and ceramics of the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.
claims.statement_id: Di kuil Metz, tangga melingkar turun ke permukaan air sehingga pemuja dapat meninggalkan persembahan di mata air atau mengambil airnya; persembahan di sana meliputi patung kecil Merkurius Gaul lokal, koin, dan keramik dari abad ke-2 hingga ke-4 M.
claims.quote: At the temple in Metz, a spiral staircase led down to the water level, allowing worshipers to leave offerings in the spring and/or to take the waters. A statuette of a local Gaulish Mercury was among the ex-votos deposited at the shrine, which also included coins and ceramics dating from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.

claims.statement: Demarolle glosses Icovellauna as bonne fontaine, 'good fountain'; Miranda Green follows Joseph Vendryes in reading Gaulish ico- as 'water', calling her a 'water goddess' of the Sablon nymphaeum, a thermal spring site.
claims.statement_id: Demarolle mengartikan nama Icovellauna sebagai bonne fontaine, "mata air yang baik"; Miranda Green mengikuti Joseph Vendryes menafsirkan akar Gaul ico- sebagai "air" dan menyebutnya "dewi air" penguasa nymphaeum di Sablon, situs mata air panas.
claims.quote: Demarolle glosses the name Icovellauna as bonne fontaine or "good fountain". Miranda Green follows Joseph Vendryes in interpreting the Gaulish root ico- as "water" and characterizes Icovellauna as a "water goddess" who "presided over the nymphaeum at Sablon in the Moselle Basin, a thermal spring-site".

claims.statement: Icovellauna, called 'most holy divinity' on the ex-votos, is often associated with the goddess Mogontia.
claims.statement_id: Icovellauna, yang disebut "dewi yang sangat suci" pada persembahan nazar, sering dikaitkan dengan dewi Mogontia.
claims.quote: Icovellauna qualifiée de "très sainte divinité" sur les ex-voto est souvent associée à la déesse Mogontia

claims.statement: An emanation of the Celtic mother goddess Herta, she presides over turbulent, sacred waters rising from the bowels of the Earth.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai pancaran dewi-ibu Kelt Herta, ia menguasai aliran air bergolak dan suci yang keluar dari perut bumi.
claims.quote: Émanation de la déesse-mère celte Herta, elle préside les flux d'eaux turbulentes et sacrées venues des entrailles de la Terre.

claims.statement: Xavier Delamarre considers Vendryes' reading very improbable and, on etymological grounds, suggests ico- may name a bird, perhaps the woodpecker.
claims.statement_id: Xavier Delamarre menganggap tafsiran Vendryes sangat tidak mungkin dan, atas dasar etimologi, mengusulkan ico- sebagai nama burung, mungkin pelatuk.
claims.quote: Xavier Delamarre, however, considers Vendryes' interpretation to be very improbable; on purely etymological grounds, he suggests that ico- might be the name of a bird, perhaps the woodpecker.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Hati Hróðvitnisson is a wolf who, according to Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, chases Máni, the Moon, across the night sky, and his patronymic marks him as Fenrir's son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Hati Hróðvitnisson adalah serigala yang menurut Edda Prosa karya Snorri Sturluson mengejar Máni, sang Bulan, di langit malam, dan nama patronimiknya menunjukkan ia putra Fenrir.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Hati Hróðvitnisson (first name meaning "He Who Hates", or "Enemy") is a wolf that, according to Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, chases Máni, the Moon, across the night sky ... Hati's patronymic Hróðvitnisson ... indicates that he is the son of Fenrir

claims.statement: Snorri also names a wolf Mánagarmr ('Moon-Hound') as the mightiest of the giantess's progeny, who will swallow the Moon and gorge on the dead; presumably another name for Hati or Sköll taken from folklore, anglicised Managarm or Manegarm.
claims.statement_id: Snorri juga menyebut serigala bernama Mánagarmr ("Anjing Bulan") sebagai keturunan terkuat sang raksasa perempuan, yang akan menelan Bulan dan melahap orang mati; ini diduga nama lain Hati atau Sköll yang diambil Snorri dari cerita rakyat, dan dapat ditulis Managarm atau Manegarm.
claims.quote: Snorri also names a wolf named Mánagarmr ("Moon-Hound", or "Moon's Dog") as the most powerful of the giantess's progeny, and goes on to say that he will swallow the Moon and gorge on the dead. This is presumably an alternate name for Hati or Sköll that Snorri took from folklore. It can be anglicized as Managarm, Manegarm

claims.statement: Managarm (Old Norse Mánagarmr, 'moon-hound') is a hound of Norse mythology; per the Younger Edda he is the son of the giantess Angrboda of the Iron Wood, roaming the earth devouring the flesh of the dead while his brothers Hati and Skalli chase the Moon and the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Managarm (Nordik Kuno Mánagarmr, "anjing bulan") adalah anjing dalam mitologi Nordik; menurut Edda Muda ia putra raksasa Angrboda yang tinggal di Hutan Besi, berkeliaran di bumi memakan daging orang mati, sementara saudaranya Hati mengejar Bulan dan Skalli mengejar Matahari.
claims.quote: Managarm (altnordisch Mánagarmr; dt. „Mondhund“) ist ein Hund aus der Nordischen Mythologie. ... Er ist laut der jüngeren Edda der Sohn der Riesin Angrboda, einer alten Frau, die im Eisenwald wohnt. Managarm geht auf der Erde umher und verschlingt das Fleisch der Toten, während sein Bruder Hati den Mond und sein Bruder Skalli die Sonne verfolgt.

claims.statement: At Ragnarök Hati corners the Moon and Managarm, grown the biggest and strongest of the brood from corpse-flesh, swallows it; the Moon's blood splashes the Sun and darkens it.
claims.statement_id: Saat Ragnarök, Hati menyudutkan Bulan, dan Managarm, yang menjadi terbesar dan terkuat karena daging mayat, menelannya; darah Bulan memercik ke Matahari dan menggelapkannya.
claims.quote: Zu Ragnarök, dem Weltuntergang, stellt Hati den Mond und Managarm, durch das Leichenfleisch zum größten und stärksten seiner Brut geworden, verschlingt ihn. Das Blut des Mondes spritzt auf die Sonne und verdunkelt sie.

claims.statement: In another tradition the wolf Hati swallows the Moon himself while Managarm must watch longingly, as punishment for eating corpses; Managarm resembles Garm, the hound guarding the underworld Hel.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi lain, serigala Hati sendiri yang menelan Bulan sementara Managarm hanya bisa menonton sebagai hukuman karena memakan mayat; Managarm mirip dengan Garm, anjing penjaga dunia bawah Hel.
claims.quote: Einer anderen Überlieferung nach wird der Wolf Hati den Mond selbst verschlingen, während Managarm schmachtend zusehen muss (als Strafe für seinen Leichenfraß). Managarm weist Ähnlichkeiten mit der Sagengestalt des Garm auf, dem Hund, der die Unterwelt Hel bewacht.

claims.statement: The Swedish metal band Månegarm is named after Managarm.
claims.statement_id: Band metal Swedia Månegarm dinamai menurut Managarm.
claims.quote: Nach Managarm ist die schwedische Metal-Band Månegarm benannt.

claims.statement: In Scandinavian folklore mylingar were the phantasmal forms of children's souls forced to roam the earth until they could persuade someone to bury them properly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, mylingar adalah penjelmaan arwah anak-anak yang terpaksa berkeliaran di bumi sampai bisa membujuk seseorang untuk menguburkan mereka dengan layak.
claims.quote: In Scandinavian folklore, the mylingar were the phantasmal incarnations of the souls of children that had been forced to roam the earth until they could persuade someone (or otherwise cause enough of a ruckus to make their wishes known) to bury them properly.

claims.statement: The myling (also utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic, ihtiriekko and liekkiö in Finnish) is said to chase lone wanderers at night, jump on their backs and demand to be carried to the graveyard; it grows heavier as the graveyard nears, and if the victim fails to reach it, kills them in rage.
claims.statement_id: Myling (juga utburd di Norwegia, útburður di Islandia, ihtiriekko dan liekkiö di Finlandia) konon mengejar pengembara yang sendirian di malam hari, melompat ke punggungnya dan meminta dibawa ke pemakaman; ia makin berat saat mendekati pemakaman, dan bila korban gagal mencapainya, myling membunuhnya dengan murka.
claims.quote: The myling (also known as utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic and ihtiriekko and liekkiö in Finnish) is said to chase lone wanderers at night and jump on their backs, demanding to be carried to the graveyard ... apparently grow heavier as they near the graveyard ... If one should prove unable to make it into the cemetery, the myling kills its victim in a rage.

claims.statement: It can be heard singing at night, revealing the mother's crime; it can be helped by naming it or by finding the body and burying it in holy soil.
claims.statement_id: Nyanyiannya di malam hari dapat membongkar kejahatan sang ibu; myling dapat ditolong dengan memberinya nama atau menemukan jasadnya dan menguburkannya di tanah suci.
claims.quote: It can be heard singing in the night, thereby revealing the mother's crime. Ways to help the myling is to give it a name or to find the corpse and bury it in holy soil.

claims.statement: The belief that mylingar are enraged and vengeful earned them a reputation as one of the most menacing ghosts in Scandinavian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Keyakinan bahwa myling murka dan menuntut balas membuatnya dikenal sebagai salah satu hantu paling mengancam dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
claims.quote: The belief that mylings are enraged and seeking revenge is what gave them the reputation as one of the most menacing types of ghosts in Scandinavian folklore.

claims.statement: In Swedish folk belief a myling (also myrding) was the revenant of an unbaptised newborn murdered and hidden by its mother; in some traditions the dead child was even buried under the cottage's wooden floor.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, myling (juga myrding) adalah mayat hidup bayi yang belum dibaptis, dibunuh dan disembunyikan ibunya; menurut sebagian tradisi bayi itu bahkan dikubur di bawah lantai kayu pondok.
claims.quote: Ein Myling (schwedisch: myling, myrding) war im schwedischen Volksglauben ein Wiedergänger eines ungetauften, neugeborenen Kindes, das von seiner Mutter ermordet und versteckt wurde. Manchen Überlieferungen zufolge wurde das tote Kind sogar unter dem Holzboden in der Hütte begraben

claims.statement: The unbaptised child could be heard crying 'give me a name!', and one could save it by answering 'you can have mine' and giving one's own name.
claims.statement_id: Bayi yang belum dibaptis itu bisa terdengar berseru "beri aku nama!", dan orang dapat menyelamatkannya dengan menjawab "ambillah namaku" sambil menyebut namanya sendiri.
claims.quote: Das ungetaufte Kind konnte man ebenfalls um Hilfe rufen hören mit den Worten: „Gib mir einen Namen!“ und man konnte das Kind retten, indem man antwortete: „Du kannst meinen haben, ich heiße N. N.“

claims.statement: The word comes from Swedish myrding or mörding, from Old Swedish myrða, 'to murder', so myling means 'the murdered one'; it is attested in Swedish since 1647.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini berasal dari bahasa Swedia myrding atau mörding, dari Swedia Kuno myrða, "membunuh", sehingga myling berarti "yang dibunuh"; kata ini tercatat dalam bahasa Swedia sejak 1647.
claims.quote: Das Wort stammt vom schwedischen myrding bzw. mörding, abgeleitet von altschwedisch: myrða mit der Bedeutung „morden“. Myling bedeutet also „Ermordetes“. Das Wort ist im schwedischen Sprachgebrauch seit 1647 belegt.

claims.statement: In the mobile game Year Walk players find lost mylings for the Brook Horse to care for, and in the PC game Phasmophobia the myling is one of the ghosts one may meet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gim seluler Year Walk pemain mencari myling yang hilang untuk dititipkan pada Brook Horse, dan dalam gim PC Phasmophobia myling adalah salah satu hantu yang dapat ditemui.
claims.quote: In the mobile game Year Walk, part of the game is spent finding lost Mylings to put in the care of the Brook Horse. ... In the PC game Phasmophobia where you take the role of a ghost hunter, one of the possible ghosts you may encounter is a Myling.

claims.statement: In Norwegian folklore Selma (Seljordsormen, 'the Seljord serpent') is a legendary sea serpent said to live in the 13-kilometre Lake Seljord (Seljordsvatnet) in Seljord Municipality, Telemark, Norway.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Norwegia, Selma (Seljordsormen, "ular Seljord") adalah ular laut legendaris yang konon hidup di Danau Seljord (Seljordsvatnet) sepanjang 13 kilometer di Kotamadya Seljord, Telemark, Norwegia.
claims.quote: In Norwegian folklore, Selma (Norwegian: Seljordsormen , "the Seljord serpent") is a legendary sea serpent said to live in the 13-kilometre-long (8-mile) Lake Seljord (Seljordsvatnet ) in Seljord Municipality, Telemark, Norway.

claims.statement: The serpent has been discussed since at least the 18th century; eyewitness accounts peak in hot, quiet summers, and the oldest written account, from 1750, says it circled the rowboat of a man from Bø crossing from Ulvenes to Nes.
claims.statement_id: Ular laut ini diperbincangkan sedikitnya sejak abad ke-18; kesaksian cenderung memuncak saat musim panas yang panas dan tenang, dan catatan tertulis tertua dari 1750 menyebut makhluk itu mengitari perahu dayung milik lelaki dari Bø yang menyeberang dari Ulvenes ke Nes.
claims.quote: The sea serpent has been the subject of discussion since at least the 18th century. Eyewitness descriptions of encounters have tended to peak during hot, quiet summers. The oldest written account of the creature dates from 1750, when it was said to have rounded a rowboat belonging to a man from Bø rowing across from Ulvenes to Nes.

claims.statement: Selma has appeared on the arms of Seljord since 1989; designed by sculptor Trygve Magnus Barstad, they show Selma in gold on red.
claims.statement_id: Selma tampil di lambang Seljord sejak 1989; lambang rancangan pematung Trygve Magnus Barstad itu menampilkan Selma berwarna emas di atas latar merah.
claims.quote: The sea serpent Selma has been depicted in the coat of arms of Seljord since 1989. Designed by sculpturer Trygve Magnus Barstad, the arms show Selma in a gold-color on a red background.

claims.statement: Selma is said to be between 4 and 50 metres long, pitch black, with a horse- or crocodile-like head, sometimes with a pair of front flippers and one or two humps.
claims.statement_id: Selma konon panjangnya antara 4 dan 50 meter, hitam legam, berkepala mirip kuda atau buaya, dan kadang disebut bersirip depan sepasang serta berpunuk satu atau dua.
claims.quote: Selma soll zwischen 4 und 50 Meter lang sein, von pechschwarzer Farbe und mit einem pferde- oder krokodilähnlichem Kopf. Gelegentlich wird auch von einem Paar Vorderflossen und ein bis zwei Buckeln gesprochen.

claims.statement: In 1977 the Swedish cryptozoologist Jan-Ove Sundberg recorded strange sonar signals on the lake, apparently showing a large target moving about 18 metres below his boat.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1977 kriptozoolog Swedia Jan-Ove Sundberg merekam sinyal sonar aneh di danau itu yang tampaknya menunjukkan sasaran besar bergerak sekitar 18 meter di bawah perahunya.
claims.quote: 1977: Der schwedische Kryptozoologe Jan-Ove Sundberg, ein begeisterter Selma-Fan, nahm seltsame Sonarsignale auf dem See auf, die offenbar ein großes Ziel anzeigten, das sich in einer Tiefe von etwa 18 Metern unter seinem Boot bewegte.

claims.statement: Sundberg tried to catch Selma with a giant fish-trap, years after failing to catch Nessie with a sea-serpent trap; this attempt also failed.
claims.statement_id: Sundberg mencoba menangkap Selma dengan perangkap raksasa berbentuk bubu, setelah bertahun-tahun sebelumnya gagal menangkap Nessie; upaya itu juga gagal.
claims.quote: Sundberg wollte Selma mithilfe einer gewaltigen Falle in Form einer Reuse einfangen, nachdem er mehrere Jahre zuvor schon vergeblich versucht hatte, Nessie mit einer Seeschlangenfalle zu fangen. Der Versuch blieb erfolglos.

claims.statement: In Scandinavian folklore the troll cat is a witch's familiar that sucked cows' milk and spat it into the witch's pails and entered homes to lick cream; similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare and troll ball.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, kucing troll adalah makhluk peliharaan penyihir yang mengisap susu sapi dan memuntahkannya ke ember susu penyihir serta masuk ke rumah untuk menjilat krim; makhluk serupa antara lain kelinci susu, terwelu susu, dan bola troll.
claims.quote: A troll cat is the familiar of a witch in Scandinavian folklore. Troll cats sucked milk from cows and spat it out in the witches' milk pails, and went into homes to lick up cream. Aside from cats, similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare, and ball-shaped troll ball.

claims.statement: Witches reportedly made them from 'human hair, nails, wood shavings and the like'; the Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa show a ball-of-yarn shape, while another kind looked like an ordinary cat, and harming it harmed the witch too.
claims.statement_id: Penyihir konon membuatnya dari "rambut manusia, kuku, serutan kayu, dan semacamnya"; nama Norwegia trollnøste dan trollnøa menunjukkan wujud gulungan benang, sedangkan jenis lain tampak seperti kucing biasa, dan melukainya akan melukai penyihir juga.
claims.quote: Witches reportedly were able to create them from "human hair, nails, wood shavings, and the like" ... The Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa indicate their shapes: those troll cats looked like balls of yarn. Another kind of troll cat had the appearance of an ordinary cat; but, unlike the ball-shaped troll cat, harming the cat-shaped troll cat would result in the same harm to the witch.

claims.statement: Shooting a troll cat was thought to make milk spray from the wound; it had to be buried with the witch, or she would leave her grave to fetch it. A related creature is the tilberi, a milk thief and witches' aide in Icelandic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Menembak kucing troll diyakini membuat susu menyembur dari lukanya; kucing itu harus dikubur bersama penyihirnya, atau penyihir akan keluar dari kuburnya untuk mengambilnya. Makhluk terkait adalah tilberi, pencuri susu pembantu penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Islandia.
claims.quote: In addition, it was thought that shooting a troll cat would cause milk to spray from its wound. ... The troll cat would have to be buried with the witch, or the witch would have to leave her grave to retrieve it. ... A related creature is the tilberi, a milk thief and witches' aide in Icelandic folklore.

claims.statement: Belief in troll cats seems linked to observing matter (such as hair) regurgitated by cattle; the slime mould Fuligo septica and spittlebug foam were seen as troll-cat droppings.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada kucing troll tampaknya berkaitan dengan pengamatan benda (seperti rambut) yang dimuntahkan sapi; jamur lendir Fuligo septica dan busa serangga ludah dianggap kotoran kucing troll.
claims.quote: The existence of troll cats appears to be related to the observation of matter (such as hair) regurgitated by cattle. The slime mold Fuligo septica and the foam made by spittle bugs were seen as troll cat droppings.

claims.statement: In Swedish folk belief a bjära (also mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten and others) was a being a witch used to steal neighbours' cows' milk; it could be a hare (Småland), a cat or bird (Dalarna) or a ball of yarn (Norrland).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, bjära (juga mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten, dan lain-lain) adalah makhluk yang dipakai penyihir untuk mencuri susu sapi tetangga; ia bisa berwujud terwelu (Småland), kucing atau burung (Dalarna), atau gulungan benang (Norrland).
claims.quote: Una bjära (mjölkhare, trollhare, pukhare, puken, trollkatten, baran, bärarn) era, en las creencias populares suecas, un ser característico que una bruja usaba para robar leche de las vacas de los vecinos. Una bjära podía ser una liebre (Småland), un gato o un pájaro (Dalarna) o un ovillo (Norrland).

claims.statement: The first description of how a bjära is made comes from a witch trial at Söderala, Hälsingland, on 15 January 1597.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi pertama cara membuat bjära berasal dari pengadilan sihir di Söderala, Hälsingland, pada 15 Januari 1597.
claims.quote: La primera descripción de cómo se fabrica una bjära es de un juicio por brujería en Söderala, Hälsingland, el 15-1-1597.

claims.statement: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to live in Aachen, Germany, featured in Aachen and Rhineland folklore, often shown as a deformed fanged calf and associated with drunken men.
claims.statement_id: Bahkauv adalah monster mitos yang konon tinggal di Aachen, Jerman, muncul dalam cerita rakyat Aachen dan Rheinland, sering digambarkan sebagai anak sapi cacat bertaring, dan dikaitkan dengan lelaki mabuk.
claims.quote: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to reside in Aachen, Germany. The creature has been featured in the folklore of both Aachen and the Rhineland. Often depicted as a deformed calf with fangs, the Bahkauv is commonly associated with drunken men.

claims.statement: The Bahkauv is typically described as an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs; legend says it lurks near fountains, streams and sewers, and Aachen's sewers and hot springs are cited as its home.
claims.statement_id: Bahkauv biasanya digambarkan seperti anak sapi memanjang atau cacat bertaring tajam; menurut legenda ia sering mengintai di dekat mata air, sungai kecil, dan selokan, dan saluran pembuangan serta mata air panas di bawah Aachen disebut sebagai tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: The Bahkauv is typically described as being similar to an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs. According to legend, the creature often lurks near fountains, streams, and sewers. The Aachen city sewers and the many thermal springs found under the city have been cited as a dwelling place for the Bahkauv.

claims.statement: The Bahkauv (from Bachkalb, 'brook calf', also Badekalb, dialect Bakauf or Bakauv) is a fabulous creature from Aachen.
claims.statement_id: Bahkauv (dari Bachkalb, "anak sapi sungai", juga Badekalb, dalam dialek Bakauf atau Bakauv) adalah makhluk khayalan dari Aachen.
claims.quote: Das Bahkauv (aus Bachkalb, auch Badekalb, mundartlich auch Bakauf, Baakauf, Bahkauf oder Bakauv) ist ein Fabelwesen aus Aachen.

claims.statement: By the legend the Bahkauv lived in the drain of the hot springs at the Büchel, the Kolbert; it looked like a large shaggy calf with sharp teeth, eyes glowing in the dark, bear-like clawed paws and a scaly tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sage, Bahkauv tinggal di saluran buangan mata air panas di Büchel yang disebut Kolbert; wujudnya seperti anak sapi besar berbulu kusut, bergigi tajam, bermata menyala dalam gelap, bercakar seperti beruang, dan berekor bersisik.
claims.quote: Nach dieser Sage hauste das Bahkauv in dem Abwasserkanal der Thermalquellen am Büchel, dem so genannten Kolbert. Seine Gestalt glich einem großen Kalb mit einem zottigen Fell. Im Maul hatte es scharfe Zähne, und seine klobigen Augen leuchteten im Dunkeln. Seine Pfoten sahen aus wie Bärentatzen mit scharfen Krallen, und sein Schweif war geschuppt

claims.statement: At night it attacked revellers, especially drunk ones heading home, jumping on them to be carried home on their shoulders; that it was a devil's beast showed in growing heavier when its bearer prayed and lighter when he cursed.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari ia menyerang orang yang pulang larut, terutama yang mabuk, melompat ke atas mereka dan minta digendong di pundak sampai rumah; tanda bahwa ia makhluk setan ialah ia makin berat bila pembawanya berdoa dan makin ringan bila ia mengumpat.
claims.quote: Nachts dagegen fiel es Nachtschwärmer an, besonders solche, die betrunken auf dem Heimweg waren. Es sprang auf sie auf und ließ sich auf ihren Schultern bis zu ihrem Zuhause tragen. ... Dass das Bahkauv ein Teufelsvieh war, erkannte man daran, dass es sich schwerer machte, wenn sein Träger betete, und dass es sich leichter machte, wenn er fluchte.

claims.statement: But the Bahkauv never killed anyone and never troubled women or children.
claims.statement_id: Namun Bahkauv tak pernah membunuh siapa pun dan tak pernah mengganggu perempuan maupun anak-anak.
claims.quote: Das Bahkauv hat aber nie jemanden umgebracht und auch Frauen und Kinder nie belästigt.

claims.statement: One legend says Pippin the Younger slew a Bahkauv lying by a spring; in 1902 Aachen erected a Bahkauv statue over an old well linked to it, which was melted down in World War II, so the city built a second in 1967.
claims.statement_id: Satu legenda menyebut Pippin Muda membunuh seekor Bahkauv yang berbaring di dekat mata air; pada 1902 Aachen mendirikan patung Bahkauv di atas sumur tua yang dikaitkan dengannya, yang dilebur untuk logamnya pada Perang Dunia II sehingga kota membangun patung kedua pada 1967.
claims.quote: One legend holds that Pippin the Younger slew a Bahkauv as it was lying by a spring. In 1902 the city of Aachen erected a statue of the Bahkauv over an old well that had been associated with the monster. This statue was melted down for its metal in World War II, prompting the city to build a second statue in 1967.

claims.statement: The Buckriders (Dutch Bokkenrijders, French Chevaliers du bouc) belong to south-eastern Dutch and north-eastern Belgian folklore: witches flying on bucks from the Devil to rob and murder people and church property, who once a year visited the Devil on the Mook Heath.
claims.statement_id: Bokkenrijders (Prancis: Chevaliers du bouc) adalah bagian dari cerita rakyat Belanda tenggara dan Belgia timur laut: penyihir yang terbang menunggangi kambing jantan pemberian Iblis untuk merampok dan membunuh rakyat serta merampas harta gereja, dan setahun sekali mereka menghadap Iblis di Padang Mook.
claims.quote: The Buckriders (Dutch: Bokkenrijders ; French: Chevaliers du bouc ) are a part of South-Eastern Dutch and North-Eastern Belgian folklore. They are witches, who rode through the sky on the back of flying bucks provided to them by the Devil to rob and murder common people and church possessions. ... Once a year, they would visit their master, the Devil, on the Mook Heath.

claims.statement: Throughout the 18th century thieves and criminals adopted the belief to frighten southern Limburg and raided a region including Limburg and parts of modern-day Germany; in response Limburg towns built defences such as moats.
claims.statement_id: Sepanjang abad ke-18, kawanan pencuri dan penjahat memakai kepercayaan ini untuk menakut-nakuti penduduk Limburg selatan dan menyerang wilayah yang mencakup Limburg dan sebagian Jerman masa kini; sebagai tanggapan kota-kota di Limburg membangun pertahanan seperti parit.
claims.quote: Throughout the 18th century, groups of thieves and other criminals adopted the belief to frighten the inhabitants of southern Limburg ... these criminal bands launched raids across a region that included Limburg, and parts of modern-day Germany. In response to the robberies towns in Limburg started to build defences like moats around them

claims.statement: It was believed the buckriders could travel fast and far through the skies to rob over a wide area and be home before dawn, hiding their crimes.
claims.statement_id: Ada kepercayaan bahwa bokkenrijders dapat menempuh jarak jauh dengan cepat lewat udara untuk merampok di wilayah luas dan pulang sebelum fajar agar kejahatannya tersembunyi.
claims.quote: The belief existed that the buckriders could travel fast and vast distances through the skies to rob in a widespread area and be home before dawn to remain obscured in their crimes.

claims.statement: Because of the occult link, authorities accused many possibly innocent men of being buckriders, most suspects were tortured, and the charges always combined robbery and witchcraft.
claims.statement_id: Karena kaitannya dengan ilmu gaib dan sihir, penguasa menuduh banyak lelaki yang mungkin tak bersalah sebagai bokkenrijder dan sebagian besar tersangka disiksa; tuduhan selalu mencakup perampokan sekaligus sihir.
claims.quote: Because of the link to the occult and witchcraft, authorities accused a large number of potentially innocent men of being buckriders and the majority of suspects were tortured ... The witch trials and robbery trials can not be seen separately in that sense: the accusations always included both robbery and witchcraft.

claims.statement: According to tradition the Bockreiter (Dutch Bokkenrijders, Limburgish Bokkeriejersj) were a gang active between 1730 and 1780 around Limburg, Herzogenrath and Schinnen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, Bockreiter (Belanda: Bokkenrijders, Limburg: Bokkeriejersj) adalah kawanan yang aktif antara 1730 dan 1780 di wilayah Limburg, Herzogenrath, dan Schinnen.
claims.quote: Die Bockreiter (Bokkenrijders in Niederländisch und Bokkeriejersj in Limburgisch) waren der Überlieferung nach eine Bande, die zwischen 1730 und 1780 im Raum Limburg, in Herzogenrath und Schinnen aktiv war.

claims.statement: An estimated 1,200 men were accused and at least 425 to 468 executed between 1743 and 1796 as buckriders.
claims.statement_id: Diperkirakan sekitar 1.200 lelaki dituduh dan sedikitnya 425 hingga 468 dieksekusi antara 1743 dan 1796 karena dihukum sebagai bokkenrijder.
claims.quote: It is estimated that about 1200 men were accused and at least between 425 and 468 men were executed between 1743 and 1796 on the conviction of being a Buckrider.

claims.statement: Based on Ton van Reen's 1986 youth novel Ontsnapt aan de galg, the TV series De Legende van de Bokkenrijders was made in 1993, and the Villa Volta ride at the Efteling park also features the gang.
claims.statement_id: Berdasarkan novel remaja Ontsnapt aan de galg (1986) karya Ton van Reen dibuat serial televisi De Legende van de Bokkenrijders pada 1993, dan wahana Villa Volta di taman hiburan Efteling juga mengangkat kisah kawanan ini.
claims.quote: Basierend auf dem 1986 erschienenen Jugendroman Ontsnapt aan de galg (deutsch: „Dem Galgen entkommen“) von Ton van Reen wurde 1993 die Fernsehserie De Legende van de Bokkenrijders gedreht ... Im niederländischen Freizeitpark Efteling steht das Mad House Villa Volta, welches die Taten der Bande ebenfalls thematisiert.

claims.statement: The name Bokkenrijders was first used publicly in 1774 in the 'trial of Wellen', a town then in the Southern Netherlands.
claims.statement_id: Nama Bokkenrijders pertama kali dipakai secara publik pada 1774 dalam "pengadilan Wellen", kota yang saat itu bagian dari Belanda Selatan.
claims.quote: Formally, the name Bokkenrijders (buckriders) was first publicly used in 1774, during the "trial of Wellen", a town in what belonged then to the Southern Netherlands.

claims.statement: The buckrider trials differed from ordinary criminal cases because they often involved an 'ungodly oath' ('I renounce God and swear submission to the Devil').
claims.statement_id: Pengadilan bokkenrijders berbeda dari perkara pidana biasa karena sering melibatkan "sumpah tak bertuhan" ("Aku menyangkal Tuhan dan bersumpah tunduk kepada Iblis").
claims.quote: The trials against the buckriders differed from 'ordinary' criminal proceedings because in many cases a so-called 'ungodly oath' was involved ("I renounce God and swear submission to the Devil").

claims.statement: Eitri, also called Sindri, is a dwarf and Brokkr's brother in Old Norse religion.
claims.statement_id: Eitri, juga disebut Sindri, adalah kurcaci dan saudara Brokkr dalam agama Nordik Kuno.
claims.quote: or Sindri) is a dwarf and the brother of Brokkr.

claims.statement: According to Skáldskaparmál, after Loki had the Sons of Ivaldi make Sif's hair, Freyr's ship Skidbladnir and Odin's spear Gungnir, he bet his head with Brokkr that Eitri could not match their craftsmanship.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skáldskaparmál, setelah Loki menyuruh para Putra Ivaldi membuat rambut Sif, kapal Skidbladnir milik Freyr, dan tombak Gungnir milik Odin, ia mempertaruhkan kepalanya dengan Brokkr bahwa Eitri tak akan mampu membuat benda yang menandingi mutu karya itu.
claims.quote: According to Skáldskaparmál, when Loki had Sif's hair, Freyr's ship Skidbladnir and Odin's spear Gungnir fashioned by the Sons of Ivaldi, he bet his own head with Brokkr that Eitri would not have been able to make items that matched the craftsmanship of those mentioned above.

claims.statement: Eitri began working at his furnace while his brother worked the bellows, but a fly (sometimes thought to be Loki himself) stung Brokkr to stop him and spoil the items.
claims.statement_id: Eitri mulai bekerja di tungkunya sementara saudaranya memompa ububan, tetapi seekor lalat (kadang dianggap Loki sendiri) menyengat Brokkr untuk menghentikannya dan merusak benda-benda itu.
claims.quote: Eitri began working in his furnace while his brother was working the bellows, but a fly (sometimes thought to be Loki himself) began stinging Brokkr, trying to stop him and spoil the items.

claims.statement: Eitri succeeded in making the golden boar Gullinbursti, the golden ring Draupnir and the hammer Mjöllnir, winning his brother the bet, though its handle was shorter than it should have been.
claims.statement_id: Eitri berhasil membuat babi emas Gullinbursti, cincin emas Draupnir, dan palu Mjöllnir sehingga saudaranya memenangkan taruhan, walau gagang palu itu lebih pendek dari semestinya.
claims.quote: Eitri succeeded in making the golden boar Gullinbursti, the golden ring Draupnir, and the hammer Mjöllnir that made his brother win the bet, even if its handle was shorter than it should have been.

claims.statement: Eitri (or Sindri) is a dwarf of Norse mythology whose brother is Brokk.
claims.statement_id: Eitri (atau Sindri) adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik, saudara Brokk.
claims.quote: Eitri (ou Sindri) est un nain de la mythologie nordique. Il a pour frère Brokk.

claims.statement: In the Marvel Cinematic Universe Eitri is a supporting character played by Peter Dinklage, mainly in Avengers: Infinity War, living on Nidavellir.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Marvel Cinematic Universe, Eitri adalah tokoh pendukung yang diperankan aktor Peter Dinklage, terutama dalam film Avengers: Infinity War, dan tinggal di Nidavellir.
claims.quote: Au sein de l'Univers cinématographique Marvel, Eitri est un personnage secondaire joué par l'acteur Peter Dinklage, essentiellement vu dans le film Avengers: Infinity War. Vivant sur Nidavellir

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Gná is a goddess running errands in other worlds for Frigg, riding the flying, sea-treading horse Hófvarpnir (Old Norse 'he who throws his hoofs about', 'hoof-thrower'); both appear in the Prose Edda written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Gná adalah dewi yang menjalankan tugas Frigg di dunia lain dan menunggang kuda terbang penapak laut Hófvarpnir (Nordik Kuno, "yang melempar-lempar kukunya", "pelempar kuku"); keduanya tercatat dalam Edda Prosa yang ditulis Snorri Sturluson pada abad ke-13.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Gná (Old Norse) is a goddess who runs errands in other worlds for the goddess Frigg and rides the flying, sea-treading horse Hófvarpnir (Old Norse "he who throws his hoofs about", "hoof-thrower" or "hoof kicker"). Gná and Hófvarpnir are attested in the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson.

claims.statement: In chapter 35 of Gylfaginning High adds that Gná rides Hófvarpnir, a horse able to ride through the air and atop the sea, and that 'once some Vanir saw her path as she rode through the air'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 35 Gylfaginning, High menambahkan bahwa Gná menunggang Hófvarpnir, kuda yang mampu melaju di udara dan di atas laut, dan bahwa "suatu kali beberapa Vanir melihat jalurnya saat ia melaju di udara".
claims.quote: In chapter 35 of the Prose Edda book Gylfaginning ... High adds that Gná rides the horse Hófvarpnir, and that this horse has the ability to ride through the air and atop the sea. High continues that "once some Vanir saw her path as she rode through the air"

claims.statement: Gná replies: 'I fly not though I fare and move through the air on Hofvarpnir, whom Hamskerpir got with Gardrofa.'
claims.statement_id: Gná menjawab: "Aku tidak terbang, tetapi melaju dan bergerak di udara di atas Hofvarpnir, yang diperanakkan Hamskerpir dengan Gardrofa."
claims.quote: I fly not though I fare and move through the air on Hofvarpnir the one whom Hamskerpir got with Gardrofa.

claims.statement: Hofvarpnir (Old Norse 'hoof-thrower') was the horse of Gná, one of the goddess Frigg's helpers; per Gylfaginning it could move through air and water, and was sired by horses named Hamskerpir and Garðrofa.
claims.statement_id: Hofvarpnir (Nordik Kuno, "pelempar kuku") adalah kuda Gná, salah satu pembantu dewi Frigg; menurut Gylfaginning ia mampu bergerak di udara dan di air, dan diperanakkan kuda-kuda bernama Hamskerpir dan Garðrofa.
claims.quote: Hofvarpnir ( del nórdico antiguo: tirador de cascos) era en la mitología nórdica, el caballo de Gna, una de las ayudantas de la diosa Frigg. Según lo que se relata en Gylfaginning, Edda prosaica, Hofvarpnir era capaz de desplazarse a través del aire y del agua. Fue engendrado por unos caballos llamados Hamskerpir y Garðrofa.

claims.statement: Hófvarpnir and the eight-legged steed Sleipnir have been cited as examples of transcendent horses in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Hófvarpnir dan kuda berkaki delapan Sleipnir disebut sebagai contoh kuda transenden dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Hófvarpnir and the eight-legged steed Sleipnir have been cited examples of transcendent horses in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: The source of these stanzas is not given and they are otherwise unattested.
claims.statement_id: Sumber bait-bait ini tidak disebutkan dan tidak tercatat di tempat lain.
claims.quote: The source for these stanzas is not provided and they are otherwise unattested.

claims.statement: The kabouter is a gnome-like creature of Dutch folklore, akin to the Irish leprechaun, Scandinavian tomte or nisse, English hob, Scottish brownie and German Klabauter or kobold.
claims.statement_id: Kabouter adalah makhluk mirip gnom dalam cerita rakyat Belanda, sekerabat dengan leprechaun Irlandia, tomte atau nisse Skandinavia, hob Inggris, brownie Skotlandia, dan Klabauter atau kobold Jerman.
claims.quote: is a gnome-like creature in Dutch folklore. The Dutch Kabouter is akin to the Irish leprechaun, Scandinavian tomte or nisse , the English hob, the Scottish brownie and the German Klabauter or kobold.

claims.statement: In Low Countries folklore kabouters are tiny people about 10–15 cm tall living in or near houses and stables, or in hills, forests or heaths; many tales mention vast kabouter kingdoms.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Negeri-Negeri Rendah, kabouter adalah orang mungil setinggi sekitar 10–15 cm yang tinggal di dalam atau dekat rumah dan kandang, atau di bukit, hutan, dan padang; banyak kisah menyebut kerajaan kabouter yang luas.
claims.quote: In the folklore of the Low Countries, kabouters are tiny people, about 10–15 cm tall, who live in or near houses and stables, or in hills, in forests or on heaths. Many stories refer to vast kabouter kingdoms

claims.statement: Kabouters can be seen as spirits who help at home by working at night and tending animals such as milking; males have long full beards, all wear tall pointed red or green hats, and they are shy and often punish people who spy on them.
claims.statement_id: Kabouter dapat dipandang sebagai roh yang membantu di rumah dengan bekerja di malam hari dan merawat ternak seperti memerah susu; yang jantan berjanggut panjang lebat dan semuanya memakai topi tinggi runcing berwarna merah atau hijau; mereka pemalu dan sering menghukum orang yang mengintip.
claims.quote: Kabouters can be regarded as spirits who help in the home by doing tasks at night and care for the animals like milking them. ... The males have long, full beards and they all wear tall, pointed hats, generally of a red or green colour. Kabouters are shy of humans and in stories often punish people for spying on them.

claims.statement: Blinding was a common punishment for spying, but they could also sour milk, blacken grain, make objects vanish or scare livestock; leaving out milk and bread improved relations, and they have various local names such as alvermanneke or auwelke.
claims.statement_id: Kebutaan adalah hukuman umum bagi pengintip, tetapi mereka juga bisa mengasamkan susu, menghitamkan biji-bijian, melenyapkan barang, atau menakuti ternak; meninggalkan susu dan roti dapat memperbaiki hubungan dengan mereka, dan mereka punya berbagai nama lokal seperti alvermanneke atau auwelke.
claims.quote: Blinding was a common punishment for spying on the gnomes, but they could also make life more difficult by souring the milk, blackening the grain, making objects disappear, or scaring the livestock. Leaving milk and bread out for kabouters was a way to improve relationships with them. ... they exist under a number of different local names such as alvermanneke or auwelke .

claims.statement: A well-known tale tells of the kabouters leaving the Campine for an unknown place after a local hunter shot their king Kyrië; in the Legend of the Wooden Shoes, an old Dutch folktale, a kabouter teaches a Dutchman to make piles and wooden shoes.
claims.statement_id: Kisah terkenal menceritakan hilangnya kabouter dari Kempen ke tempat tak dikenal setelah seorang pemburu setempat menembak raja mereka Kyrië; dalam Legenda Sepatu Kayu, kisah rakyat Belanda lama, seorang kabouter mengajari orang Belanda membuat tiang pancang dan sepatu kayu.
claims.quote: A well known story is about the disappearance of kabouters from the Campine to an unknown place after a local hunter shot their king Kyrië. ... In the Legend of the Wooden Shoes, an old Dutch folktale, a kabouter teaches a Dutch man how to make piles and wooden shoes.

claims.statement: The kabouter is a little-folk creature of Flanders, Belgium (called nuton in French-speaking Belgium) and the Netherlands, comparable to the gnome and the French lutin.
claims.statement_id: Kabouter adalah makhluk kaum kecil yang khas Flandria, Belgia (di Belgia berbahasa Prancis disebut nuton), dan Belanda, sebanding dengan gnom dan lutin Prancis.
claims.quote: Le Kabouter est une créature du petit peuple propre aux Flandres, à la Belgique (appelé « nuton » en Belgique francophone) et aux Pays-Bas. Il est comparable au gnome et au lutin français.

claims.statement: The Dutch illustrator Rien Poortvliet played an important part in modern kabouter lore with his 1976 book Leven en werken van de Kabouter (Gnomes), with text by Wil Huygen.
claims.statement_id: Ilustrator Belanda Rien Poortvliet berperan penting dalam tradisi modern kabouter lewat bukunya tahun 1976, Leven en werken van de Kabouter (Les Gnomes), dengan teks Wil Huygen.
claims.quote: L'illustrateur néerlandais Rien Poortvliet a joué un rôle important dans la tradition moderne du Kabouter avec son livre de 1976 Les Gnomes (en néerlandais Leven en werken van de Kabouter) sur des textes de Wil Huygen.

claims.statement: Lange Wapper is a Flemish folk character, a legendary giant and trickster whose tales were told especially in Antwerp and nearby towns, with similar tales prominent in other Flemish cities.
claims.statement_id: Lange Wapper adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Flandria, raksasa legendaris dan penipu yang kisahnya terutama diceritakan di Antwerpen dan sekitarnya, meski kisah serupa juga menonjol di kota-kota Flandria lain.
claims.quote: Lange Wapper is a Flemish folkloric character. He is a legendary giant and trickster whose folk tales were told especially in the city of Antwerp and its neighbouring towns, but similar tales are also prominent in other Flemish cities.

claims.statement: In a parsley bed a farmer found a huge red cabbage holding a baby; later the boy saved an old woman from drowning in the Scheldt, and she gave him the power to make himself big or small; preferring his tall form, he was nicknamed Lange Wapper.
claims.statement_id: Di petak peterseli seorang petani menemukan kubis merah raksasa berisi bayi; kelak anak itu menyelamatkan seorang nenek dari tenggelam di Sungai Schelde, dan nenek itu memberinya kemampuan membesarkan atau mengecilkan diri; karena suka tampil tinggi ia dijuluki Lange Wapper.
claims.quote: In a parsley bed, a farmer found a red cabbage that was so big it could not fit in a cauldron. ... One day he saved an old woman from drowning in the Scheldt river, and she gave him the ability to make himself big or small. Because he preferred to appear in his tall form, he gained the nickname Lange Wapper.

claims.statement: He disguised himself as a child to get breast milk, vexed drunkards and cheated children at games; his bleating laugh frightened people, who called him 'water devil'.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai anak untuk mendapat air susu, mengganggu pemabuk, dan mencurangi anak-anak dalam permainan; tawanya yang mengembik menakutkan orang sehingga ia disebut "setan air".
claims.quote: He would disguise himself as a child to receive breastmilk to drink, would vex drunkards, and would cheat children in games. His bleating laughter frightened the general public, who began to call him “water devil”.

claims.statement: It is Lange Wapper, as big as a house, who warns: 'If you get drunk again, I will break your neck!'
claims.statement_id: Sosok itu ternyata Lange Wapper, sebesar rumah, yang memperingatkan: "Kalau kau mabuk lagi, akan kupatahkan lehermu!"
claims.quote: It is Lange Wapper, as big as a house, who warns, "If you get drunk again, I will break your neck!"

claims.statement: Lange Wapper (French le Grand Wapper) is a legendary giant who plays tricks on the people of Antwerp, Belgium; he appears at night, pursues those who drank too much, and can make himself very big or very small.
claims.statement_id: Lange Wapper (Prancis: le Grand Wapper) adalah raksasa legenda yang mempermainkan warga Antwerpen, Belgia; ia muncul di malam hari, mengejar orang yang terlalu banyak minum, dan bisa membuat dirinya sangat besar atau sangat kecil.
claims.quote: Le Lange Wapper (en français, le Grand Wapper) est un géant de légende qui joue de mauvais tours aux habitants de la ville d'Anvers, en Belgique. Il apparaît la nuit et poursuit les gens qui ont trop bu. Il sait se faire très grand et très petit.

claims.statement: One version says Lange Wapper feared statues of the Virgin, which would explain their great number in the city.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi menyebut Lange Wapper takut pada patung Perawan Maria, yang konon menjelaskan banyaknya patung itu di kota.
claims.quote: Une version dit aussi que Lange Wapper avait peur des statues de la Vierge et que cela expliquerait le grand nombre de celle-ci dans la ville.

claims.statement: His name was given to a huge bridge project (Lange Wapperbrug) over part of the city, rejected by Antwerp residents in a public consultation on 19 October 2009.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dipakai untuk proyek jembatan raksasa (Lange Wapperbrug) di atas sebagian kota itu, yang ditolak warga Antwerpen dalam konsultasi publik pada 19 Oktober 2009.
claims.quote: Il a aussi donné son nom au projet d'un immense pont (Lange Wapperbrug) surplombant une partie de la même ville. Les Anversois ont rejeté le projet par consultation populaire, le 19 octobre 2009 .

claims.statement: Lange Wapper appears in several stories of Willy Vandersteen's comic series Bob et Bobette.
claims.statement_id: Lange Wapper muncul dalam beberapa kisah seri komik Bob et Bobette karya Willy Vandersteen.
claims.quote: On retrouve Lange Wapper dans quelques histoires de la série de bande dessinée Bob et Bobette de Willy Vandersteen

claims.statement: In German folklore the Nachzehrer (literally 'after-consumer'; also Nachtzehrer, 'night-consumer') is a type of Wiedergänger (revenant) believed able to drag the living after it into death, from malice or a wish to be closer to loved ones.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, Nachzehrer (harfiah "pemakan sesudah"; juga Nachtzehrer, "pemakan malam") adalah sejenis Wiedergänger (mayat hidup) yang diyakini dapat menyeret orang hidup menyusulnya ke kematian, karena dengki atau karena ingin dekat dengan orang yang dicintainya.
claims.quote: literally "after-consumer" (a creature that consumes from the afterlife) in German; also spelt Nachtzehrer, literally "night-consumer") is a type of Wiedergänger (revenant), which was believed to be able to drag the living after it into death, either through malice or through the desire to be closer to its loved ones through various means.

claims.statement: The word Nachzehrer came into use in the 19th century, but belief in the creature it names is several centuries older.
claims.statement_id: Kata Nachzehrer mulai dipakai pada abad ke-19, tetapi kepercayaan pada makhluk yang dinamainya beberapa abad lebih tua.
claims.quote: The word Nachzehrer came to use in the nineteenth century, but belief in the creature the label is applied to precedes this by several centuries.

claims.statement: This could involve eating its own shroud and clothes, thought a very common sign of a Nachzehrer; the danger was held to be especially great if the living had given the dead some of their own possessions, e.g. as grave goods.
claims.statement_id: Hal ini bisa berupa memakan kain kafan dan pakaiannya sendiri, yang dianggap tanda Nachzehrer yang sangat umum; bahayanya dianggap sangat besar bila orang hidup memberi jenazah sebagian barang miliknya, misalnya sebagai bekal kubur.
claims.quote: This could involve devouring their own funeral shrouds and clothing – thought to be a very common sign of a nachzehrer. The danger was thought to be particularly great if the living had given the deceased some of their own possessions (e.g. as grave goods).

claims.statement: Nachzehrer is a German folk-belief term, formerly common especially in the Mark, for a revenant or undead being closely related to vampires.
claims.statement_id: Nachzehrer adalah sebutan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Jerman, dulu terutama di Mark, untuk mayat hidup atau Untote yang berkerabat dekat dengan vampir.
claims.quote: Nachzehrer ist eine früher vor allem in der Mark übliche Bezeichnung im deutschen Volksglauben für einen Wiedergänger oder Untoten, der den Vampiren nah verwandt ist

claims.statement: Unlike the vampire, which must leave its grave, the Nachzehrer lies or sits underground and drains the life-force of the living, usually its survivors or fellow villagers.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari vampir yang harus meninggalkan kubur, Nachzehrer berbaring atau duduk di bawah tanah dan menyedot daya hidup orang hidup, biasanya keluarga yang ditinggalkannya atau warga desanya.
claims.quote: Im Gegensatz zum Vampir, der sein Grab verlassen müsse, liege oder sitze der Nachzehrer unter der Erde und sauge den Lebenden – meistens seinen Hinterbliebenen oder den Bewohnern seines Dorfes – die Lebenskraft ab.

claims.statement: Warding metal objects (scissors, nails, knives) were often laid on the corpse's chest, and survivors poured dried pulses or pebbles into the coffin; being possessed by the Devil, it could never count past two peas or stones.
claims.statement_id: Benda logam penangkal (gunting, paku, pisau) sering diletakkan di dada jenazah, dan keluarga menuang kacang kering atau kerikil ke peti; karena dirasuki Iblis, ia tak pernah bisa menghitung lebih dari dua kacang atau batu.
claims.quote: Oft wurden bannende Metallgegenstände (Scheren, Nägel, Messer) auf die Brust des Toten gelegt. Häufig schütteten die Hinterbliebenen auch getrocknete Hülsenfrüchte oder Kieselsteine in den Sarg. ... Da er aber vom Teufel beseelt war, konnte er nie über zwei Erbsen oder Steine hinaus kommen

claims.statement: Contrary to a long-held folklorists' view, the Nachzehrer was not confined to the partly Slavic east and north-east of Germany but was known as far as the Rhineland.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari anggapan lama dalam ilmu folklor, sebaran Nachzehrer tidak terbatas pada wilayah timur dan timur laut Jerman yang sebagian bercorak Slavia, tetapi juga sampai ke Rheinland.
claims.quote: Im Gegensatz zu einer lange verbreiteten Auffassung in der Volkskunde beschränkt sich das Verbreitungsgebiet des Nachzehrers keineswegs auf die teilweise slawisch geprägten Gebiete im Osten und Nordosten Deutschlands, sondern er war auch bis ins Rheinland verbreitet.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk mitologi atau cerita rakyat: artikel membahas klaim kasus poltergeist tahun 1967 di sebuah kantor pengacara di Rosenheim yang diselidiki parapsikolog Hans Bender dan dikritik skeptis, yaitu peristiwa modern, bukan sosok dalam tradisi. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosenheim_poltergeist_claim).

claims.statement: Türst is a folk figure of Lucerne's farming communities dating to pre-Christian times, a 'dreadful huntsman' to beware of in stormy weather, who blows his horn through villages in the stormy months before Epiphany with a pack of three-legged hounds.
claims.statement_id: Türst adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dari komunitas petani Luzern yang berasal dari masa pra-Kristen, digambarkan sebagai "pemburu mengerikan" yang harus diwaspadai saat cuaca berbadai; ia meniup terompet berburu menembus desa-desa pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani bersama kawanan anjing berkaki tiga.
claims.quote: is a legendary folkloric figure from the agricultural communities of Lucerne, dating to the pre-Christian era. He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. Türst blows his hunting horn through villages in the tempestuous months preceding Epiphany, accompanied by a baying pack of three-legged hunting dogs.

claims.statement: Türst's hallmark is his threat 'drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs' ('step right; get out of my way'): a careless walker who fails to move aside in time is turned into a member of his dog pack.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas Türst adalah ancaman "drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs" ("ke kanan, minggir"): pejalan lalai yang tak menyingkir tepat waktu diubah menjadi anggota kawanan anjingnya.
claims.quote: Türst's distinguishing features are his threat "drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs", or, roughly, "step right; get out of my way" in which the careless pedestrian is turned into a member of the dog-pack if he should fail to get out of Türst's way in time.

claims.statement: In Horw, Türst is followed by small hounds led by a one-eyed hound, his wife Sträggele, a hideous witch, and the Pfaffenkellnerin, the glowing-eyed ghost of a dead parson's mistress.
claims.statement_id: Di Horw, Türst diiringi anjing-anjing kecil yang dipimpin anjing bermata satu, istrinya Sträggele si penyihir buruk rupa, dan Pfaffenkellnerin, hantu kekasih seorang pastor yang bermata menyala.
claims.quote: In Horw, Türst is accompanied by small hounds, a leading hound with only one eye, Türst's wife, Sträggele, a hideous witch, and the Pfaffenkellnerin, the ghost of a deceased parson's mistress with glowing eyes.

claims.statement: In Rickenbach he appears in green hunting dress with a half-dog, half-pig pack; in Wolhusen people raised crosses against him, and a fallen cross brought farmers bad luck until set upright; the people of Pilatus call him a ghost and a 'dreadful huntsman'.
claims.statement_id: Di Rickenbach ia tampil berpakaian berburu hijau dengan kawanan setengah anjing setengah babi; di Wolhusen warga mendirikan salib untuk menghindarinya, dan bila salib roboh petani akan sial sampai salib ditegakkan; warga Pilatus menyebutnya hantu dan "pemburu mengerikan".
claims.quote: He appears in a green hunting costume in Rickenbach, accompanied by a pack of animals which are half dog and half pig. In Wolhusen, to avoid Türst, the citizens erected crosses. If a cross were to fall, the farmers would have bad luck until the cross stood straight again. The local people of Pilatus say that Türst is a ghost and a "dreadful huntsman"

claims.statement: Türst (also called Dürst) is a legendary figure from the Lucerne hinterland dating from heathen times, called the 'hellish huntsman'.
claims.statement_id: Türst (juga disebut Dürst) adalah tokoh legenda dari pedalaman Luzern yang berasal dari masa kafir dan disebut "pemburu neraka".
claims.quote: Der Türst (auch Dürst genannt) ist eine Sagenfigur aus dem Luzerner Hinterland, die noch aus heidnischen Zeiten stammt. Er wird als „höllischer Jäger“ bezeichnet

claims.statement: Barn doors should be left open at this time so Türst can hunt through unhindered; his wife Sträggele appears in some legends, and others say he terrifies dairy cows until they sicken and stop giving milk.
claims.statement_id: Konon pintu lumbung harus dibiarkan terbuka pada masa itu agar Türst dapat berburu menembus lumbung tanpa halangan; istrinya Sträggele muncul dalam sebagian legenda, dan legenda lain menyebut ia menakuti sapi perah hingga sakit dan berhenti menghasilkan susu.
claims.quote: It is also said that barn doors should stay open at this time, enabling Türst to hunt through the barn unhindered. Sträggele, his wife, appears in some Türst legends. Other legends say that Türst terrifies dairy cows, causing them to sicken and cease their milk production.

claims.statement: A valravn is a supernatural raven of Danish Renaissance folklore, appearing mainly in the ballad 'Valravnen' as a knight transformed into a raven whose curse can only be broken by drinking a boy's blood.
claims.statement_id: Valravn adalah gagak gaib dalam cerita rakyat Denmark masa Renaisans yang terutama muncul dalam balada rakyat "Valravnen" sebagai ksatria yang diubah menjadi gagak, yang kutukannya hanya dapat dipatahkan dengan meminum darah anak lelaki.
claims.quote: A valravn is a supernatural raven in Danish renaissance folklore. It principally appears in the folk ballad "Valravnen" (Danish: The Valravn ) where it is depicted as a knight who was transformed into a raven, and whose curse can only be broken by consuming the blood of a boy.

claims.statement: The earliest version of the ballad is known from Jens Billes Håndskrift, dated 1555–1559, though it probably originated in the late Middle Ages.
claims.statement_id: Versi tertua balada ini dikenal dari Jens Billes Håndskrift, bertanggal 1555–1559, meski balada ini diduga berasal dari akhir Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: The earliest version of the ballad is known from Jens Billes Håndskrift (Danish: Jens Bille's Handwritten Notes ), dated to 1555-1559, though the ballad is thought to have originated in the late Middle Ages.

claims.statement: In the ballad the raven asks for the maiden's first son in return for taking her to her betrothed's land; later it pierces the child's chest, drinks half his heart-blood and becomes the loveliest knight on earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam balada, gagak meminta anak lelaki pertama sang gadis sebagai imbalan membawanya ke negeri tunangannya; kemudian gagak itu menembus dada sang anak, meminum separuh darah jantungnya, dan menjadi ksatria paling rupawan di bumi.
claims.quote: "The first son you have together, will you give to me: to your betrothed's land I will then take you." ... The raven impaled his chest, drank half his heart-blood: then he turned into the loveliest knight, to ever walk the earth.

claims.statement: In Danish folklore the valraven or valravn is a supernatural raven called the 'raven of the slain'; after eating a child's heart it takes the form of a knight or a half-wolf, half-raven creature.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Denmark, valraven atau valravn adalah gagak gaib yang disebut "gagak orang yang gugur"; setelah memakan jantung seorang anak ia berwujud ksatria atau makhluk setengah serigala setengah gagak.
claims.quote: Un valraven ou valravn est, dans le folklore danois, un corbeau surnaturel décrit comme le corbeau des tués. ... Après avoir dévoré le cœur d'un enfant, il prend la forme d'un chevalier ou d'une créature mi-loup mi-corbeau.

claims.statement: In late-1800s Danish folklore, when a king or war chief was killed in battle and not buried at once, ravens devoured him and became valraven; the one that ate the king's heart gained all his knowledge and could do great evil.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Denmark akhir abad ke-19, bila raja atau panglima gugur dalam perang dan tidak segera dikuburkan, gagak-gagak memakannya dan berubah menjadi valraven; yang memakan jantung raja memperoleh seluruh pengetahuannya dan dapat berbuat sangat jahat.
claims.quote: Selon le folklore danois de la fin des années 1800, lorsqu'un roi ou un chef de guerre est tué dans une bataille et n'est pas enterré immédiatement, les corbeaux viennent et le dévorent. Cet acte les transforme en valraven. Le valraven qui a mangé le cœur du roi acquiert toute la connaissance de l'homme et peut alors accomplir des actes d'une grande malveillance

claims.statement: The ballad opens with the raven flying at night and forbidden by day; later the nobleman offers it lovely castles and half his land if only he may keep his son.
claims.statement_id: Balada itu dibuka dengan larik bahwa gagak terbang di malam hari dan tak boleh terbang di siang hari; kelak sang bangsawan menawarkan istana-istana dan separuh negerinya agar boleh mempertahankan putranya.
claims.quote: The raven flies at night, during the day he mustn't: ... Out then walked the nobleman and offered him castles so lovely: and in addition half his land, if only he could keep his son.

claims.statement: According to Jacob Grimm the vilde ravn or vilde valravn (wild raven) is equivalent to the evil troll of old Danish songs; the Old High German name is walahraban, equivalent to Danish valravn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Jacob Grimm, vilde ravn atau vilde valravn (gagak liar) setara dengan troll jahat dalam lagu-lagu Denmark lama; nama Jerman Hulu Kuno untuk valraven adalah walahraban, padanan valravn dalam bahasa Denmark.
claims.quote: Selon Jacob Grimm, le vilde ravn ou vilde valravn (corbeau sauvage) serait l'équivalent du troll diabolique dans les vieilles chansons danoises. Le nom du Valraven en vieux haut-allemand est walahraban, équivalent du danois valravn.

claims.statement: The modern Danish band Valravn draws on traditional songs.
claims.statement_id: Grup musik Denmark modern Valravn terinspirasi dari lagu-lagu tradisional.
claims.quote: comme le groupe de musique danoise moderne Valravn, qui s'inspire des chants traditionnels.

claims.statement: Baldanders or Soon-Different is a creature of Germanic literary myth with protean properties.
claims.statement_id: Baldanders atau "Segera-Lain" adalah makhluk mitos sastra Jermanik yang bersifat protean.
claims.quote: Baldanders or Soon-Different is a creature of Germanic literary myth that features protean properties.

claims.statement: Baldanders is a character in Grimmelshausen's Simplicius Simplicissimus, in its Continuatio (1669) or Sixth Book, taken from Hans Sachs's poem Baldanderst dated 31 July 1534; Sachs probably derived it from Proteus, the Greco-Roman shapeshifter.
claims.statement_id: Baldanders adalah tokoh novel Simplicius Simplicissimus karya Grimmelshausen dalam Continuatio (1669) atau Buku Keenam, diambil dari puisi Hans Sachs Baldanderst bertanggal 31 Juli 1534; Sachs kemungkinan menurunkannya dari Proteus, pengubah wujud mitologi Yunani-Romawi.
claims.quote: is a character in the novel Simplicius Simplicissimus by Grimmelshausen, appearing in its Continuatio (1669) or Sixth Book. The character was appropriated from Hans Sachs's poem Baldanderst [sic] dated to 31 July 1534. Hans Sachs probably derived his "Baldanderst" from Proteus, the shapeshifter of classical Greco-Roman mythology.

claims.statement: Baldanders then changes into a series of forms: an oak, a sow, a bratwurst, excrement, a clover meadow, cow dung, a flower, a mulberry tree and a silk carpet; the sequence shows a natural cycle of things perishing and being reborn.
claims.statement_id: Baldanders lalu berubah menjadi serangkaian wujud: pohon ek, babi betina, sosis bratwurst, kotoran, padang semanggi, kotoran sapi, bunga, pohon murbei, dan permadani sutra; urutan ini menggambarkan siklus alam tentang hal-hal yang binasa dan lahir kembali.
claims.quote: Baldanders subsequently changes into a succession of forms: an oak tree, a sow, a bratwurst sausage, then a peasant's excrement, a meadow of clovers, cow dung (Kuhfladen ), a flower, mulberry tree, and silk carpet. ... in a natural cycle of things that perish and are reborn.

claims.statement: In the novel the protagonist finds in a forest a stone figure of a god from an old Germanic temple; touched, it says it is Baldanders ('each time another'), and finally becomes a man again to teach Simplicius various skills, including talking to inanimate things.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel itu sang tokoh utama menemukan di hutan patung batu dewa dari kuil Jermanik kuno; saat disentuh, patung itu berkata ia Baldanders ("setiap kali yang lain"), dan akhirnya kembali menjadi manusia untuk mengajari Simplicius berbagai keterampilan, termasuk berbicara dengan benda mati.
claims.quote: Darin stößt der Protagonist in einem Wald auf eine Steinfigur, die einen Gott aus einem alten germanischen Tempel darstellt. Als er die Figur mit dem Finger berührt, sagt sie, sie sei Baldanders („jedesmal ein anderer“) ... Am Ende wird Baldanders wieder zum Menschen, um Simplicius in verschiedenen Fertigkeiten – unter anderem auch darin, mit leblosen Dingen zu sprechen – zu unterrichten.

claims.statement: According to Sachs and collected descriptions, Baldanders symbolises continual change in nature and society.
claims.statement_id: Menurut uraian Sachs dan uraian lain yang dihimpun, Baldanders melambangkan perubahan terus-menerus dalam alam dan masyarakat.
claims.quote: According to Sachs’ and collected descriptions, the Baldanders is a creature that is symbolic for the continual change in nature and society

claims.statement: Jorge Luis Borges listed a Baldanders in his 1974 bestiary El libro de los seres imaginarios, and the group Ougenweide wrote the song Bald anders based on Hans Sachs's creation.
claims.statement_id: Jorge Luis Borges memasukkan Baldanders dalam bestiarium El libro de los seres imaginarios (1974), dan kelompok Ougenweide menggubah lagu Bald anders berdasarkan ciptaan Hans Sachs.
claims.quote: Auch Jorge Luis Borges führt in dem von ihm 1974 herausgegeben Bestiarium El libro de los seres imaginarios einen Baldanders auf. Basierend auf Hans Sachs’ Schöpfung komponierte die Gruppe Ougenweide das Lied Bald anders, in der die Figur Baldanders die Hauptrolle spielt.

claims.statement: The name Baldanders is also used for a recurring character in Gene Wolfe's science-fantasy series The Book of the New Sun.
claims.statement_id: Nama Baldanders juga dipakai untuk tokoh berulang dalam seri fantasi ilmiah The Book of the New Sun karya Gene Wolfe.
claims.quote: The name Baldanders is also used for a recurring character in Gene Wolfe's science fantasy series The Book of the New Sun.

claims.statement: Dáinn ('Dead') or Dain is a character of Norse mythology; most tales make him a dwarf, others a king of elves.
claims.statement_id: Dáinn ("Yang Mati") atau Dain adalah tokoh mitologi Nordik; kebanyakan kisah menyebutnya kurcaci, sebagian raja para elf.
claims.quote: "Dead") or Dain is a character in Norse mythology. Mostly the tales relate to him being a dwarf and in others as king of elves.

claims.statement: His name is on King Högni's sword Dáinsleif ('Dáinn's legacy'), cursed always to kill a man when drawn.
claims.statement_id: Namanya terdapat pada pedang Raja Högni, Dáinsleif ("warisan Dáinn"), yang dikutuk agar selalu membunuh seseorang setiap kali dihunus.
claims.quote: His name is found on king Högni's sword Dáinsleif ("Dáinn's legacy"). It is laid with a curse which says it must always kill a man when it is drawn.

claims.statement: In the Hyndluljóð (7) he made Freyja's boar Hildisvíni with another dwarf, his brother Nabbi; he is a dwarf in the Völuspá's dwarf-þula (11) and in a stanza by Sigvatr Þórðarson, but in the Hávamál an elf who carved the runes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hyndluljóð (7) ia disebut membuat babi Hildisvíni milik Freyja bersama kurcaci lain, saudaranya Nabbi; ia disebut kurcaci dalam daftar kurcaci Völuspá (11) dan dalam bait Sigvatr Þórðarson, tetapi dalam Hávamál ia elf yang mengukir rune.
claims.quote: In the Hyndluljóð (7) he is said to have made Freyja's boar Hildisvíni, along with another dwarf, his brother Nabbi. Dáinn is referred to as a dwarf in the dwarf-þula of the Völuspá (11) and in a stanza by Sigvatr Þórðarson. But in the Hávamál (153) he is said to be an elf who carved the runes:

claims.statement: Dain or Dainn (Old Norse Dáinn, 'dead') is a dwarf of Norse mythology who made the goddess Freyja's golden boar Hildisvini; unlike other dwarfs he is mentioned fairly often in the old texts.
claims.statement_id: Dain atau Dainn (Nordik Kuno Dáinn, "yang mati") adalah kurcaci mitologi Nordik yang membuat babi hutan emas Hildisvini milik dewi Freyja; berbeda dari kurcaci lain, ia cukup sering disebut dalam teks lama.
claims.quote: Dain, auch Dainn (altnordisch Dáinn „gestorben“), ist ein Zwerg der nordischen Mythologie, der den goldenen Eber Hildisvini der Göttin Freyja schuf. Im Gegensatz zu anderen Zwergen wird Dain vergleichsweise häufig in den alten Texten erwähnt.

claims.statement: In J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit, Dáin II Ironfoot is a dwarf king who helps his cousin Thorin Oakenshield in the Battle of the Five Armies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Hobbit karya J. R. R. Tolkien, Dáin II Ironfoot adalah raja kurcaci yang membantu sepupunya Thorin Oakenshield dalam Pertempuran Lima Pasukan.
claims.quote: In The Hobbit by J. R. R. Tolkien, Dáin II Ironfoot is a Dwarvish King who helps his cousin Thorin Oakenshield in the Battle of the Five Armies.

claims.statement: The Hávamál stanza: 'Odin for Aesir, and Dain for the elves, Dvalin for the dwarfs, Asvid for the giants, I myself carve some.'
claims.statement_id: Bait Hávamál: "Odin bagi Æsir, dan Dain bagi para elf, Dvalin bagi para kurcaci, Asvid bagi para raksasa, aku sendiri mengukir sebagian."
claims.quote: "Odin for Aesir, and Dain for the elves, Dvalin for the dwarfs, Asvid for the giants, I myself carve some".

claims.statement: Egil is a legendary hero of the Völundarkviða and Thidreks saga; his name comes from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same legend appears in Old English Ægil on the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil on the Pforzen buckle.
claims.statement_id: Egil adalah pahlawan legendaris Völundarkviða dan Thidreks saga; namanya dari Proto-Jermanik *Agilaz, dan legenda yang sama tercermin pada Ægil dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno di Peti Franks dan Aigil dalam bahasa Alemannik di gesper Pforzen.
claims.quote: Egil is a legendary hero of the Völundarkviða and the Thidreks saga. The name is from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same legend is reflected in Old English Ægil [ˈæɡil] of the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil of the Pforzen buckle.

claims.statement: The Proto-Germanic legend can only be guessed at, but Egil seems to have been a renowned archer who with his wife Alruna defended a keep against many attackers; the Franks Casket shows Aegil and his wife in the keep, Aegil shooting at attacking troops.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk Proto-Jermanik legenda ini hanya bisa ditebak, tetapi tampaknya Egil adalah pemanah termasyhur yang bersama istrinya Alruna mempertahankan benteng dari banyak penyerang; Peti Franks menampilkan Aegil dan istrinya di dalam benteng, Aegil memanahi pasukan penyerang.
