claims.quote: The Proto-Germanic form of the legend may only be guessed at, but it appears likely that Egil was a renowned archer who defended a keep together with his wife Alruna, against numerous attackers. ... The Franks Casket shows the scene of Aegil and his wife enclosed in the keep, with Aegil shooting arrows against attacking troops.

claims.statement: In the Völundarkviða Egil is a Finnish king's son, Slagfiðr his elder and Völund his younger brother; the three marry valkyries met in swan form, Egil marrying Ölrún, daughter of the Roman Emperor (Kiár of Valland).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Völundarkviða, Egil adalah putra raja Finn dengan kakak Slagfiðr dan adik Völund; ketiganya menikahi valkyrie yang mereka temui dalam rupa angsa, dan Egil menikahi Ölrún, putri Kaisar Romawi (Kiár dari Valland).
claims.quote: In the Völundarkviða, Egil is a son of a Finn king, his elder brother being Slagfiðr, his younger one Völund. The three brothers marry valkyries they encounter in swans' form ... while Egil marries Ölrún, a daughter of the Roman Emperor (Kiár of Valland).

claims.statement: In the Thidreks saga Egil is a master archer once forced by King Nidung to shoot an apple from his son's head; he readies two arrows but succeeds with the first.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Thidreks saga, Egil adalah pemanah ulung yang pernah dipaksa Raja Nidung memanah apel dari kepala putranya; ia menyiapkan dua anak panah tetapi berhasil dengan yang pertama.
claims.quote: In the Thidreks saga, Egil acts as a masterly archer, once he is forced by king Nidung to shoot an apple from the head of his son. He readies two arrows, but succeeds with the first one.

claims.statement: In a free translation of the saga passage, Egil had his three-year-old son with him; the king put an apple on his head and told Egil to split it, and Egil took three arrows from his quiver.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan bebas petikan saga, Egil membawa putranya yang berusia tiga tahun; raja meletakkan apel di kepalanya dan meminta Egil membelahnya, dan Egil mengambil tiga anak panah dari tabungnya.
claims.quote: Egil hatte seinen Sohn mit sich. Drei Jahre alt. Der König legte einen Apfel auf sein Haupt und bat Egil den Apfel entzwei zu schießen. Egil nahm drei Pfeile aus seinem Köcher

claims.statement: Egil also gathered wild birds' feathers for his brother, from which Wieland made wings; when ordered to shoot him, Egil, as agreed, aimed at a calf's bladder full of blood carried under Wieland's arm.
claims.statement_id: Egil juga mengumpulkan bulu burung liar untuk saudaranya, yang dipakai Wieland membuat sayap; ketika disuruh menembaknya, Egil sesuai kesepakatan membidik kantong kandung kemih anak sapi berisi darah yang dibawa Wieland di ketiaknya.
claims.quote: Das zweite Mal, als er für seinen Bruder Federn von Wildvögeln sammelt. Aus diesen Federn macht sich Wieland die Flügel ... Egil zielt aber, wie vorher mit seinem Bruder vereinbart, auf eine Kalbsblase voll Blut, welche Wieland unter seiner Achsel trägt.

claims.statement: The archer Egil (also Egill or Eigill) is a brother of Wayland the Smith and thus part of the legend cycle of Dietrich von Bern.
claims.statement_id: Pemanah Egil (juga Egill atau Eigill) adalah saudara Wieland si pandai besi dan karena itu termasuk dalam lingkaran legenda Dietrich von Bern.
claims.quote: Der Bogenschütze Egil (auch Egill o. Eigill) ist ein Bruder von Wieland dem Schmied und damit eingebunden in den Sagenkreis um Dietrich von Bern.

claims.statement: Fossegrim, also the grim (Norwegian) or Strömkarlen (Swedish), is a water spirit or troll of Scandinavian folklore, often shown as a handsome naked man playing the fiddle.
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim, juga disebut grim (Norwegia) atau Strömkarlen (Swedia), adalah roh air atau troll dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki tampan tanpa busana yang bermain biola.
claims.quote: Fossegrim, also known simply as the grim (Norwegian) or Strömkarlen (Swedish), is a water spirit or troll in Scandinavian folklore. He is often depicted as a handsome, nude man playing the fiddle in

claims.statement: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler whose strings carry the sounds of forest, wind and water; he can be induced to teach, and the Swedish strömkarl's lay has eleven variations, the last reserved for the night spirits.
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim digambarkan sebagai pemain biola yang luar biasa berbakat, yang senarnya memainkan bunyi hutan, angin, dan air; ia dapat dibujuk mengajarkan keahliannya, dan lagu strömkarl Swedia konon punya sebelas variasi, yang terakhir disimpan untuk roh malam.
claims.quote: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler: the sounds of forest, wind and water play over his fiddle strings. Fossegrims can be induced to teach the skill. The Swedish strömkarl's lay is said to have eleven variations, the final one being reserved for the night spirits

claims.statement: Fossegrim will teach his skills for a secret food offering on a Thursday evening: a white he-goat thrown into a north-flowing waterfall, or smoked mutton (fenalår); if there is too little meat, he teaches only how to tune the fiddle.
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim konon mau mengajarkan keahliannya dengan imbalan persembahan makanan pada Kamis malam secara rahasia: kambing jantan putih yang dilempar ke air terjun yang mengalir ke utara, atau daging domba asap (fenalår); bila dagingnya kurang, ia hanya mengajari cara menyetel biola.
claims.quote: Fossegrim is said to be willing to teach away his skills in exchange for a food offering made on a Thursday evening and in secrecy: a white he-goat thrown with head turned away into a waterfall that flows northwards, or smoked mutton (fenalår). If there is not enough meat on the bone, he will only teach the supplicant how to tune the fiddle.

claims.statement: Famous fiddlers rumoured to have learned from the fossegrim include Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872), known as Myllarguten, and Ole Bull (1810–1880), whose statue in central Bergen shows a fossegrim playing his harp under falling water.
claims.statement_id: Pemain biola terkenal yang dikabarkan belajar dari fossegrim antara lain Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872) alias Myllarguten dan Ole Bull (1810–1880), yang patungnya di pusat Bergen menampilkan fossegrim memainkan harpa di bawah air terjun.
claims.quote: Famous fiddlers who were rumored to have learnt from the Fossegrim include Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872) known as Myllarguten and Ole Bull (1810–1880) whose statue in the centre of Bergen depicts a fossegrim playing his harp under the falling water.

claims.statement: Dungeons & Dragons introduced the fossegrim as the monster 'fossergrim' in Deities & Demigods (1980), and in God of War: Ragnarok (2022) grims are a class of frog-like enemies.
claims.statement_id: Dungeons & Dragons memperkenalkan fossegrim dengan nama "fossergrim" sebagai monster dalam Deities & Demigods (1980), dan dalam gim God of War: Ragnarok (2022) grim menjadi kelas musuh mirip katak.
claims.quote: Dungeons & Dragons introduced the fossegrim, under the name "fossergrim", as a monster in Deities & Demigods (1980). ... Grims are a class of frog-like enemies featured in the video game God of War: Ragnarok (2022).

claims.statement: Fossegrim is linked with the mill spirit (kvernknurr), related to the water spirit (nokken) and sometimes called näcken in Sweden; he is tied to watercourses (Swedish Strömkarlen means 'the man of the stream'), especially those with waterfalls (Norwegian foss).
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim dikaitkan dengan roh penggilingan (kvernknurr), berkerabat dengan roh air (nokken), dan di Swedia kadang disebut näcken; ia terkait aliran air (nama Swedia Strömkarlen berarti "lelaki aliran air"), terutama yang berair terjun (foss dalam bahasa Norwegia).
claims.quote: Fossegrim è stato associato allo spirito del mulino (kvernknurr) ed è imparentato con lo spirito dell'acqua (nokken) ed è talvolta chiamato anche näcken in Svezia. È associato ai corsi d'acqua (il nome svedese "Strömkarlen" significa "L'uomo del corso d'acqua") e in particolare ai corsi d'acqua a cascata (foss in norvegese)

claims.statement: The Heinzelmännchen are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with Cologne in Germany, akin to the brownies of Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah tangga penolong atau kobold yang dikaitkan dengan kota Köln di Jerman, mirip brownie dari Skotlandia.
claims.quote: are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with the city of Cologne in Germany, akin to brownies of Scotland.

claims.statement: The little house gnomes are said to have done all of Cologne's work at night so the citizens could be lazy by day, until a tailor's wife, curious to see them, scattered peas on the workshop floor to make them slip; infuriated, they vanished and never returned.
claims.statement_id: Gnom-gnom rumah kecil itu konon mengerjakan semua pekerjaan warga Köln di malam hari sehingga penduduk bisa bermalas-malasan di siang hari, sampai istri seorang penjahit yang ingin melihat mereka menaburkan kacang polong di lantai bengkel agar mereka terpeleset; mereka murka, menghilang, dan tak pernah kembali.
claims.quote: The little house gnomes are said to have done all the work of the citizens of Cologne during the night, so that the inhabitants of Cologne could be very lazy during the day. ... this went on until a tailor's wife got so curious to see the gnomes that she scattered peas onto the floor of the workshop to make the gnomes slip and fall. This infuriated the gnomes, who disappeared and never returned.

claims.statement: Marianne Rumpf (1976) proposed a two-pronged theory of the name, first from Heinzelmännlein, a colloquial name for mandrake dolls; the genuine Cologne dialect form is Heizemann or Heizemännche.
claims.statement_id: Marianne Rumpf (1976) mengajukan teori ganda asal nama, pertama dari bentuk Heinzelmännlein, sebutan sehari-hari untuk boneka mandragora; bentuk asli dalam dialek Köln adalah Heizemann atau Heizemännche.
claims.quote: A two-pronged theory on the origin of the name was proposed by Marianne Rumpf [de] (1976), first from the form "Heinzelmännlein" as a colloquial name for mandrake dolls ... The genuine Kölsch (Colognian) dialect form should be Heizemann/Heizemännche

claims.statement: The legend was first written down by the Cologne teacher Ernst Weyden (1805–1869) in 1826.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Heinzelmännchen pertama kali ditulis oleh guru Köln Ernst Weyden (1805–1869) pada 1826.
claims.quote: This legend of the Heinzelmännchen was first written down by the Cologne teacher Ernst Weyden (1805–1869) in 1826.

claims.statement: By legend the Heinzelmännchen were Cologne house spirits who did the citizens' work at night while they slept; their small size, pointed cap and diligence mark them as kin of kobolds, Wichtel and dwarfs.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sage, Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah Köln yang mengerjakan pekerjaan warga di malam hari saat mereka tidur; ukuran kecil, topi runcing, dan kerajinannya menunjukkan mereka segolongan dengan kobold, Wichtel, dan kurcaci.
claims.quote: Die Heinzelmännchen waren der Sage nach Kölner Hausgeister. Sie verrichteten nachts, wenn die Bürger schliefen, deren Arbeit. ... Neben ihrer geringen Größe zeigen auch typische Attribute, wie die Zipfelmütze und ihr Fleiß, dass die Heinzelmännchen zur Gruppe der Kobolde, Wichtel und Zwerge gehören.

claims.statement: The tale became popular through the 1836 ballad by the painter and poet August Kopisch, who moved the originally Rhineland legend from the Siebengebirge to Cologne.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini menjadi populer lewat versi puisi (balada) tahun 1836 karya pelukis dan penyair August Kopisch, yang memindahkan sage asal Siebengebirge di Rheinland ke Köln.
claims.quote: Populär geworden ist sie in der Gedichtfassung (Ballade) von 1836 des Malers und Dichters August Kopisch (1799–1853), mit der er die ursprünglich rheinländische Sage aus dem Siebengebirge nach Köln transportierte

claims.statement: Second, Heinz or Heinzenkunst were names of mine-draining devices, so according to Rumpf their operators may have been called Heinzelmänner.
claims.statement_id: Kedua, Heinz atau Heinzenkunst adalah nama alat pembuang air di pertambangan, sehingga menurut Rumpf para operatornya mungkin disebut Heinzelmänner.
claims.quote: Zum anderen waren Heinz oder Heinzenkunst Namen von Vorrichtungen im Bergbau zur Wasserabführung. Daher könnten nach Rumpf die Bediener solch hilfreicher Vorrichtungen Heinzelmänner genannt worden sein.

claims.statement: The Christmas market at Cologne's Heumarkt and Alter Markt is called 'Heinzels Wintermärchen' and shows Heinzelmännchen figures in various scenes.
claims.statement_id: Pasar Natal di Heumarkt dan Alter Markt di Köln bernama "Heinzels Wintermärchen" dan menampilkan figur Heinzelmännchen dalam berbagai adegan.
claims.quote: Der Weihnachtsmarkt auf dem Heumarkt und dem Platz Alter Markt in Köln nennt sich „Heinzels Wintermärchen“. Auf ihm werden Heinzelmännchenfiguren in verschiedenen Situationen dargestellt.

claims.statement: Hinzelmann (originally Hintzelmann, also Katermann or Katzen-Veit) was a kobold of northern German mythology, an ambivalent household spirit like Puck (Robin Goodfellow); the similar-sounding Heinzelmännchen of Cologne is held by modern scholars to be distinct.
claims.statement_id: Hinzelmann (aslinya Hintzelmann, juga Katermann atau Katzen-Veit) adalah kobold dalam mitologi Jerman utara, roh rumah tangga bersifat mendua yang mirip Puck (Robin Goodfellow); Heinzelmännchen dari Köln yang namanya mirip dianggap makhluk terpisah oleh sarjana modern.
claims.quote: also known as Katermann or Katzen-Veit ) was a kobold in the mythology of northern Germany. He was described as a household spirit of ambivalent nature, similar to Puck (Robin Goodfellow). The similar-sounding Heinzelmann (Heinzelmännchen) of Cologne is considered a distinct and separate being by modern scholars.

claims.statement: Grimm explains that Hinz was the cat's name in Reineke Fuchs, so Hinz or Hinze became emblematic of 'cat'.
claims.statement_id: Grimm menjelaskan bahwa Hinz adalah nama kucing dalam Reineke Fuchs, sehingga Hinz atau Hinze menjadi nama lambang "kucing".
claims.quote: Grimm explains that Hinz was the name of the cat in Reineke Fuchs (Reynard the Fox), so that Hinz/Hinze became a name that was emblematic for a "cat".

claims.statement: By the legend Hinzelmann ('Hintzelmann' in the source) began haunting Hudemühlen Castle in Lower Saxony in 1584; at first only banging was heard, then he said he was named Lüring, had a wife Hille Bingels and once lived in the Bohemian Forest mountains.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Hinzelmann (dalam sumber asli Hintzelmann) mulai menghantui Kastel Hudemühlen di Niedersachsen pada 1584; mula-mula hanya terdengar gedoran, lalu ia mengaku bernama Lüring, beristri Hille Bingels, dan dulu tinggal di pegunungan Hutan Bohemia.
claims.quote: According to this legend, the Hinzelmann ("Hintzelmann" in the original source) began haunting the castle Hudemühlen in Lower Saxony beginning in the year 1584. First only its presence was felt from the banging noises. ... began telling his personal details, that he was named Lüring, with a wife named Hille Bingels, and that he used to live in the Bohemian Forest mountain range.

claims.statement: Hinzelmann dutifully did kitchen chores such as washing dishes and scrubbing cookware, recovered lost items and groomed horses; he gave advice but could strike with a stick if ignored, and the cook or servants had to set out a bowl of sweet milk with crumbled white bread.
claims.statement_id: Hinzelmann rajin mengerjakan tugas dapur seperti mencuci piring dan menggosok perkakas, menemukan barang hilang, dan merawat kuda; ia memberi nasihat tetapi bisa memukul dengan tongkat bila diabaikan, dan juru masak atau pelayan wajib menyiapkan semangkuk susu manis berisi remah roti putih.
claims.quote: Hinzelmann would usefully and dedicatedly perform kitchen chores such as dish-washing and scrubbing cookware, recover lost items, and groom horses. It gave advice or pep talks, but could strike with a stick when his words were not paid attention to. ... The cook or the servants were obliged to put out a bowl of sweet milk with crumbled white bread in it

claims.statement: Hinzelmann was certainly a trickster, but his pranks were generally harmless; he has been compared with Puck (Robin Goodfellow) of English tradition.
claims.statement_id: Hinzelmann jelas seorang penipu, tetapi keisengannya umumnya tak berbahaya; ia dibandingkan dengan Puck (Robin Goodfellow) dari tradisi Inggris.
claims.quote: The Hinzelmann was certainly a trickster, but his pranks were generally harmless. A comparison has been made between the Hinzelmann and Puck (Robin Goodfellow) of English tradition.

claims.statement: Hinzelmann (also Lüring) is a legendary kobold said to have done good, such as housework, but could turn nasty if provoked; he appeared without form and with a child's voice, and in 1588 left Hudemühlen of his own accord and settled in Eystrup.
claims.statement_id: Hinzelmann (juga Lüring) adalah kobold dalam sage yang konon berbuat baik seperti mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah, tetapi bisa jahat bila diganggu; ia tampil tanpa wujud dengan suara anak kecil, dan pada 1588 pergi dengan sukarela dari Hudemühlen lalu menetap di Eystrup.
claims.quote: Hinzelmann (auch Lüring) ist die Bezeichnung für einen Kobold als Sagengestalt. Er soll Gutes, wie die Erledigung von Hausarbeit, vollbracht haben. Er konnte aber auch böse werden, wenn man ihn reizte. Dabei trat Hinzelmann ohne Gestalt auf und hatte die Stimme eines Kindes. ... 1588 ging er freiwillig von Hudemühlen fort und ließ sich danach in Eystrup nieder.

claims.statement: Hinzelmann also predicted the death of a castle visitor, Lord Falkenberg, who had taunted and tricked him; the annoyed spirit pronounced the lord's death in veiled terms.
claims.statement_id: Hinzelmann juga meramalkan kematian tamu kastel bernama Tuan Falkenberg, yang mengejek dan mengusilinya; Hinzelmann yang kesal mengucapkan kematian tuan itu dengan kata-kata samar.
claims.quote: Hinzelmann also predicted the demise of a visitor to the castle named lord Falkenberg, who had taunted the spirit and hassled him by playing tricks. The annoyed Hinzelmann pronounced the lord's death in veiled terms

claims.statement: By legend Hinzelmann will return when three conditions are met at once: the cook fills a broken bucket with a broken ladle, a dachshund whelps under a willow, and a child is born with only one eye.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Hinzelmann akan kembali bila tiga syarat terpenuhi bersamaan: juru masak mengisi ember rusak dengan gayung rusak, anjing dachshund beranak di bawah pohon dedalu, dan seorang anak lahir bermata satu.
claims.quote: Der Legende nach wird Hinzelmann bei gleichzeitiger Erfüllung dreier Bedingungen wiederkommen: Wenn die Köchin einen kaputten Wassereimer mit einer kaputten Kelle füllt, wenn der Dackel unter einem Weidenbaume Junge wirft und wenn ein Kind mit nur einem Auge zur Welt kommt.

claims.statement: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse 'colour, appearance') is the name of a dwarf and a jötunn in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Litr (juga Lit; Nordik Kuno, "warna, rupa") adalah nama seorang kurcaci dan seorang jötunn dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse: [ˈlitz̠] , 'colour, appearance') is the name borne by a dwarf and a jötunn in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: In Snorri Sturluson's Gylfaginning (49) Thor kicks Litr into Baldr's funeral pyre: as Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir, a dwarf named Litr ran before his feet, and Thor kicked him into the fire, where he burned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Gylfaginning (49) karya Snorri Sturluson, Litr ditendang Thor ke api pembakaran jenazah Baldr: Thor menyucikan api dengan Mjöllnir, seorang kurcaci bernama Litr berlari di depan kakinya, lalu Thor menendangnya ke api dan ia terbakar.
claims.quote: In Snorri Sturluson's Gylfaginning (49), Litr is kicked into Baldr's funeral pyre by Thor: ... Then Thor stood by and hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir; and before his feet ran a certain dwarf which was named Litr; Thor kicked at him with his foot and thrust him into the fire, and he burned.

claims.statement: The Old Norse name Litr has been translated 'colour', 'hue' or 'appearance', from a reconstructed Proto-Germanic *ulituz.
claims.statement_id: Nama Nordik Kuno Litr diterjemahkan "warna", "corak", atau "rupa", dan berasal dari bentuk Proto-Jermanik yang direkonstruksi *ulituz.
claims.quote: The Old Norse name Litr has been translated as 'colour', 'hue', or 'appearance'. It stems from a Proto-Germanic form reconstructed as *ulituz

claims.statement: Litr is also listed as a dwarf in Völuspá (12), and a dwarf Litr appears in Áns saga bogsveigis, forced by the hero Án to build him a bow.
claims.statement_id: Litr juga tercantum sebagai kurcaci dalam Völuspá (12), dan kurcaci bernama Litr muncul dalam Áns saga bogsveigis, dipaksa tokoh utama Án membuatkan busur.
claims.quote: Litr is also listed as a dwarf in Völuspá (12). A dwarf named Litr also appears in Áns saga bogsveigis, where he is coerced by the protagonist Án to build him a bow.

claims.statement: In a stanza by the skald Bragi Boddason quoted by Snorri in the Skáldskaparmál, Litr appears in a kenning for Thor, 'challenger of Lit's men' (Litar flotna fangboði); as Thor is the giants' enemy, Litr here is generally taken as a giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bait skald Bragi Boddason yang dikutip Snorri dalam Skáldskaparmál, Litr disebut dalam kenning untuk Thor, "penantang tarung orang-orang Lit" (Litar flotna fangboði); karena Thor musuh para raksasa, Litr di sini umumnya dianggap raksasa.
claims.quote: En una estrofa del escaldo Bragi Boddason citada por Snorri en Skáldskaparmál Litr es también mencionado en un kenning para Thor: «El que desafía a luchar a los hombres de Lit» («Litar flotna fangboði»). Dado que Thor es el enemigo de los gigantes, generalmente se asume que, en este kenningar, Litr debe hacer referencia a un gigante.

claims.statement: This led John Lindow to suggest there was probably only one original Litr, a giant.
claims.statement_id: Hal ini membuat John Lindow menduga bahwa semula mungkin hanya ada satu Litr, seorang raksasa.
claims.quote: Esto llevó a John Lindow a sugerir que probablemente hubiera solo un Litr original, un gigante

claims.statement: In Anderson's translation of the Gylfaginning, Thor stood by the pile and hallowed it with Mjolner; a dwarf named Lit ran before his feet, Thor kicked him into the fire, and he was burned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Anderson atas Gylfaginning, Thor berdiri di dekat tumpukan kayu pembakaran jenazah dan menyucikannya dengan Mjolner; seorang kurcaci bernama Lit berlari di depan kakinya, Thor menendangnya ke dalam api, dan ia terbakar.
claims.quote: Thor stood by and hallowed the pile with Mjolner. Before his feet ran a dwarf, whose name is Lit. Him Thor kicked with his foot and dashed him into the fire, and he, too, was burned.

claims.statement: In the same translation, the funeral pile was attended by many kinds of folk; first of all came Odin, accompanied by Frigg and the valkyries and his ravens.
claims.statement_id: Menurut terjemahan yang sama, tumpukan kayu pembakaran itu didatangi banyak jenis makhluk; yang pertama datang adalah Odin bersama Frigg, para valkyrie, dan gagak-gagaknya.
claims.quote: But this funeral-pile was attended by many kinds of folk. First of all came Odin, accompanied by Frigg and the valkyries and his ravens.

claims.statement: In Anderson's translation the dwarfs were first created and quickened in Ymer's flesh as maggots; now, by the decision of the gods, they have the understanding and likeness of men but must still dwell in the earth and in rocks.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Anderson, para kurcaci mula-mula tercipta dan hidup di daging Ymer sebagai belatung; kini, atas keputusan para dewa, mereka memperoleh akal dan rupa manusia, tetapi tetap harus tinggal di dalam bumi dan di bebatuan.
claims.quote: The dwarfs had first been created and had quickened in Ymer’s flesh, and were then maggots; but now, by the decision of the gods, they got the understanding and likeness of men, but still had to dwell in the earth and in rocks.

claims.statement: A dwarf named Litr appears in Þorsteins saga Víkingssonar as foster-father of Halfdan, sworn brother of Viking. After Dís, daughter of King Kol Kroppinbak of India, uses a magic drinking horn to afflict Viking with leprosy, Halfdan asks Litr to steal the horn from Dís.
claims.statement_id: Seorang kurcaci bernama Litr muncul dalam Þorsteins saga Víkingssonar sebagai bapak asuh Halfdan, saudara sumpah Viking. Setelah Dís, putri Raja Kol Kroppinbak dari India, memakai tanduk minum ajaib untuk menjangkitkan kusta pada Viking, Halfdan meminta Litr mencuri tanduk itu dari Dís.
claims.quote: A dwarf named Litr appears in Þorsteins saga Víkingssonar. In this, he is the foster-father of Halfdan, sworn brother of Viking. After Dís, daughter of King Kol Kroppinbak of India, uses a magic drinking horn to afflict Viking with leprosy, Halfdan asks Litr to steal the horn from Dís.

claims.statement: Litr does not want to, fearing Dís, but agrees and returns with the horn seven days later, which heals Viking.
claims.statement_id: Litr tidak mau karena takut kepada Dís, tetapi ia setuju dan kembali dengan tanduk itu tujuh hari kemudian; tanduk itu menyembuhkan Viking.
claims.quote: Litr does not want to, fearing Dís, but he agrees and returns with the horn seven days later, which heals Viking.

claims.statement: Dís's husband Jokul later says that Litr used tricks to betray Dís and steal the horn, and that Litr grievously wounded her.
claims.statement_id: Jokul, suami Dís, kemudian mengatakan bahwa Litr memakai tipu daya untuk mengkhianati Dís dan mencuri tanduk itu, dan bahwa Litr melukai Dís dengan parah.
claims.quote: Dís's husband Jokul says later that Litr used tricks to betray Dís and steal the horn, and also that Litr grievously wounded her.

claims.statement: Litr is also a jötunn in one version of the poem about Thor by Þorbjörn dísarskáld, where the skald lists jötnar and gýgjar killed by the god; Litr appears in only one manuscript, the others naming Lútr.
claims.statement_id: Litr juga seorang jötunn dalam satu versi puisi tentang Thor karya Þorbjörn dísarskáld, tempat sang skald mendaftar jötnar dan gýgjar yang dibunuh sang dewa; Litr hanya muncul dalam satu naskah, sedangkan naskah lain menyebut Lútr.
claims.quote: Litr is also a jötunn in one version of the poem about Thor by Þorbjörn dísarskáld, where the skald lists jötnar and gýgjar killed by the god (but Litr only appears in one manuscript, the others mentioning Lútr instead).

claims.statement: Mótsognir ('he who drinks in might'), also Móðsognir in the Hauksbók variant ('he who drinks in courage'), is ruler of the dwarfs; Völuspá 10 calls him 'lord of all the dwarves'.
claims.statement_id: Mótsognir ("yang meminum kekuatan"), juga Móðsognir dalam varian naskah Hauksbók ("yang meminum keberanian"), adalah penguasa para kurcaci; Völuspá 10 menyebutnya "penguasa semua kurcaci".
claims.quote: "he who drinks in might"), also found as Móðsognir ([ˈmoːðˌsoɣnez̠] ; Hauksbók manuscript variant), "he who drinks in courage", is the ruler of the dwarves. In Völuspà 10, he is identified as mæztr um orðinn dverga allra, "lord of all the dwarves".

claims.statement: Per Snorri in Gylfaginning 14, the dwarfs first took shape and life in Ymir's flesh as maggots, then by the gods' decision gained awareness, intelligence and human shape though living in earth and rocks; Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Snorri dalam Gylfaginning 14, para kurcaci mula-mula terbentuk dan hidup di daging Ymir sebagai belatung, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh kesadaran, akal, dan rupa manusia walau tinggal di tanah dan bebatuan; Modsognir kurcaci pertama dan Durinn yang kedua.
claims.quote: "the dwarfs had taken shape first and acquired life in the flesh of Ymir and were then maggots, but by decision of the gods they became conscious with intelligence and had the shape of men though they live in the earth and in rocks. Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn."

claims.statement: According to Völuspá 9, the dwarfs were made by 'the high holy gods', who resolved to shape them 'out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones', usually read as the blood and flesh of the primordial giant Ymir.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Völuspá 9, para kurcaci diciptakan "dewa-dewa yang mahasuci" yang memutuskan membentuk mereka "dari darah Brimir dan tulang Blainn", ungkapan yang biasa ditafsirkan sebagai darah dan daging raksasa purba Ymir.
claims.quote: According to Völuspà 9, the dwarfs were created by ginnheilög goð, "the high holy gods", who resolved to fashion them "out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones," a phrase typically interpreted to mean the blood and flesh of the primordial giant, Ymir.

claims.statement: Modsognir or Motsognir is the first dwarf in Norse mythology, created by the gods; the meaning of the name is disputed, most likely 'the weary, powerless one'.
claims.statement_id: Modsognir atau Motsognir adalah kurcaci pertama dalam mitologi Nordik yang diciptakan para dewa; arti namanya diperdebatkan, paling mungkin "yang lelah, yang tak bertenaga".
claims.quote: Modsognir, auch Motsognir (altnordisch Módsognir bzw. Mótsognir), ist in der nordischen Mythologie der erste Zwerg und wurde von den Göttern erschaffen. Umstritten ist die Bedeutung des Namens, am ehesten könnte man ihn mit ‚der Müde, der Kraftlose‘ wiedergeben

claims.statement: Scholars dispute Snorri's interpretation of Völuspá 9–10 in the Prose Edda, chiefly because his text of the verse differs from independent manuscripts of the poem.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kajian ilmiah, tafsiran Snorri atas Völuspá 9–10 dalam Edda Prosa diperdebatkan, terutama karena teks baitnya berbeda dari naskah-naskah puisi yang independen.
claims.quote: In scholarship, the interpretation of Völuspà 9–10 in Snorri's Prose Edda, (Gylfaginning 14), is disputed, primarily because his text of the verse varies from that found in independent manuscripts of the poem.

claims.statement: No sources say whether Modsognir is to be understood as king or leader of the dwarfs.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada sumber yang menyatakan apakah Modsognir harus dipahami sebagai raja atau pemimpin para kurcaci.
claims.quote: Quellen darüber, ob Modsognir als König oder Anführer der Zwerge zu verstehen ist, liegen nicht vor.

claims.statement: In Bellows's translation of the Völuspá, Motsognir is the mightiest of all the dwarfs and Durin next; they made many a likeness of men, the dwarfs in the earth, as Durin said.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Bellows atas Völuspá, Motsognir adalah yang paling perkasa di antara semua kurcaci dan Durin berikutnya; keduanya membuat banyak rupa manusia, yaitu para kurcaci di dalam bumi, seperti dikatakan Durin.
claims.quote: There was Motsognir the mightiest made Of all the dwarfs, and Durin next; Many a likeness of men they made, The dwarfs in the earth, as Durin said.

claims.statement: The holy gods took their assembly-seats and held council to find who should raise the race of dwarfs out of Brimir's blood and the legs of Blain.
claims.statement_id: Para dewa yang kudus menempati tempat sidang dan berunding untuk menentukan siapa yang akan membangkitkan bangsa kurcaci dari darah Brimir dan kaki Blain.
claims.quote: Then sought the gods their assembly-seats, The holy ones, and council held; To find who should raise the race of dwarfs Out of Brimir's blood and the legs of Blain.

claims.statement: In Anderson's translation the dwarfs were first created and quickened in Ymer's flesh as maggots; by decision of the gods they got the understanding and likeness of men but still dwell in the earth and in rocks. Modsogner was one dwarf and Durin another.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Anderson, para kurcaci mula-mula tercipta dan hidup di daging Ymer sebagai belatung; atas keputusan para dewa mereka memperoleh akal dan rupa manusia, tetapi tetap tinggal di dalam bumi dan di bebatuan. Modsogner adalah salah satu kurcaci dan Durin yang lain.
claims.quote: The dwarfs had first been created and had quickened in Ymer’s flesh, and were then maggots; but now, by the decision of the gods, they got the understanding and likeness of men, but still had to dwell in the earth and in rocks. Modsogner was one dwarf and Durin another.

claims.statement: In Sigurd Nordal's report, Sophus Bugge read the second half of verse 10 as "these dwarfs made many manikins in the earth, as Durinn said", assuming Modsognir and Durin shape the dwarfs only as manikins (dead images of men) and the Æsir then give them life.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan Sigurd Nordal, Sophus Bugge membaca paruh kedua bait 10 sebagai "para kurcaci ini membuat banyak boneka manusia di dalam bumi, seperti dikatakan Durinn", yang mengandaikan Modsognir dan Durin membentuk para kurcaci hanya sebagai boneka (gambaran mati manusia), lalu Æsir memberi mereka kehidupan.
claims.quote: Sophus Bugge read the second half of verse 10 as "these dwarfs made many manikins in the earth, as Durinn said", noting "this appears to assume Modsognir and Durin shape the dwarfs, but only as manikins (i.e. dead images of men) and that the Æsir then gave them life."

claims.statement: The original text in the Codex Regius and Hauksbók manuscripts appears to describe the dwarfs together giving shape to human beings (manlíkon), who are then brought to life by Odin and his brothers in the verses following the so-called Dvergatal.
claims.statement_id: Teks asli dalam naskah Codex Regius dan Hauksbók tampaknya menyebut para kurcaci bersama-sama membentuk manusia (manlíkon), yang kemudian dihidupkan Odin dan saudara-saudaranya dalam bait-bait sesudah yang disebut Dvergatal.
claims.quote: The original text in the Codex Regius and Hauksbók manuscripts, appear to refer to how the dwarfs together gave shape to human beings (manlíkon), which are then brought to life by Odin and his brothers in the verses following the so-called Dvergatal

claims.statement: The skogsrå, also skogsfru ('mistress of the forest'), skogsjungfru ('maiden of the forest'), skogssnua, skogssnuva or skogsnymf ('forest nymph'), is a mythical female forest creature (rå) of Swedish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Skogsrå, juga skogsfru ("nyonya hutan"), skogsjungfru ("gadis hutan"), skogssnua, skogssnuva, atau skogsnymf ("nimfa hutan"), adalah makhluk mitos perempuan (rå) penghuni hutan dalam cerita rakyat Swedia.
claims.quote: skogsfru (definite: skogsfrun , 'the mistress of the forest'), skogsjungfru (definite: skogsjungfrun , 'the maiden of the forest'), skogssnua , skogssnuva , or skogsnymf (definite: skogssnuvan , skogsnymfen , 'the forest nymph'), is a mythical female creature (or rå ) of the forest in Swedish folklore.

claims.statement: She appears as a beautiful, seemingly friendly woman; from the front like a woman, but from behind often with a tail, a hollow rotten back, one human foot and one horse foot, and skin like bark.
claims.statement_id: Ia tampil sebagai perempuan cantik yang tampak ramah; dari depan seperti perempuan, tetapi dari belakang sering berekor, berpunggung berongga dan busuk, berkaki satu manusia dan satu kuda, serta berkulit seperti kulit kayu.
claims.quote: appears in the form of a beautiful woman with a seemingly friendly temperament. She appears like a woman from the front but seen from behind she often has a tail and a hollow, rotten back, a human foot and a horse foot, and skin like tree bark.

claims.statement: Men enticed into following her into the forest are led astray as she laughs at them; one beguiled man thought he was led home, but everything vanished and he found himself in a swamp.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki yang terpikat mengikutinya ke hutan disesatkan dan ia menertawakan korbannya; seorang lelaki yang mengira diantar pulang mendapati semuanya lenyap dan dirinya berada di rawa.
claims.quote: The men who are enticed into following her into the forest are led astray, and she laughs at the victim. A beguiled man thought he was led back home, when everything disappeared and he found himself in a swamp.

claims.statement: If the seduced man is a hunter he may be rewarded with hunting luck, but punished harshly if unfaithful; she is also said to bestow her favour and bounty on charcoal makers or woodcutters.
claims.statement_id: Bila lelaki yang tergoda seorang pemburu, ia bisa diganjar keberuntungan berburu, tetapi dihukum berat bila tak setia; ia juga konon melimpahkan kasih dan karunianya kepada pembuat arang atau penebang kayu.
claims.quote: If the seduced man is a hunter, he may be rewarded with good luck in the hunt, but should he be unfaithful to the skogsrå, he will be punished with dire inconveniences. She is also said to bestow her affection and bounty upon the charcoal maker, or woodcutter.

claims.statement: Tales usually include verse lines naming daphne (tibast) and valerian (vändelrot), two plants usable as talismans against her; she can reportedly be killed by a silver bullet or a gun she loaded herself.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisah biasanya disisipkan larik yang menyebut daphne (tibast) dan valerian (vändelrot), dua tanaman yang dapat dipakai sebagai jimat pelindung terhadapnya; konon ia dapat dibunuh dengan peluru perak atau senapan yang diisinya sendiri.
claims.quote: there is usually inserted lines of verse naming the daphne (Swedish: tibast ) and valerian (vändelrot ). These two plants can be used as talisman to protect against her. ... It is said she can be killed by a silver bullet or with a gun loaded by herself.

claims.statement: The skogsrå is a supernatural female forest creature of Swedish folklore, very like the Norwegian huldre, also called skogsfrun, skogssnuvan, skogsnymfen or råndan.
claims.statement_id: Skogsrå adalah makhluk perempuan gaib penghuni hutan dalam cerita rakyat Swedia, sangat mirip huldre Norwegia, dan juga disebut skogsfrun, skogssnuvan, skogsnymfen, atau råndan.
claims.quote: Une skogsrå ( ; skogsrået dans la forme définie en suédois) est une créature féminine surnaturelle de la forêt dans le folklore suédois, très similaire à l'huldre norvégienne. ... La créature est aussi désignée par skogsfrun, skogssnuvan, skogsnymfen ou råndan.

claims.statement: Vardøger, also known as vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor in Scandinavian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Vardøger, juga dikenal sebagai vardyvle atau vardyger, adalah roh pendahulu dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
claims.quote: Vardøger, also known as vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor in Scandinavian folklore.

claims.statement: Its stories are like déjà vu in reverse: a spirit with a person's footsteps, voice, scent or looks precedes them; subtly different from the doppelgänger and less sinister, it is likened to a phantom double or bilocation, and in Finnish folklore is called etiäinen.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya mirip déjà vu terbalik: roh dengan langkah, suara, bau, atau rupa seseorang mendahuluinya di suatu tempat; berbeda tipis dari doppelgänger dan kurang seram, ia disamakan dengan kembaran gaib atau bilokasi, dan dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia disebut etiäinen.
claims.quote: nearly déjà vu in substance, but in reverse, where a spirit with the subject's footsteps, voice, scent, or appearance and overall demeanor precedes them in a location or activity ... This bears a subtle difference from a doppelgänger, with a less sinister connotation. It has been likened to being a phantom double, or form of bilocation. In Finnish folklore, the concept is known as etiäinen.

claims.statement: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word meaning 'premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives', from Old Norse varðhygi, of vǫrð ('guard') and hugr ('mind, will, spirit'); in Sweden the same concept is called vård.
claims.statement_id: Vardøgr adalah kata Norwegia yang berarti "bunyi atau penampakan pertanda seseorang sebelum ia tiba"; asalnya bahasa Nordik Kuno varðhygi, dari vǫrð ("penjaga") dan hugr ("pikiran, kehendak, roh"); di Swedia gagasan yang sama disebut vård.
claims.quote: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word defined as ‘‘premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives’’. ... The word vardøger is from Old Norse varðhygi, consisting of the elements vǫrð, "care taker, guard, watchman" (akin to "warden") and hugr, 'the mind, will, thought, spirit'. The same concept exists in Sweden but under the name of vård

claims.statement: According to Norwegian folklore, seeing a vardøger means you are crossing someone's path, and often only that the person is on the way.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Norwegia, melihat vardøger berarti kau berpapasan di jalan seseorang, dan sering hanya berarti orang itu sedang dalam perjalanan.
claims.quote: Si ves un vardøger, según el folclore noruego, eso significa que te estas cruzando en el camino de una persona. A menudo solo quiere decir que esa persona de la cual has visto su vardøger está en camino.

claims.statement: Originally a vardøger was considered a fylgja, a kind of guardian spirit of that person.
claims.statement_id: Semula, vardøger dianggap sebuah fylgja, sejenis roh pelindung orang itu.
claims.quote: originalmente, un vardøger era considerado un fylgja, una especie de espíritu guardián de esa persona.

claims.statement: Since the vardøger is a kind of guardian spirit, people who have one are usually called good people protected by a kindly spirit; in short, the vardøger is the counterpart of a doppelgänger.
claims.statement_id: Karena vardøger sejenis roh pelindung, orang yang memilikinya biasa disebut orang baik yang dilindungi roh baik; singkatnya vardøger adalah lawan doppelgänger.
claims.quote: Debido a que el vardøger es un tipo de espíritu guardián, se suele decir de aquellos que tienen un vardøger que son buenas personas, ya que un espíritu benéfico les protege. En resumen, podríamos decir que un vardøger es la contraparte de un doppelgänger.

claims.statement: In Old Swedish the word is varþer, in modern Swedish vård; belief in these guardian spirits stayed strong in Scandinavian folklore until recent centuries, and English wraith derives from vǫrðr.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Swedia Kuno padanannya varþer, dalam bahasa Swedia modern vård; kepercayaan pada roh penjaga ini tetap kuat dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia sampai beberapa abad terakhir, dan kata Inggris wraith diturunkan dari vǫrðr.
claims.quote: In Old Swedish, the corresponding word is varþer ; in modern Swedish vård . The belief in this type of guardian spirits remained strong in Scandinavian folklore up until the last centuries ... The English word '"wraith" is derived from vǫrðr

claims.statement: The warden might appear as a small light or in its person's shape; sensing another's warden could cause an itching hand or nose as a foreboding; it could arrive before the person, and a dead person's warden could become a revenant haunting places or people.
claims.statement_id: Kadang penjaga menampakkan diri sebagai cahaya kecil atau sosok orangnya; merasakan penjaga orang lain bisa menimbulkan gatal di tangan atau hidung sebagai pertanda; penjaga bisa tiba sebelum orangnya, dan penjaga orang mati bisa menjadi hantu yang menghuni tempat atau orang tertentu.
claims.quote: At times, the warden could reveal itself as a small light or as the shape of the person ... The perception of another person's warden could cause a physical sensation such as an itching hand or nose, as a foreboding or an apparition. The warden could arrive before the actual person ... The warden of a dead person could also become a revenant, haunting particular spots or individuals.

claims.statement: A very old tree (often linden, ash or elm) on the farm could be called a 'warden tree' (Danish værnetræ, Swedish vårdträd, Norwegian tuntre), believed to guard against bad luck; breaking its leaves or twigs was a serious offence.
claims.statement_id: Pohon sangat tua (sering linden, ash, atau elm) di pekarangan dapat dijuluki "pohon penjaga" (Denmark: værnetræ; Swedia: vårdträd; Norwegia: tuntre) dan diyakini melindungi dari nasib buruk; mematahkan daun atau rantingnya dianggap pelanggaran berat.
claims.quote: A very old tree (often a linden, ash or elm) growing on the farm lot could be dubbed a "warden tree" (Danish: værnetræ ),(Swedish: vårdträd ), or (Norwegian: tuntre ) and was believed to defend it from bad luck. Breaking a leaf or twig from the warden tree was considered a serious offence.

claims.statement: A vörðr (Old Norse 'caretaker' or 'guardian') is a guardian spirit of Norse mythology believed to follow each person's soul (hugr) from birth to death.
claims.statement_id: Vörðr (Nordik Kuno, "pemelihara" atau "penjaga"; juga ditulis vǫrðr) adalah roh penjaga dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini mengikuti jiwa (hugr) setiap orang sejak lahir sampai mati.
claims.quote: Un vörðr (del nórdico antiguo: cuidador o guardián) es un espíritu guardián en la mitología nórdica, que se supone sigue desde el nacimiento hasta la muerte el alma (hugr) de cada persona.

claims.statement: In this case the revenant warden was always distinct from more conscious undead such as the draugar.
claims.statement_id: Dalam hal ini, penjaga yang menjadi hantu selalu berbeda dari mayat hidup yang lebih sadar seperti draugar.
claims.quote: In this case, the revenant warden was always distinct from more conscious undeads, such as the draugar .

claims.statement: Under Christian influence belief in wardens changed among adherents: some see the spirit as akin to a good and a bad conscience, others as guardian angels.
claims.statement_id: Di bawah pengaruh Kristen, kepercayaan pada penjaga berubah bagi para penganutnya: sebagian memandangnya seperti konsep hati nurani baik dan buruk, sebagian lagi sebagai malaikat pelindung.
claims.quote: Under the influence of Christianity, the belief in wardens changed in those adherent to the religion. Some view the spirit as being more akin to the Christian concept of a good and a bad conscience, while others view them as guardian angels.

claims.statement: In German, Wiedergänger is a term for revenants and various ghost phenomena from different cultures, meaning 're-walker' or 'one who walks again', cognate with Scandinavian gjenganger; they usually cause problems and frighten the living.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Jerman, Wiedergänger adalah istilah untuk mayat hidup dan berbagai fenomena hantu dari beragam budaya, berarti "yang berjalan lagi", sekerabat dengan kata Skandinavia gjenganger; mereka biasanya menimbulkan masalah dan menakuti orang hidup.
claims.quote: is a term for a revenant and different ghost phenomena from different cultural areas, meaning "re-walker", or by extension, "one who walks again"; cognate to Scandinavian gjenganger ("again-walker"). ... They usually cause problems and frighten living people.

claims.statement: Wiedergänger, also spelled Widergänger, denotes various ghostly apparitions from many cultures; its core is the idea of the dead returning to the living, often in bodily form (undead), uncanny and usually ill-disposed.
claims.statement_id: Wiedergänger, juga ditulis Widergänger, adalah sebutan untuk berbagai penampakan hantu dari beragam budaya; inti mitosnya adalah orang mati yang kembali ke dunia orang hidup, sering dalam wujud jasmani (Untote), dan mereka menyeramkan serta biasanya berniat jahat.
claims.quote: Als Wiedergänger, auch in der Schreibweise Widergänger belegt, werden verschiedene Gespenstererscheinungen aus diversen Kulturräumen bezeichnet. ... Der Kern des Wiedergänger-Mythologems ist die Vorstellung von Verstorbenen, die – oft als körperliche Erscheinung („Untote“) – in die Welt der Lebenden zurückkehren. Sie sind den Lebenden unheimlich und meist böse gesinnt

claims.statement: In various parts of Germany until the early 20th century people believed the dead lived on and exerted baleful influence from the grave, partly telepathically, so the fiend called Nachzehrer need not leave the grave.
claims.statement_id: Di berbagai wilayah Jerman sampai awal abad ke-20 orang percaya orang mati tetap hidup dan memberi pengaruh buruk dari kubur, sebagian lewat pengaruh telepatis, sehingga makhluk jahat yang disebut Nachzehrer tak perlu bangkit dari kubur.
claims.quote: In verschiedenen Teilen Deutschlands war bis ins frühe 20. Jahrhundert der Glaube verbreitet, dass Tote nach ihrem Tod trotzdem weiterlebten und einen unheilvollen Einfluss aus dem Grab heraus ausübten. Teilweise geschah dies durch eine telepathische Wirkung (Sympathiezauber), so dass der als Nachzehrer bezeichnete Unhold nicht aus dem Grab steigen musste

claims.statement: In folk belief other undead rose from graves and jumped onto night walkers' backs; this Aufhocker, which could take various shapes such as a werewolf in the Rhineland, had to be carried and grew heavier until the victim collapsed exhausted or dead.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, mayat hidup lain keluar dari kubur dan melompat ke punggung pengembara malam; Aufhocker ini, yang bisa berubah rupa, misalnya menjadi manusia serigala di Rheinland, harus digendong dan makin berat sampai korban ambruk kelelahan atau mati.
claims.quote: Andere Untote stiegen dem Volksglauben nach aus den Gräbern und sprangen nächtlichen Wanderern auf den Rücken. Diesen Aufhocker, der auch verschiedene Gestalten annehmen konnte, zum Beispiel im Rheinland die des Werwolfs, musste der Mensch tragen ... Dabei wurde der Aufhocker (auch „Huckop“ oder „Huckupp“ genannt) immer schwerer, und das Opfer brach schließlich erschöpft oder gar tot zusammen.

claims.statement: The French medievalist Jean-Claude Schmitt, studying Central European images of the 12th–16th centuries, divides the undead by depiction into revenant, Lazarus, soul and ghost types; the revenant resembles a living person.
claims.statement_id: Mediavis Prancis Jean-Claude Schmitt, peneliti sumber gambar Eropa Tengah abad ke-12 sampai ke-16, membagi mayat hidup menurut cara penggambarannya menjadi tipe Wiedergänger (revenant), Lazarus, jiwa, dan hantu; tipe Wiedergänger menyerupai orang hidup.
claims.quote: Der französische Mediävist Jean-Claude Schmitt, der mitteleuropäische Bildquellen aus dem 12. bis 16. Jahrhundert untersucht hat, unterteilt Untote je nach Darstellungsweise in Wiedergänger (Revenant), Lazarus-, Seelen- und Gespensttypen. ... gleicht der Wiedergänger einem Lebenden.

claims.statement: Especially in Catholic areas, belief in the back-riding Wiedergänger merged with belief in souls.
claims.statement_id: Terutama di wilayah Katolik, kepercayaan pada Wiedergänger penunggang punggung bercampur dengan kepercayaan pada jiwa.
claims.quote: Gerade in den katholisch geprägten Gebieten verschmolz der Glaube an den aufhockenden Wiedergänger mit dem Seelenglauben

claims.statement: The Askafroa (Swedish 'wife of the ash tree'), Danish Askefrue, is a legendary creature of Scandinavian folklore like the Greek hamadryads, guardian of the ash tree; thought malicious and destructive, she had to be appeased with a sacrifice on Ash Wednesday.
claims.statement_id: Askafroa (bahasa Swedia, "istri pohon ash"), dalam bahasa Denmark Askefrue, adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang mirip hamadryad Yunani, penjaga pohon ash; ia dianggap makhluk jahat yang banyak merusak, sehingga perlu diberi persembahan pada Rabu Abu.
claims.quote: The Askafroa (Swedish: wife of the ash tree ), also known as the Danish Askefrue is a type of legendary creature in Scandinavian folklore, similar to the Greek Hamadryads. The Askafroa is the guardian (tutelary deity) of the ash tree. The Askafroa was thought to be a malicious creature that did much damage, and to appease her, it was necessary to make a sacrifice to her on Ash Wednesday.

claims.statement: The Askafroa lives in ash trees in Skåne, Sweden, and is said to be very dangerous; she is the tree's soul and will take revenge if it is cut down.
claims.statement_id: Askafroa tinggal di pohon ash di wilayah Skåne, Swedia, dan disebut sangat berbahaya; ia jiwa pohon itu dan akan membalas dendam bila pohonnya ditebang.
claims.quote: The Askafroa lives in ash trees in the Scania region of Sweden, and is said to be a very dangerous creature. She is the soul of the tree and if it is cut down, she will exert revenge.

claims.statement: The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in his ethnographic work Wärend och Wirdarne a belief in Ljunit Hundred in a female being in the ash tree; the elders sacrificed to her on Ash Wednesday morning, pouring water over the roots before sunrise.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Swedia Hyltén-Cavallius mencatat dalam karya etnografinya Wärend och Wirdarne kepercayaan di Ljunit Hundred tentang makhluk perempuan di pohon ash; para tetua berkorban kepadanya pada pagi Rabu Abu dengan menuang air ke akar pohon sebelum matahari terbit.
claims.quote: The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in his ethnographic work Wärend och Wirdarne a belief of a female creature living in the ash tree, in Ljunit Hundred. The elders sacrificed to the Askafroa on the morning of Ash Wednesday. Before the sun had risen, they poured water over the roots of the ash tree.

claims.statement: The ash holds a very prominent place in Norse mythology; with the oak it was the most magical tree, credited with powers such as stopping bleeding or countering snake venom, and the mythological Yggdrasil was an ash.
claims.statement_id: Pohon ash amat menonjol dalam mitologi Nordik; bersama pohon ek, ia pohon paling sakti yang diberi kekuatan khusus seperti menghentikan aliran darah atau menangkal bisa ular, dan pohon mitologis Yggdrasil pun pohon ash.
claims.quote: The ash tree has a very prominent place in Nordic mythology. It was, together with the oak tree, the most magical tree to which special powers were assigned, such as the ability to stop blood flow or as an antidote to snake poison. The mythological tree Yggdrasil was also an ash tree.

claims.statement: The Askafroa (Swedish 'wife of the ash'), Danish Askefrue, German Eschenfrau, remains rather obscure and so is little represented in modern fiction, but appears in the online role-playing game Dark Age of Camelot.
claims.statement_id: Askafroa (Swedia, "istri pohon ash"), dalam bahasa Denmark Askefrue dan Jerman Eschenfrau, tetap makhluk yang cukup samar sehingga jarang tampil dalam fiksi modern, tetapi muncul dalam gim peran daring Dark Age of Camelot.
claims.quote: L’Askafroa (qui signifie en suédois « femme du frêne »), Askefrue en danois ou Eschenfrau en allemand ... L'Askafroa reste une créature assez obscure. Par conséquent, elle n'est pas très représentée dans la fiction moderne. Elle apparaît dans le jeu de rôle en ligne Dark Age of Camelot

claims.statement: While doing so they said 'Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada', meaning 'Now I sacrifice [to you], so that you do us no harm'; they also believed anyone breaking branches or twigs from the ash would fall ill.
claims.statement_id: Sambil melakukannya mereka berkata "Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada", artinya "Kini aku berkorban [kepadamu], agar kau tidak mencelakai kami"; mereka juga percaya siapa pun yang mematahkan dahan atau ranting pohon ash akan jatuh sakit.
claims.quote: While doing this, they said: "Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada", meaning "Now I sacrifice [to you], so that you do us no harm". Hyltén-Cavallius further writes that they believed that if anyone broke branches or twigs from the ash tree, they would become ill.

claims.statement: Bäckahästen (Swedish bäck 'brook' and hästen 'the horse') is in Scanian folk belief a brook spirit or the Näck in horse form, comparable with Celtic water horses such as the Scottish each uisge, the kelpie and the Welsh ceffyl dŵr.
claims.statement_id: Bäckahästen (Swedia: bäck, "sungai kecil", dan hästen, "kuda") dalam kepercayaan rakyat Skåne adalah roh sungai atau Näck dalam wujud kuda, yang dapat dibandingkan dengan kuda air mitologi Kelt seperti each uisge Skotlandia, kelpie, dan ceffyl dŵr Wales.
claims.quote: Bäckahästen (schwedisch, von bäck „Bach“ und hästen „das Pferd“) ist im schonischen Volksglauben der Geist eines Baches oder der Näck in Pferdegestalt. Es kann mit den Wasserpferden aus der keltischen Mythologie wie dem schottischen Each Uisge, dem schottisch-irischen Kelpie oder dem walisischen Ceffyl dŵr verglichen werden.

claims.statement: The bäckahäst is a treacherous predator lurking by brooks, rivers and lakes, dragging riders and other horses into the water to drown them; it appears as a fine stallion, usually shimmering white, sometimes dapple-grey, black or blue, its mouth full of sharp fangs.
claims.statement_id: Bäckahäst adalah pemangsa licik yang mengintai di sungai dan danau untuk menyeret penunggang dan kuda lain ke air dan menenggelamkannya; ia tampak sebagai kuda jantan gagah yang biasanya putih berkilau, kadang kelabu belang, hitam, atau kebiruan, dengan mulut penuh taring tajam.
claims.quote: Das Bäckahäst ist ein hinterhältiges Raubtier, das an Bächen, Flüssen und Seen lauert, wo es Reiter und andere Pferde ins Wasser zieht, um sie zu ertränken. Es zeigt sich als stattlicher Hengst, meist weiß schimmernd, aber sein Fell kann auch apfelgrau, schwarz oder blau changieren. Sein Maul ist voller scharfer Fangzähne.

claims.statement: The number of children does not matter, as the horse's back grows longer the more climb on; to stop it drowning children, throw a piece of steel between horse and water, or a child may cry out the Christian word 'cross'.
claims.statement_id: Jumlah anak tak jadi soal karena punggung kuda makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang naik; untuk mencegahnya menenggelamkan anak, orang melempar sepotong baja di antara kuda dan air, atau seorang anak menyerukan kata Kristen "salib".
claims.quote: Die Anzahl der Kinder spielt dabei keine Rolle, da der Pferderücken immer länger wird, je mehr Kinder sich auf das Untier setzen. Wenn man ein Bäckahäst daran hindern will, Kinder zu ertränken, soll man ein Stück Stahl zwischen das Pferd und das Wasser werfen. ... Eine andere Möglichkeit, dem Untier zu entkommen, besteht darin, dass ein Kind das christliche Wort „Kreuz“ ausruft

claims.statement: The bäckahäst, bäckahästen or bækhesten ('brook horse') is a fantastic horse of Scandinavian folklore very close to the kelpie: a majestic white horse appearing near rivers, especially in fog, and whoever mounts it cannot get off.
claims.statement_id: Bäckahäst, bäckahästen, atau bækhesten (harfiah "kuda sungai kecil") adalah kuda khayalan cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang sangat mirip kelpie: kuda putih megah yang muncul dekat sungai, terutama saat berkabut, dan siapa yang naik ke punggungnya tak bisa turun.
claims.quote: Le bäckahäst, bäckahästen ou bækhesten (littéralement « cheval des ruisseaux ») est un cheval fantastique issu du folklore scandinave, très proche du kelpie. Il s'agit d'un majestueux cheval blanc qui apparait près des rivières, en particulier par temps de brouillard. Celui qui monte sur son dos se trouve incapable d'en descendre.

claims.statement: Bækhesten or Bäckahästen is a mythical animal of Nordic folklore and Scanian belief, the nøkk in horse form, and the Scandinavian version of the Celtic kelpie.
claims.statement_id: Bækhesten atau Bäckahästen adalah hewan mitos dalam cerita rakyat Nordik dan kepercayaan Skåne, padanan nøkken dalam wujud kuda, dan versi Skandinavia dari kelpie Kelt.
claims.quote: Bækhesten eller Bäckahästen (fra svensk: bäckhästen) er et mytologisk dyr i nordisk folklore og skånsk folketro, svarende til nøkken, blot i hesteform. Hesten er den skandinaviske udgave af den keltiske Kelpie

claims.statement: In Swedish belief the bäckahäst let a farmer harness it to the plough; the stallion was tamed through the working day by the steel in its harness.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Swedia, bäckahäst pernah membiarkan seorang petani memasangnya pada bajak; kuda jantan itu jinak sepanjang hari kerja karena baja pada tali kekangnya.
claims.quote: Im schwedischen Volksglauben wird weiter berichtet, dass das Bäckahäst einem Bauern erlaubte, es vor den Pflug zu spannen ... Der Hengst war durch den Stahl im Pferdegeschirr während der Tagesarbeit gebändigt worden.

claims.statement: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English wyrm, Old Norse ormr, Old High German wurm), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons in Germanic mythology and folklore, often shown as large venomous snakes hoarding gold.
claims.statement_id: Worm, wurm, atau wyrm (Inggris Kuno wyrm, Nordik Kuno ormr, Jerman Hulu Kuno wurm), berarti "ular", adalah istilah kuno untuk naga dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Jermanik, yang sering digambarkan sebagai ular besar berbisa dan penimbun emas.
claims.quote: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English: wyrm ; Old Norse: ormr ; Old High German: wurm ), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons (Old English: draca ; Old Norse: dreki/*draki ; Old High German: trahho ) in the wider Germanic mythology and folklore, in which they are often portrayed as large venomous snakes and hoarders of gold.

claims.statement: Prominent worms in medieval Germanic works include the dragon that killed Beowulf, Fáfnir of the Völsung Cycle, Nidhogg and the world serpent Jǫrmungandr, with subcategories such as lindworms and sea serpents.
claims.statement_id: Cacing-naga terkenal dalam karya Jermanik abad pertengahan antara lain naga pembunuh Beowulf, Fáfnir dalam siklus Völsung, Nidhogg, dan ular dunia Jǫrmungandr, termasuk subkategori seperti lindworm dan ular laut.
claims.quote: Prominent worms attested in medieval Germanic works include the dragon that killed Beowulf, the central dragon in the Völsung Cycle – Fáfnir, Nidhogg (Old Norse: Níðhǫggr ), and the great world serpent, Jǫrmungandr, including subcategories such as lindworms and sea serpents.

claims.statement: The Germanic dragon (Germaanske draak) is a mythical beast of Germanic peoples' mythology and folklore that differs sharply from the usual dragon: instead of a scaly four-legged body, long tail and bat wings, it has the form of a gigantic snake (gigantyske slange) without legs (poaten) or wings (wjukken).
claims.statement_id: Naga Jermanik adalah hewan mitos dari mitologi dan cerita rakyat bangsa Jermanik yang cirinya sangat berbeda dari gambaran naga biasa: bukannya bertubuh bersisik berkaki empat, berekor panjang, dan bersayap kelelawar, ia berbentuk ular raksasa tanpa kaki atau sayap.
claims.quote: In Germaanske draak is in mytysk bist ôfkomstich út 'e mytology en folkloare fan 'e Germaanske folken, dat kwa skaaimerken sterk ôfwykt fan hoe't in draak ornaris foarsteld wurdt. Ynstee fan in mei skobben bepânsere lichem mei fjouwer poaten, in lange sturt en twa flearmûseftige wjukken op 'e rêch hat in Germaanske draak de foarm fan in gigantyske slange, sûnder poaten of wjukken.

claims.statement: The link between dragons and treasure hoards is widespread in Germanic literature; in the Völsung Cycle Fáfnir, having claimed a hoard including the ring Andvaranaut, becomes a dragon to guard and brood over it.
claims.statement_id: Kaitan naga dengan timbunan harta tersebar luas dalam sastra Jermanik; dalam siklus Völsung, Fáfnir yang menguasai timbunan harta, termasuk cincin Andvaranaut, berubah menjadi naga untuk menjaga dan mengeraminya.
claims.quote: The association between dragons and hoards of treasure is widespread in Germanic literature ... In the Völsung Cycle, Fáfnir , upon claiming a hoard of treasure, including the ring Andvaranaut, transforms into a dragon to protect and brood over it.

claims.statement: Fáfnir's brother Regin reforges the sword Gram for the hero Sigurd, who kills the dragon with it; in Beowulf the dragon wakes in its burial mound when a cup is stolen from its hoard and seeks vengeance on the Geats.
claims.statement_id: Regin, saudara Fáfnir, menempa ulang pedang Gram dan memberikannya kepada pahlawan Sigurd yang memakainya untuk membunuh naga itu; dalam Beowulf, naga terbangun dari gundukan kuburnya ketika sebuah piala dari hartanya dicuri dan menuntut balas kepada orang Geat.
claims.quote: Fáfnir's brother, Regin, reforges the sword Gram from broken shards, and gives it to the hero Sigurd, who uses it to kill the dragon ... In Beowulf, the dragon slain by the poem's eponymous hero, is awoken from the burial mound in which it dwells when a cup from its hoard is stolen, leading it to seek vengeance from the Geats.

claims.statement: Especially in later tales, however, they share many features with other European dragons, such as wings.
claims.statement_id: Namun terutama dalam kisah-kisah belakangan, mereka berbagi banyak ciri dengan naga lain dalam mitologi Eropa, misalnya bersayap.
claims.quote: Especially in later tales, however, they share many common features with other dragons in European mythology, such as having wings.
